## Severity rubric

| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| S0 | Funds are lost or stranded on a live path with no unusual condition. |
| S1 | Capital can be lost, stranded, overspent or exposed under a plausible condition. |
| S2 | Correctness/robustness defect with bounded or indirect capital effect, or test/infra drift that can hide an S0/S1. |
| S3 | Misleading behavior, telemetry or ops friction. |
| S4 | Hygiene. |

## Capital-impact classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| LOSS | Funds can be lost. |
| STRAND | A position is held without a working exit or protection. |
| OVERSPEND | More is spent than configured or capped. |
| EXPOSURE | A risk limit or trust boundary is bypassed. |
| none | No capital effect. |

## Lifecycle

candidate -> confirmed -> decided -> fixed -> verified, or NOT-A-BUG (never for a research candidate in Phase 22).

Escalation tiers (D-16): **immediate** for any S0, any finding tagged `rail` or `test-origin-db-row`, and any secret with `secret_class` non-public; **area-batch** for S1, presented when the area finishes; **pre-phase** for the items surfaced during plan-phase (D-23). Known-public secrets and scan records never escalate. Nothing is fixed in Phase 22 (NAC-13).

- **Summary:** Phase 23 stop-the-line record for a possible severity increase on a registered capital finding (23-SPEC line 103). While registering AUD-ANTIRUG-024 the 23-01 executor re-read the related HTTP poller finding AUD-ANTIRUG-018 (S2, STRAND, confirmed) and found its rationale ("only chains running without a WebSocket URL, after an outage larger than the provider range limit ... Protection then stays off until restart") wrong on two points, confirmed by the execute-phase orchestrator re-reading the code at HEAD. (1) A restart does not clear it: the HTTP poller re-reads its start block from chain_state on restart (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1228-1232 at the audit base, :1231-1235 at HEAD); the row advances only after a successful poll (:1300-1306 base, :1303-1309 HEAD) or a tick with no registered positions (:1269-1276 base, :1272-1279 HEAD); held positions are re-registered before the poller starts (src/bot.ts:2120-2144 base, :2122-2146 HEAD). (2) Ordinary downtime triggers it: getLogs requests lastBlock+1..currentBlock in one call (:1279-1291 base, :1282-1294 HEAD) and the repo's own range assumption is 10 blocks on ETH ("Alchemy free-tier safe", src/chainRegistry.ts:223-230) and 500 elsewhere, so about two minutes of downtime on ETH is enough. It is silent: the dashboard shows the chain connected (AUD-ANTIRUG-007) and only antirug.http-polling.error log lines appear. Not reproduced; whether the operator's provider refuses these ranges is unmeasured. The operator was asked what grade it should have and whether any chain runs without a WebSocket URL.

### ESC-BUY-01

- **Date / tier:** 2026-11-06 / immediate (tags: capital, d-stop-the-line)
- **Items:** AUD-BUY-001
- **Resolved items:** none
- **Summary:** S0 finding from the BUY slice audit (22-17 Task 1), presented at once because it is S0 (D-16 immediate tier). After scripts/deliberate-buy.ts lands a buy, the exit monitor and anti-rug protection are armed inside the script's own process (src/bot.ts recordAndArmDeliberateBuy -> armPositionMonitoring -> startExitMonitor / registerAntiRugPosition), and the script then calls process.exit(0) (scripts/deliberate-buy.ts:150), which kills them. The main bot reloads open positions only when it boots (src/bot.ts:1797, :1805), so the bought position has no exit and no rug protection until the main bot is next started, and nothing tells the operator to start it. The bot is OFF for all of v7.0, so there is no live exposure now. Proposed fix directions are on card BUY-01 (hand the position to the running bot; refuse while the bot runs and tell the operator loudly to start it; or keep the script alive until the position closes). Nothing is changed in Phase 22.
- **Presented at:** 2026-11-06 session: the 22-17 Task 1 immediate-tier (S0) blocking checkpoint returned right after commit 93c001e, relayed to the operator by the execute-phase orchestrator
- **Operator response:** Acknowledge continue
- **Acknowledgement evidence:** not required (operator_response is the operator's own verbatim reply). Presented at presented_at through the 22-17 Task 1 blocking checkpoint (gate blocking-human).
- **Ruling:** acknowledge-continue: the finding is acknowledged, its severity stays S0 (the operator did not re-rate it), no decimal phase is inserted, and Phase 22 continues
- **Phase continued:** true

Already escalated, listed at the checkpoint and not asked again: the two RC-10 stuck-nonce-lock sub-findings AUD-TX-001 (re-entrancy deadlock) and AUD-TX-002 (an operation that never settles: wait() with timeout 0 inside the lock) stay on ESC-PRE-02 through its resolved_items. ## Findings

### Area: src

#### S0

##### AUD-BUY-001: A landed deliberate buy is armed for exit and anti-rug only inside the short-lived operator script, which exits at once; the position runs unprotected until the main bot next boots

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S0 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** C12 (timer leaks), C14 (idempotent exits)
- **Severity rationale:** S0 under the rubric: on the ordinary success path of an operator-run money path (every landed deliberate buy, no unusual condition), the position is held with no exit monitor and no anti-rug protection from the moment the script exits until the main bot is next started. If the main bot was already running, it does not pick the position up until it is restarted. The length of the unprotected window depends only on what the operator does next, and nothing in the code prompts a restart. The bot is OFF throughout Phase 22, so there is no live exposure now. Grading between S0 and S1 is a judgment (S1 if one treats 'the operator restarts the bot afterwards' as the expected procedure); it is escalated at the immediate tier so the operator can rule. Operator ruling (ESC-BUY-01, recorded 2026-11-07): acknowledge-continue; the severity stays S0, no decimal phase, Phase 22 continues; interim rule: after any landed deliberate buy, start (or restart) the main bot immediately.
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`, `scripts/deliberate-buy.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:565@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - private-landed branch of executeDeliberateBuy: await recordAndArmDeliberateBuy(...) then return the hash
  - code: `src/bot.ts:594@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - late-land (reconciled included) branch: same record-and-arm call, then return
  - code: `src/bot.ts:759-760@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - public-fallback branch: same record-and-arm call, then return txHash
  - code: `src/bot.ts:820-863@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - recordAndArmDeliberateBuy: writes the trades row, reads balanceOf, resolves the trade id and pair, then calls armPositionMonitoring in the CURRENT process
  - code: `src/bot.ts:413-452@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - armPositionMonitoring: await startExitMonitor (:422), then snapshotLpBaseline + registerAntiRugPosition (:432, :440). Both arm in-process timers and listeners.
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1906@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - startExitMonitor arms a setInterval poll loop in the calling process
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1945@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - registerExitMonitor stores the interval in the in-memory timerRegistry (src/utils/exitManager.ts:104), which dies with the process
  - code: `scripts/deliberate-buy.ts:142@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the operator script is the only caller of executeDeliberateBuy (D-DELIBERATE-EXPLICIT-ONLY)
  - code: `scripts/deliberate-buy.ts:150@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - on a landed buy the script calls process.exit(0) right after printing the result, which kills the just-armed exit poll timer and the anti-rug WebSocket subscription
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1797@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the main bot re-reads open trades from the DB only once, at boot (resumeMultiChainMonitoring); a running main bot never picks up a trade row another process wrote later
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1805@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - anti-rug resume also runs only once, at boot (resumeAntiRugMonitoring)
  - command: `git grep -n "getResumeExitMonitorTrades\|getResumeAntiRugTrades\|resumeMultiChainMonitoring\|resumeExitMonitor(" 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src scripts` - the only consumers of the resume queries are the two boot-time functions in src/bot.ts; src/exitEngine.ts:731 re-arms only a position the same process already monitors; no src/api route re-arms monitoring. Nothing re-scans the trades table while the bot runs.
- **Sibling sites checked:** All three landed branches of executeDeliberateBuy (src/bot.ts:565 private-landed, :594 late-land, :759 public fallback) route through recordAndArmDeliberateBuy and so share the defect. The snipe paths (handleNewPairForChain :1173, handleNewV3PoolForChain :1483-1492) run inside the long-lived main bot process and are not affected by this mechanism. Callers of executeDeliberateBuy at the base: only scripts/deliberate-buy.ts:142 (git grep). Re-arm paths in a running bot: none that read new trade rows (the resume queries are read only at boot, src/bot.ts:1797 and :1805; exitEngine.ts:731 re-arms a position already tracked in-process; src/api routes call none of startExitMonitor/resumeExitMonitor/registerAntiRugPosition). The script also signs from a second process on the same wallet while the main bot may run, so the in-process nonce lock is not shared (that hazard is RC-18 and the out-of-process-signer scope deferred to Phase 29 HYG-03; recorded here only as context, not as this finding). The script's closing text (scripts/deliberate-buy.ts:157-162 region) tells the operator nothing about restarting the main bot.
- **Escalation:** ESC-BUY-01
- **Decision card:** OD-26
- **Related:** AUD-TX-005, AUD-BUY-002, AUD-BUY-025, AUD-ANTIRUG-025
- **Tags:** capital, d-stop-the-line
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24 (capital fix, after a Phase 23 real-path proof): make the protection of a deliberately bought position not depend on the short-lived script process. Options to decide on the card: (a) the script hands the new position to the running main bot (for example the main bot re-scans pending buys without a monitor on a timer, or an explicit IPC/DB-flag handoff), (b) the script refuses to run unless the main bot is stopped and then tells the operator, loudly, to start the main bot at once (and the main bot's boot resume already covers the row), (c) the script stays alive and keeps monitoring until the position is closed. Until fixed, after any landed deliberate buy the operator must start or restart the main bot immediately. Nothing is changed in Phase 22 (NAC-13).
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-17 executor) / 2026-11-06 / 23a6461

#### S1

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-001: Three reconnect paths (anti-rug handleWsClose, one bot.ts loop per DEX, dashboard onRestart) each rewrite ctx.wsProvider, so the anti-rug rug-log subscription can vanish after a dashboard stop, be duplicated after a reconnect, or be left on a provider nothing destroys

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill), C12 (timer leaks)
- **Research candidates:** RC-13 (research suggested S1)
- **Severity rationale:** S1, as the research suggested. The vanish case (sub-claim 1) needs only an operator stop and start from the dashboard and leaves every open position on that chain without rug protection while the health badge keeps saying connected. The duplicate and orphan cases need a socket drop, which is routine. Not S0: each case needs an operator stop or a socket drop, and the routine exit monitor still runs.
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/bot.ts`, `src/api/routes/chains.ts`, `src/utils/provider.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:916-944@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - handleWsClose: removeWsProvider(chain), new WebSocketProvider (:921), ctx.wsProvider = new (:925), state.wsProvider = new (:926), activeDispatcher/activeFilter nulled (:941-942), then startChainAntiRugListener (:943)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:643-657@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - re-subscribe calls off(activeFilter, activeDispatcher) and on(filter) on whatever ctx.wsProvider is NOW; when the earlier subscription lives on another provider the off() is a no-op and the old dispatcher keeps running
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:678@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - state.wsProvider follows ctx.wsProvider, not the provider the previous dispatcher is attached to
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1552-1576@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 per-DEX reconnect: removeWsProvider, new WebSocketProvider (:1561), ctx.wsProvider = new (:1562), PoolCreated re-subscribed on it (:1564), close handler on its socket (:1568); one such loop per DEX close handler (:1576)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1593-1618@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 per-DEX reconnect, same shape (:1603-1606, close handler :1618)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1808-1852@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - onRestart: replaces ctx.wsProvider only when it is missing or destroyed (:1812-1817, through getWsProvider, which caches it), re-runs startDexListener for every dex (:1836-1845); it never calls startChainAntiRugListener
  - code: `src/api/routes/chains.ts:136-142@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - dashboard stop: stoppedChains.add, then ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners() ("Do NOT destroy the provider -- exit monitors may need it")
  - command: `node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js:1159-1176 (ethers@6.16.0)` - removeAllListeners() with no event stops and deletes every subscription on the provider, so it removes the anti-rug log filter installed at detector.ts:655 as well as the factory listeners
  - code: `src/utils/provider.ts:33-52@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - getWsProvider caches one provider per chain; removeWsProvider destroys only that cached entry. Providers built with new WebSocketProvider in the three loops are never cached, so nothing ever destroys them; and the provider cached by onRestart can be destroyed by an unrelated loop
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:782-807@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - heartbeat keeps broadcasting chain_ws_health_change connected every 30 s while the raw socket answers pings, whether or not a rug-log subscription exists
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:885@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - while (true) with no shutdown or stopped-chain check (same at bot.ts:1557 and :1598)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1013@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - backfillSinceLastSeen calls getBlockNumber outside any try; a rejection there propagates out of startChainAntiRugListener into the reconnect loop catch (:945) after the new subscription was already installed
  - command: `git grep -n "new WebSocketProvider\|new ethers.WebSocketProvider\|ctx.wsProvider = " 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src` - writers of ctx.wsProvider: detector.ts:925, bot.ts:1562, bot.ts:1604, bot.ts:1816; constructors: detector.ts:921, bot.ts:1561, bot.ts:1603, provider.ts:37
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every writer of ctx.wsProvider at the base (detector.ts:925, bot.ts:1562, :1604, :1816), every provider constructor (detector.ts:921, bot.ts:1561, :1603, provider.ts:37), every remover (chains.ts:141 removeAllListeners; bot.ts:2333-2336 shutdown removeAllListeners plus destroy) and every removeWsProvider caller (detector.ts:920, bot.ts:1555, :1596, :1814). Subscribers that live on ctx.wsProvider: the anti-rug log filter (detector.ts:655), the V3 and V2 factory listeners (bot.ts:1545, :1586 and the reconnect copies :1564, :1606) and the V3 Mint wait (bot.ts:163-172). The DEX-listener consequences (double buys, no PairCreated backfill, leaked providers, stop not stopping buys) are AUD-BUY-008 and AUD-BUY-011 and are not repeated here; this entry is the anti-rug consumer of the same shared handle. The process exit on a failed reconnect attempt is AUD-ANTIRUG-002. Card OD-11 (single WebSocket owner) is owned by the API slice (22-22).
- **Escalation:** ESC-ANTIRUG-01
- **Decision card:** OD-11
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-008, AUD-BUY-011, AUD-ANTIRUG-002, AUD-ANTIRUG-003, AUD-ANTIRUG-008
- **Tags:** capital
- **Traces:**
  - WS reconnect while the dashboard stops and starts the chain (does the rug-log subscription survive, get duplicated, or vanish?): Boot: ctx.wsProvider = P0 from getWsProvider (cached in provider.ts). Factory listeners on P0 (bot.ts:1545, :1586); anti-rug log filter on P0 (detector.ts:655). Close handlers on the P0 socket: one per DEX (bot.ts:1576, :1618), one per startChainAntiRugListener call (detector.ts:710) and one from setupHeartbeat (detector.ts:809)., Operator clicks Stop: chains.ts:141 ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners() stops and deletes every ethers subscription on P0 (abstract-provider.js:1167-1173), the anti-rug filter included. The raw socket stays open, so the heartbeat (detector.ts:782-807) keeps pinging and broadcasting connected. chainState.activeDispatcher/activeFilter still name the removed subscription., Case A, no socket drop while stopped. Operator clicks Start: chains.ts:176 onRestart. P0 is not destroyed, so bot.ts:1812 skips the rebuild; startDexListener runs for each dex (bot.ts:1836-1845) and adds factory listeners plus one more close handler per DEX on P0. Nothing calls startChainAntiRugListener., Case A result: the rug-log subscription is GONE. It comes back only when a new position on that chain registers (detector.ts:447 -> :643-657, which re-installs the filter for every registered address) or the socket next closes (detector.ts:943). Until then a rug on any open position of that chain triggers nothing, and the dashboard shows connected., Case B, the socket drops while stopped: every close handler on P0 runs. handleWsClose (detector.ts:852-862, connected -> reconnecting) waits 1 s, removeWsProvider destroys the cached P0, builds P1, sets ctx.wsProvider = P1, nulls activeDispatcher/activeFilter and calls startChainAntiRugListener, which installs the filter on P1 (stoppedChains is never consulted). Each DEX loop (bot.ts:1557-1574, :1598-1615) builds its own P2..Pk, re-subscribes its factory listener there (buying resumes while the dashboard says stopped) and writes ctx.wsProvider; the last writer wins., Case B, then Start: onRestart sees a live ctx.wsProvider (say P2, a DEX loop provider) and adds every factory listener again on P2, so the DEX whose own listener is on P2 now has two and the others gain a copy on P2 (AUD-BUY-008 doubling). The anti-rug filter stays on P1., Case B, next buy on the chain: registerAntiRugPosition -> startChainAntiRugListener calls P2.off(old filter, old dispatcher) (no-op, the dispatcher is on P1) and P2.on(new filter) (detector.ts:643-657). Two live rug-log subscriptions now exist (P1 with the old address set, P2 with all addresses); every rug log of the older positions is dispatched twice, which doubles evaluations, confirm gates and circuit-breaker counts (AUD-ANTIRUG-003). The sell lock keeps the sells serialized., Afterwards P1 is never destroyed (provider.ts:46-52 only destroys the cached entry), and the heartbeat now pings P2 only (setupHeartbeat replaced the interval), so a half-open P1 socket goes unnoticed: P1 is an orphan. -> All three outcomes occur depending on order. VANISH: stop, then start with no drop in between, leaves the chain without rug-log monitoring until the next buy or socket close, while the dashboard shows connected. DUPLICATE: a drop during the stop, then a new registration, yields two live subscriptions and double dispatch of every rug log. ORPHAN: the replaced anti-rug provider is never destroyed. The subscription never survives cleanly through the stop: it is either removed (Case A) or rebuilt by the reconnect loop against the stop (Case B).
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] (1) Dashboard Stop removes the anti-rug rug-log subscription together with the factory listeners, and Start (onRestart) does not re-subscribe it. Monitoring returns only on the next registerAntiRugPosition on that chain (a new buy, detector.ts:447) or the next socket close (detector.ts:943). Meanwhile the heartbeat reports connected. (evidence: src/api/routes/chains.ts:139-142@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1808-1852@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:782-807@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, ethers@6.16.0 abstract-provider.js:1159-1176)
  - [confirmed] (2) After one socket close each loop builds its own provider. The anti-rug subscription sits on the anti-rug loop provider while ctx.wsProvider ends on whichever loop wrote last. The next startChainAntiRugListener call (any new registration) runs off() against the wrong provider and adds a second subscription, so each rug log of the earlier positions is dispatched twice. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:643-657@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:925@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1562@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1604@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (3) Replaced providers are never destroyed: removeWsProvider destroys only the cached entry and none of the loop-built providers is cached. Their sockets and any subscription still attached stay alive (orphan). (evidence: src/utils/provider.ts:46-52@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:921@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (4) The anti-rug loop removeWsProvider(chain) destroys whatever provider is cached under the chain name. After an onRestart that rebuilt the provider through getWsProvider (cached), a close of the separate anti-rug socket destroys that live provider and every DEX listener on it. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:920@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1814-1816@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (5) No loop checks shutdown or the dashboard stopped state, so a reconnect during a stop re-subscribes the factory listeners (buying resumes, AUD-BUY-011) and the anti-rug filter. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:885@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1557@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1598@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (6) A backfill RPC error right after a successful re-subscribe (detector.ts:1013 is outside any try) is caught by the reconnect loop as a failed attempt. The next pass builds another provider and subscribes again without removing the first subscription (activeDispatcher was nulled at :941), which is one more duplicate and orphan. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:941-956@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1013@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** One owner for each chain WebSocket (card OD-11): a single reconnect loop that rebuilds the provider, re-attaches every consumer (factory listeners and the anti-rug filter) on that same provider, destroys the old provider, honours shutdown and the stopped state, and makes dashboard Stop remove only the factory listeners and never the anti-rug filter (what Stop should do to anti-rug is card ANTIRUG-05). Phase 24, after a Phase 23 real-path test of stop/start and a socket drop with an open position (no mocked provider).
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-002: A WebSocket reconnect attempt that cannot connect kills the bot: no socket has an error listener, so the ws library throws its error event as an uncaught exception and the process exits

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill), C11 (unhandled rejections)
- **Severity rationale:** S1. Effect: the process exits, so every open position on every chain loses its exit monitor and anti-rug protection until the operator restarts the bot (there is no supervisor). Condition: the endpoint is unreachable or refuses the upgrade (outage, 429, 5xx, DNS) at the moment of a reconnect attempt, 1 s after any socket drop; plausible, because drops often come from the same provider trouble. Not S0: a drop followed by a successful reconnect does not crash.
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/bot.ts`, `src/utils/provider.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:916-944@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the try around new WebSocketProvider only catches synchronous throws; the doc comment at :834 says the constructor "raises if RPC unreachable; loops", which is not what the library does
  - command: `node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider-websocket.js:25-51 (ethers@6.16.0)` - the constructor calls new WebSocket(url) and sets only onopen and onmessage; no onerror, so a failed connect is not caught by the constructor and no error listener exists
  - command: `node_modules/ethers/node_modules/ws/lib/websocket.js:876-881, :911-915, :1033-1037 (ws@8.17.1)` - a refused connect or an unexpected upgrade response (for example HTTP 429) calls emitErrorAndClose / abortHandshake, which does websocket.emit('error', err); receiverOnError (:1176-1192) does the same for a bad frame on a live socket
  - command: `git grep -n -e uncaughtException -e onerror -e "on('error'" -e "on(\"error\"" 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src` - no output: no error listener on any socket and no uncaughtException handler anywhere in src
  - command: `node -e "const {WebSocketProvider}=require('ethers');const p=new WebSocketProvider('ws://127.0.0.1:1',1);p.websocket.on('close',...)" (Node 22.16.0, loopback only, no src import)` - printed "constructed without throw", then "Unhandled 'error' event ... connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:1 ... at emitErrorAndClose (ws/lib/websocket.js:1035)", exit=1; the same script with an error listener printed "error handled: ECONNREFUSED", "close handler ran", "still alive after 3s", exit=0
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:945-980@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the RECONNECT_FAILURE_ALERT tier and the backoff growth live in the catch; the >60 s tier (:889-914) needs a later loop pass; a refused connect ends the process before either is reached
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1561@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 DEX reconnect builds a provider the same way (no error listener)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1603@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 DEX reconnect, same
  - code: `src/utils/provider.ts:37@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - getWsProvider at boot and in onRestart (bot.ts:1815), same
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every WebSocketProvider construction at the base: detector.ts:921, bot.ts:1561, bot.ts:1603, provider.ts:37 (git grep). None attaches an error listener. Once a connection is established, a socket-level error (ECONNRESET) is handled inside ws by socketOnError (websocket.js:1328-1338), which destroys the socket without emitting error on the WebSocket, so a plain drop only closes; a protocol error on a live socket (receiverOnError) does emit error and crashes the same way. AUD-BUY-005 (no unhandledRejection handler) is the promise-rejection sibling; this is a synchronous EventEmitter throw, a separate mechanism with the same effect.
- **Escalation:** ESC-ANTIRUG-01
- **Decision card:** OD-11
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-005, AUD-BUY-008, AUD-ANTIRUG-001, AUD-ANTIRUG-008, AUD-TX-009
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Attach an error listener to every WebSocket before it can fail (part of the single WebSocket owner, card OD-11); treat a failed connect as a failed attempt that stays in the backoff loop, so the tiered alerts become reachable; decide the process-level uncaught-exception policy together with AUD-BUY-005. Phase 24, proven in Phase 23 with a refused-connect test against a real socket (not a mocked provider).
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-003: The circuit breaker counts dispatches, not rugs: every matching log of one LP removal starts its own confirm gate and exit attempt, refused duplicates still count, so one rug can trip the chain breaker and suppress every later anti-rug exit on that chain

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C14 (idempotent exits), C15 (TOCTOU), C12 (timer leaks)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 candidate. The counting rule is a code fact (sub-claims 1, 3, 4). Whether one real rug reaches three dispatches depends on how many matched logs one removal emits (sub-claim 2), which needs a Phase 23 fork replay of a complete removal transaction; with two per removal, two rugs within an hour trip the breaker, which is the serial-rugger case. After a trip, every other open position on the chain has no anti-rug exit until the operator resets the breaker or restarts. Live mode only: in dry-run (the default) the breaker is never reached (exitTrigger.ts:179-216).
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/anti-rug/events.ts`, `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts`, `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/chainRegistry.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1341-1396@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - dispatchEvent evaluates each log on its own; there is no per-position, per-transaction or in-flight dedupe
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:628-637@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - one filter covers four topics (V2 Burn, V2 Transfer, V3 Burn, V3 Collect) on every registered pair or pool (events.ts:81-95)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:2251-2253@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 Burn and V2 Transfer logs both go to the V2 evaluator; decodeDestination (:1519-1532) takes the to field of each
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1964-1983@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - each unsafe verdict schedules its own confirm gate; each gate (:1848-1908) calls triggerAntiRugExit
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:240@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - every trigger clears the token timers and calls executeFullSell (:263-269)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:832-835@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the second and later calls return false at once because the sell lock is held
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:312-319@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - incrementCircuitBreaker runs on every call, success or failure (refusals included)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:107-128@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - per-chain timestamp count; trips at recent.length >= threshold
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:227-228@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - default threshold 3 in a 1 h window (same at :291-292, :348-349, :405-406)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:221-232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - once tripped, every anti-rug exit on the chain returns false with only a log.fatal; no Telegram per suppressed exit
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:464-492@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - unregisterAntiRugPosition removes the registry entry but not pending confirm gates (:1909) or V3 grace watchers (:2167); a gate scheduled before a close still fires and counts
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:337-397@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the fork tests build one synthetic log per case; the HORSE replay (:808-826) dispatches only the Burn log of the rug transaction, so the full log set of a removal is never dispatched in any test
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1967-1982@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Multiple logs from one withdrawal create independent exit triggers
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:221-232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Concurrent exits bypass the circuit-breaker threshold
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:471-487@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Unregistering a trade leaves its delayed exits active
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every path into triggerAntiRugExit: the confirm gate (detector.ts:1834, :1900) reached from the live WS dispatcher (:652), the HTTP poller (:1297), the backfill replay (:1155, AUD-ANTIRUG-005) and the V3 grace watcher (:2140). Every call site of incrementCircuitBreaker (exitTrigger.ts:316 only) and isCircuitBreakerTripped (exitTrigger.ts:221, api/routes/antiRug.ts:59). Multipliers of the count: duplicate subscriptions (AUD-ANTIRUG-001), stacked HTTP pollers (AUD-ANTIRUG-007), backfill replays (AUD-ANTIRUG-005), stale gates of closed positions (this entry).
- **Escalation:** ESC-ANTIRUG-01
- **Decision card:** OD-47
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-001, AUD-ANTIRUG-004, AUD-ANTIRUG-005, AUD-ANTIRUG-007, AUD-ANTIRUG-010, AUD-EXIT-014
- **Tags:** capital
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] (1) The breaker counts each triggerAntiRugExit call, and each unsafe log verdict makes one; nothing groups calls by position or by transaction. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1341-1396@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1964-1983@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:312-319@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [candidate] (2) A V2 removal through the router emits several logs this filter matches: the LP Transfer from the remover to the pair, the LP Transfer from the pair to the zero address, and the pair Burn. Each is evaluated against post-removal state, so one removal yields up to three unsafe verdicts. Uniswap source is not in the repo; the Phase 23 fork replay must count the dispatched logs of a real removal. (evidence: src/anti-rug/events.ts:39-49@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1519-1532@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:808-826@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (3) Duplicate subscriptions, stacked pollers, backfill replays and stale gates of closed positions add further counts. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:643-657@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1261@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1155@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:464-492@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (4) The increment happens after the exit returns, so the threshold-th exit has already been sent when the breaker trips; the breaker limits damage only from the next trigger on. (evidence: src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:263-319@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:127@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Keep one in-flight anti-rug dispatch per position (keyed by tradeId, with the triggering tx hash as evidence), count the breaker per position or per rug event rather than per log, cancel pending gates and grace watchers on unregister, and send a Telegram alert for every suppressed exit. Card ANTIRUG-01. Phase 24, after a fork replay of a complete removal transaction.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-004: A refused, timed-out or failed anti-rug escape is never retried by the detector: nothing records the unsafe verdict, re-triggering needs a new LP log, and the poll timer the escape cleared comes back only on some failure paths

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C14 (idempotent exits), C12 (timer leaks), C07 (nonce management)
- **Severity rationale:** S1, confirmed by code reading; this also confirms the mechanism AUD-EXIT-014 left as a candidate (that entry is EXIT-owned; its status is for the 22-28 consolidation to update). Plausible conditions: a rug that starts while another exit of the token is in flight (stop-loss firing on the first dumps), a 60 s budget overrun behind the wallet nonce lock, or one RPC error during the evaluation or the confirm re-read. The emergency exit is then lost, and in the partial-sell case the routine exit too.
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1832-1842@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - confirmBlocks 0: triggerAntiRugExit is awaited and its boolean discarded
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1900-1907@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - confirmBlocks > 0: same, the result is discarded; no pending-rug state is kept anywhere in the module
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1850@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the gate removes its block handler before it re-evaluates; one gate is one attempt
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1871-1882@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a re-evaluation RPC error aborts the dispatch; the log calls it fail-closed but it means no exit and no alert
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1991-2003@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - an RPC error while evaluating the triggering log returns verdict unknown with only log.error (V3 the same at :2078-2091); no retry, no alert
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:255-262@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - comment: the position "retries on a later poll/anti-rug cycle"; no anti-rug cycle exists, dispatch is log-driven only (:1341), plus backfill (:1007) and the gate and grace watchers
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:240@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - every timer of the token is cleared before executeFullSell
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:832-835@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a sell-lock refusal returns false without keepMonitoringFailedHeld, so this path never re-arms the timer
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:719-732@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the re-arm exists only inside keepMonitoringFailedHeld (failed or still-held exits that reach it)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1483-1591@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a detached partial sell holding the lock ends (return true :1584, false :1588) without re-arming the poll interval anti-rug cleared
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:263-296@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a budget overrun frees the caller and counts as failure; the underlying executeFullSell keeps running and decides the re-arm on its own later
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:782-789@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the private escalation holds the wallet nonce lock for the whole ladder, so an anti-rug exit of another token waits there and can overrun its 60 s budget (RC-11 sibling owned by the TX slice; AUD-EXIT-014)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1871-1881@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): A transient confirmation RPC error permanently consumes the trigger
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:270-286@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Watchdog timeout does not restore the exit timers it cleared
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every way a dispatch can end without a sell: sell-lock refusal (exitEngine.ts:832), routine-pause check (bypassed for anti-rug, :824), budget overrun (exitTrigger.ts:263-296), executeFullSell returning false on its own paths (AUD-EXIT-007), confirm re-read error (detector.ts:1871), evaluator error (:1991, :2078), circuit breaker (exitTrigger.ts:221) and dry-run (:179). Every way a dispatch can recur: a new matching log on the pair or pool (dispatchEvent :1341), a backfill replay (:1007, AUD-ANTIRUG-005), the V3 grace timeout (:2123-2141, once per Burn). No other trigger exists in the slice.
- **Escalation:** ESC-ANTIRUG-01
- **Decision card:** OD-45
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-014, AUD-EXIT-007, AUD-ANTIRUG-003, AUD-ANTIRUG-005
- **Tags:** capital
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] (1) Answer to the AUD-EXIT-014 open question (22-18): a refused or timed-out rug escape does NOT fire again by design. It recurs only when (a) a new Burn, Transfer or Collect log arrives on the same pair or pool and evaluates unsafe, or (b) a backfill replay (AUD-ANTIRUG-005) happens to re-cover the original rug logs, which needs a WS reconnect or any new registration on the chain with a gap within maxBackfillBlocks. After a completed rug there are usually no further LP logs, so in practice the escape is lost. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1832-1842@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1900-1907@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1341-1396@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1146-1159@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (2) If the sell lock was held by a detached partial sell when anti-rug fired, nothing re-arms the poll interval anti-rug cleared; the position stays held with anti-rug registered but no stop-loss, trailing or urgency exit (the AUD-EXIT-007 shape). (evidence: src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:240@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:832-835@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:1483-1591@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (3) Each refused or timed-out attempt still counts against the circuit breaker. (evidence: src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:312-319@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Keep per-position anti-rug state: an unsafe verdict stays pending until a successful exit or a genuine close, and a refused, aborted or failed escape is retried on the next block (bounded, with the anti-rug parameters) with an alert each time; re-arm the poll timer on every false return after clearing it. Precedence over in-flight exits is card EXIT-11; dedupe and retry are card ANTIRUG-01. Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-005: Backfill does not do what its contract says: it fires live exits through the evaluator, it replays already-handled windows on every registration, and after a long healthy session any reconnect exceeds the maximum window so the real outage is never replayed

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill), C14 (idempotent exits), C13 (SQLite transaction boundaries and crash consistency)
- **Severity rationale:** S1. Sub-claim 3 is the capital case: a rug during a WebSocket outage that follows a long connected period is never evaluated, so no anti-rug exit fires for it; the GAP DETECTED alert only says that blocks were missed, with a count measured from the last subscription rather than the outage. At typical block times (12 s ETH, about 2 s Base, about 0.25 s Arbitrum; block times are not in the repo) 7200 blocks is about 24 h, 4 h and 30 min, so on Arbitrum any reconnect more than half an hour after the last registration skips the replay. Sub-claim 1 partly helps (a still-held position does get an exit attempt) but contradicts the documented rule and adds breaker counts (AUD-ANTIRUG-003).
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/chainRegistry.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
