The HTTP poller is LIVE by design and advances the block every tick; its own defects are AUD-ANTIRUG-007. The restart window has the same bound: it starts at the last subscription of the previous run, not at shutdown.
- **Escalation:** ESC-ANTIRUG-01
- **Decision card:** OD-48
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-003, AUD-ANTIRUG-004, AUD-ANTIRUG-016
- **Tags:** capital
- **Traces:**
  - A backfill runs while an anti-rug exit for the same position is pending (double trigger or skipped trigger?): Rug log R (block X) arrives on the live WS filter (detector.ts:655 -> dispatchEvent :1341). The V2 evaluator returns unsafe and schedules confirm gate G1 at getBlockNumber()+confirmBlocks (:1845-1909)., G1 fires: triggerAntiRugExit clears the token timers (exitTrigger.ts:240) and executeFullSell takes the sell lock (exitEngine.ts:832) and works through the private attempt and fallback, up to the 60 s budget (exitTrigger.ts:263-269)., While G1 is in flight, a backfill starts: a buy of another token on the chain registers (detector.ts:447 -> :718), or the socket closes (:943). last_seen_block still holds the block of the previous subscription, because only the backfill writes it on the WS path (:1018, :1040, :1079, :1093, :1199), so the window [last_seen+1, now] contains R., The backfill evaluates R for the still-registered position (:1155). The evaluator returns unsafe and schedules gate G2 (:1976) before returning; the backfill then logs antirug.backfill.too-late and broadcasts outcome too-late (:1160-1183)., G2 fires on the next block: timers cleared again, executeFullSell refused because G1 holds the sell lock (exitEngine.ts:832-835), broadcast exit-fired success false (exitTrigger.ts:303-310), incrementCircuitBreaker with outcome exit-fired-failure (:312-319)., If G1 had already finished: a genuine close unregistered the position (exitEngine.ts:673), so the backfill finds no position for R and does nothing; a failed, still-held exit makes G2 an unplanned retry (helpful, but still counted). -> A double trigger, not a skipped one. There is no double sell (the sell lock serializes), but the duplicate costs one circuit-breaker count, puts a false exit-failed state and a too-late event on the dashboard while the real exit is in flight, and clears the timers a second time. With confirmBlocks 0 the duplicate runs inside the backfill and the registering buy waits for it.
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] (1) Backfilled unsafe verdicts schedule live exits, contrary to the D-BACKFILL comments. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1146-1159@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1964-1983@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:713-718@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (2) On the WS path last_seen_block moves only when a (re)subscription runs a backfill, so every new registration replays every log since the previous registration, including logs that were already dispatched live. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1018@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1199@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:447@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (3) After a connected stretch longer than maxBackfillBlocks since the last registration, any reconnect (or restart) takes the gap branch and replays nothing, so the outage window itself is never evaluated. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1048-1085@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/chainRegistry.ts:231@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (4) A failed backfill getLogs only logs; no alert, and the listener reports connected. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1117-1131@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:678-693@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (5) With confirmBlocks 0 the replayed trigger runs inside the backfill loop and the registering buy (or the boot resume) waits for the exit, up to the 60 s budget per event. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1832-1843@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:432-440@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Advance last_seen_block from the live stream (every dispatched log block, or a block subscription) so a replay covers the real outage; decide on card ANTIRUG-02 whether backfilled unsafe verdicts for still-held positions should exit (today they do, against the comment) and make code and docs agree; alert on a failed backfill; never run a backfill inside a buy registration. Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-011: After a restart anti-rug re-registers each position with the first dex of its pool type, not the dex it was bought on, so a position on a chain second V2 dex (every chain has two) gets its emergency exit routed through the wrong router

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C14 (idempotent exits)
- **Severity rationale:** S1, as AUD-EXIT-013. After any restart, every position bought on a second dex has an anti-rug exit that sells through a router whose factory either has no pair for the token (the sell reverts) or a different pool. On BSC V3 the sell simulation hits the other dex quoter, reverts, and trips signal 3 (fail-closed), so the trigger fires and the escape fails. Restarts are routine, and half of the V2 dexes are second dexes. Merged at 22-28 into AUD-EXIT-013 (canonical): same defect, one root cause (the resume path picks the first dex of the pool type instead of the stored dex_name), one fix, card EXIT-10.
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`, `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/utils/db.ts`, `src/chainRegistry.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:2096-2098@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - ctx.chain.dexes.find(d => d.dexType === trade.pool_type): first dex of that type
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:612-621@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - getResumeAntiRugTrades does not select dex_name
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:321-322@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - dex_name is recorded on the buy row (bot.ts:1145, :1469 pass dex.name), so the right dex is known and not used
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:397-406@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the dex is stored on the RegisteredPosition
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1900-1907@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - it is passed to triggerAntiRugExit, which calls executeFullSell(ctx, dex, ...) (exitTrigger.ts:266)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1713-1722@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the V3 sell simulation uses position.dex.quoterAddress
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:176-195@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - ETH lists uniswap-v2 and sushiswap-v2; BSC lists two V2 and two V3 (:238-264), Base two V2 (:302-321), Arbitrum two V2 (:359-378)
- **Sibling sites checked:** AUD-EXIT-013 records the same first-of-type choice for the exit-monitor resume (bot.ts:1940-1956) and the dashboard sells (controls.ts findDex); its sibling list does not name this anti-rug resume site (bot.ts:2098), which is why this is a separate entry. The registrations at buy time (bot.ts:440, :1492) pass the correct dex. The backfill and dispatch paths use whatever dex the registration stored.
- **Escalation:** ESC-EXIT-01
- **Decision card:** OD-44
- **Duplicate of:** AUD-EXIT-013
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-013
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Resolve the dex from trades.dex_name on resume, for both the exit monitor and anti-rug (card EXIT-10). Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-018: HTTP anti-rug polling requests the whole outstanding range unchunked and resumes from the stored chain_state block after a restart, so a gap larger than the provider log-range limit (an ordinary few-minute outage or restart) fails every poll from then on while the chain reports connected

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / external
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 (raised from S2 on 2026-11-11 by operator ruling ESC-ANTIRUG-03). Capital can be stranded under a plausible condition: on a chain running without a WebSocket URL, a held position loses rug protection, silently, after an ordinary outage or restart. The S2 rationale rested on two sub-claims that a code re-read falsified. (a) "Protection then stays off until restart" is wrong: a restart does not clear it. The poller re-reads its start block from the chain_state row (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1228-1232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, :1231-1235 at HEAD), the row advances only after a successful poll (:1300-1306 at base, :1303-1309 at HEAD) or a tick with no registered positions (:1269-1276 at base, :1272-1279 at HEAD), and on restart the held positions are re-registered before the poller starts (src/bot.ts:2120-2144 at base, :2122-2146 at HEAD), so the first poll after a restart requests the whole downtime range again and fails the same way. (b) "after an outage larger than the provider range limit" understated how ordinary the condition is: getLogs asks for lastBlock+1..currentBlock in one call (:1279-1291 at base, :1282-1294 at HEAD), and the repo's own range assumption is 10 blocks on ETH ("Alchemy free-tier safe", src/chainRegistry.ts:223-230, unchanged at HEAD) and 500 on the other chains (:294, :351, :408), so about two minutes of downtime on ETH (10 blocks of 12 s) is enough. It is silent: the dashboard shows the chain connected (detector.ts:1242 at base, :1245 at HEAD; AUD-ANTIRUG-007) and the only signal is a repeating antirug.http-polling.error log line (:1312 at base, :1315 at HEAD). Not reproduced yet; whether the operator's provider refuses these ranges is unmeasured, and the operator does not know whether any chain runs without a WebSocket URL. The grade does not depend on that exposure. Phase 23 Wave 5 gives it a real-path test that fails today; the fix is a Phase 24 capital fix (card OD-48).
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1279-1291@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - getLogs from lastBlock + 1 to current, no chunking
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1300@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - lastBlock advances only after success
  - command: `sed -n 1279,1300p of the base snapshot (22-27 merge)` - Claude verification: lines re-read. A failed poll leaves lastBlock unchanged, so the range only grows. Not reproduced against a provider.
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1228-1232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the poller seeds lastBlock from the chain_state row when one exists (HEAD :1231-1235), so a restart resumes from the stuck block
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1269-1276@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the row also advances on a tick with no registered positions (HEAD :1272-1279); with a held position it does not
  - code: `src/bot.ts:2120-2144@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - restart re-registers held positions (Step 3) before startChainAntiRugListener starts the poller (Step 4) (HEAD :2122-2146)
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:223-230@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - defaultAntiRugBackfillCapBlocks 10 on ETH, "Alchemy free-tier safe"; 500 on the other chains (:294, :351, :408)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1242@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - HTTP polling sets healthState connected (HEAD :1245); a failed tick only logs antirug.http-polling.error (:1312, HEAD :1315)
  - command: `git show 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820:src/anti-rug/detector.ts | grep -n (2026-11-11, 23-01 continuation executor)` - line refs re-measured at the audit base and at HEAD; the 23-01 checkpoint cited bot.ts :2120-2144 as HEAD, which is the base range (HEAD is :2122-2146). Not reproduced against a provider.
- **Sibling sites checked:** Backfill uses a chunked helper (getLogsForBackfill) and TH-ANTIRUG-06 holds that cap. The HTTP poller does not use it. Re-read 2026-11-11: the first anti-rug start stamps the dry-run row before the poller seeds (detector.ts:585 at base, :588 at HEAD; AUD-ANTIRUG-024), so the poller's no-row seed branch is not taken after the stamp and its start block on a chain's first start is 0; this is harmless while no position is registered (the no-positions tick moves it to the head) and is noted here, not graded separately.
- **Escalation:** ESC-ANTIRUG-03
- **Decision card:** OD-48
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-007, AUD-ANTIRUG-005
- **Tags:** external-only, capital, phase-23, regraded
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] (1) A restart does not clear the stuck range: the poller resumes from the stored chain_state block, which only advances after a successful poll or a no-positions tick, and held positions are registered before the poller starts. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1228-1232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1269-1276@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1300-1306@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:2120-2144@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed (code reading); provider refusal of these ranges not measured] (2) Ordinary downtime triggers it: getLogs requests lastBlock+1..currentBlock unchunked, and the repo assumes a 10-block range on ETH (about two minutes) and 500 blocks elsewhere. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1279-1291@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/chainRegistry.ts:223-230@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] (3) It is silent: HTTP polling reports the chain connected and a failed tick only logs antirug.http-polling.error and retries the same range. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1242@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1307-1316@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Use the chunked helper in the poller and bound the catch-up so a long gap is replayed in provider-sized windows; surface a failed poll as a health change instead of reporting connected; decide the outage handling in card OD-48. Phase 24 (capital fix, S1 since ESC-ANTIRUG-03), after a Phase 23 Wave 5 real-path test that fails today. Nothing is fixed in Phase 22 or 23.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** codex, claude (23-01 executor and execute-phase orchestrator, code re-read 2026-11-11) / 2026-11-09 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-025: Every boot that resumes an open position drops the anti-rug WebSocket subscription: resume registers the position and then re-arms the chain listener, whose un-awaited off() and on() of the same filter race inside ethers, so the new dispatcher lands on a stopped subscriber and no eth_subscribe is sent

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 (capital can be stranded under a plausible condition), STRAND, graded by the 23-06 executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. Condition: any boot with an open position on a chain that has a WebSocket URL, which is the ordinary restart. Effect: the position is registered, the dashboard shows it monitored and the log says the subscription was installed, but no rug log reaches the evaluator until a later buy on a new pair re-subscribes, so liquidity removal is not seen for as long as that takes. The exit monitor is not affected. Graded like AUD-ANTIRUG-001 (S1, STRAND: the rug-log subscription can vanish after a dashboard stop); anti-rug live execution defaults to dry-run, which limits what a delivered log would do today but not the grade, as for AUD-ANTIRUG-001.
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:2120@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - resumeAntiRugMonitoring step 3: registerAntiRugPosition for each open position, which calls startChainAntiRugListener (detector.ts:447) and installs the address filter
  - code: `src/bot.ts:2130-2144@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - step 4: startChainAntiRugListener(ctx) again for every verified chain, with the same registered address set
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:644@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a dispatcher is already installed, so ctx.wsProvider.off(state.activeFilter, state.activeDispatcher) is called and not awaited
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:655@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - then ctx.wsProvider.on(filter, dispatcher), also not awaited, with a filter of the same addresses and topics, so ethers computes the same subscription tag
  - command: `sed -n 1040,1160p node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js (ethers 6.16.0, the version package-lock.json pins for node_modules/ethers)` - on() and off() each await getSubscription before touching #subs; on() looks the tag up before off() deletes it, gets the old subscriber (already started, so nothing is started) and pushes the new listener onto it; off() then removes the old listener, finds none left, calls subscriber.stop() (eth_unsubscribe) and deletes the tag. Pure microtask order inside ethers, no network between, so a real node sees the same sequence
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:664@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - antirug.listener.subscribed is logged on both calls, so the log says the subscription was installed twice while none remains
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1805@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - startMultiChainBot calls resumeAntiRugMonitoring once at every boot; the same code at HEAD (src unchanged in Phase 23): bot.ts:1807, :2122, :2132-2146; detector.ts:450, :647, :658, :667
  - command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/triage/AUD-ANTIRUG-025.test.ts (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-11)` - real ETH V2 snipe on a temp-file database, armed; an LP Transfer to an allowlisted locker is evaluated (antirug.allowlist-hit); after restartGraph and the real resumeMultiChainMonitoring and resumeAntiRugMonitoring: two antirug.listener.subscribed lines, one eth_subscribe for the pair then its eth_unsubscribe and no other, the node holds no logs subscription, and a second LP Transfer to another locker is never evaluated (claim resume-drops-ws-subscription); the position is still in getRegisteredPositions and its exit monitor is armed. Fix-shaped mutations (await the off(); skip an unchanged re-subscribe) each read looks fixed, detector.ts restored identical
  - command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/triage/AUD-BUY-001.test.ts (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-11)` - first seen here: on base, after the restart that picks up the script's deliberate position, the queued eth_unsubscribe drained and the node held zero subscriptions
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every caller of startChainAntiRugListener at the base: registerAntiRugPosition (detector.ts:447), the reconnect path (:943) and boot step 4 (bot.ts:2144). Reconnect: the new provider has no subscriber under the old tag, so off() is a no-op on it and on() subscribes (not affected; the old provider is AUD-ANTIRUG-001). registerAntiRugPosition for a position on a pair that is NOT yet watched changes the address set, so the tag differs and on() creates a new subscriber (not affected). registerAntiRugPosition for a second position on a pair that IS already watched (bucket.push, :416-421) keeps the address set unchanged and takes the same off()/on() path: by code reading the same race drops the subscription for every watched pair (not run). After a drop, the next registration of a new pair restores the subscription with the full set, so the blind window is from boot to the next new-pair buy. The HTTP-polling fallback (no WS URL) does not use the filter subscription. bot.ts DEX listeners call on() once per start (not affected). Interaction: the interim operator rule on AUD-BUY-001 (ESC-BUY-01, restart the main bot after any deliberate buy) re-arms the exit monitor but, through this finding, not the anti-rug subscription.
- **Escalation:** ESC-ANTIRUG-04
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-001, AUD-ANTIRUG-016, AUD-ANTIRUG-005, AUD-BUY-001
- **Tags:** capital, found-by-realpath-harness, phase-23
- **Traces:**
  - Boot with one open position on a WebSocket chain (ETH V2 in the proof): startMultiChainBot calls resumeAntiRugMonitoring (bot.ts:1805)., Step 3: registerAntiRugPosition adds the position and calls startChainAntiRugListener: no prior dispatcher, so on(F) subscribes (eth_subscribe for [pair])., Step 4: startChainAntiRugListener again: a dispatcher exists, so off(F) then on(F') run without await; F and F' have the same tag., Inside ethers, on(F') finds the existing subscriber and attaches the new dispatcher to it; off(F) then removes the old dispatcher, stops the subscriber (eth_unsubscribe) and deletes the tag., No eth_subscribe follows; the node holds no subscription; LP Transfer and Burn logs on the pair are never delivered. -> Anti-rug is blind for every resumed position until a new pair is registered, while the registry, the dashboard and the logs show it armed.
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24 (capital fix, with card OD-11's single WebSocket owner if that lands first): await the off() before the on(), or skip the re-subscribe when the watched address set is unchanged, and assert the node-side subscription after boot (test/realpath/triage/AUD-ANTIRUG-025.test.ts reads looks fixed for both shapes). Until fixed, after any restart with open positions on a WebSocket chain the anti-rug subscription is not live; this weakens the interim rule on AUD-BUY-001 (restart the main bot after a deliberate buy). Nothing is fixed in Phase 23.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (23-06 executor) / 2026-11-11 / 23a6461

##### AUD-API-001: Emergency-sell and force-sell skip still-held positions whose exit already failed

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / independent
- **Classes:** C14 (idempotent exits), C15 (TOCTOU)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 STRAND: a failed exit on a position that is still held is a plausible, already-observed condition (the LADYS case this code was written for: a reverting or honeypot-like sell, an RPC or bundle error inside the sell). After it, the operator's two manual exits cannot reach the position: force-sell answers 404 'Trade not found or already closed' and emergency sell-all either says 'No open positions to sell' or reports success while the tokens stay in the wallet; the dashboard does not even list the position. The bot's own monitor and anti-rug are kept (exitEngine.ts:723-732), so it is not S0, but the human safety net that exists for exactly this moment is gone and is told nothing. The bot is OFF for all of v7.0, so there is no live exposure. Escalated early as ESC-PRE-04 (operator ruling 2026-11-06 'Escalate early + own in 22-22'); this entry is that record's resolution, not a second escalation.
- **Files:** `src/api/routes/controls.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/utils/db.ts`, `src/bot.ts`, `src/api/helpers/positions.ts`, `src/api/routes/trades.ts`, `src/api/routes/risk.ts`, `src/api/routes/health.ts`, `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx`, `dashboard/src/pages/Overview.tsx`, `dashboard/src/components/PositionTable.tsx`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1112-1167@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - executeFullSell catch path: re-fetches balanceOf; when the position is STILL HELD (balance > dust, or the re-fetch failed and the -1n sentinel is used) it runs the still-held branch
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1163@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - updateTradeStatus.run('failed', token, chain): the buy row becomes trades.status = 'failed' while the tokens are still in the wallet
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:325-327@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - updateTradeStatus: UPDATE trades SET status = ? WHERE token = ? AND chain = ? AND status = 'pending' (every pending row of that token and chain)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1164@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - then keepMonitoringFailedHeld(...)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:700@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - keepMonitoringFailedHeld: markExitFailedHeld.run(tradeId)
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:540-545@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - markExitFailedHeld: UPDATE exit_state SET exit_status = 'exit_failed_held', exit_failure_count = exit_failure_count + 1
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:723-732@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the bot itself keeps the position alive: anti-rug kept, poll timer re-armed through resumeExitMonitor
  - code: `src/api/routes/controls.ts:51-56@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - prepared statements getPendingTrade / getAllPendingTrades: SELECT ... FROM trades WHERE [id = ? AND] status = ? AND action = ?
  - code: `src/api/routes/controls.ts:70-74@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - force-sell: getPendingTrade.get(tradeId, 'pending', 'buy'); no row -> 404 { error: 'Trade not found or already closed' }
  - code: `src/api/routes/controls.ts:126-131@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - emergency-sell: getAllPendingTrades.all('pending', 'buy'); empty -> { ok: true, sold: 0, failed: 0, message: 'No open positions to sell' }
  - code: `src/api/routes/controls.ts:140-219@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - emergency-sell loops only over the selected pending rows; when every selected sell succeeds it answers { ok: true, sold, failed: 0, errors: [] } with no word about rows it never selected
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:597-604@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - getResumeExitMonitorTrades: WHERE (t.status = 'pending' AND t.action = 'buy') OR e.exit_status = 'exit_failed_held' (restart-resume already includes failed-held positions)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1892-1911@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - resumeMultiChainMonitoring uses getResumeExitMonitorTrades at :1904; the comment at :1893-1903 names exactly this class (a catch-path failed-held row dropped by a pending-only scan)
  - code: `src/api/helpers/positions.ts:55-56@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the dashboard position list (REST /api/positions and the 5 s positions_update broadcast) keeps only getPnL rows with buy_status === 'pending'
  - code: `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:98-103@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the Emergency Sell All handler shows a message only when result.failed > 0; sold: 0 with "No open positions to sell" and a partial success both show nothing
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every API, dashboard and scripts site that selects or labels open positions, re-measured at the base SHA: (1) src/api/routes/controls.ts:51-56/:70/:126 force-sell and emergency-sell select status='pending' AND action='buy' only (this finding). (2) src/api/helpers/positions.ts:56 keeps buy_status === 'pending' only, and :73 getTradeIdForPendingToken (src/utils/db.ts:549-551, status='pending') resolves the trade id the same way: a failed-held position is absent from the dashboard Open Positions table, so no Force Sell button exists for it (sub_claim 3). (3) src/api/routes/trades.ts:103 labels buy_status !== 'pending' as 'closed', so trade history shows the still-held position as closed at a full loss (sub_claim 4; dashboard/src/components/TradeTable.tsx:189-194 renders that label). (4) src/api/routes/risk.ts:85 and :88 (getOpenPositionCount db.ts:420-422, getTotalExposure db.ts:425-438), src/api/routes/health.ts:59-60 and risk.ts:37 / health.ts:60 getPortfolioExposure (src/riskManager.ts:48-63, WHERE at :61): the dashboard position count, exposure total, exposure donut and /health leave failed-held positions out (sub_claim 5, display only; the enforcement side of the same statements is AUD-DB-003, DB slice, named not edited). (5) DB-slice siblings named by path only: src/riskManager.ts:61, src/utils/db.ts:421, :437, :550 and :561 (getStaleTradesQuery, used by preflight checkStaleData, so a failed-held position is also never reported as stale). (6) scripts/: git grep at the base SHA for FROM trades, status =, getPnL, getOpenPositionCount, getAllPendingTrades and exit_status under scripts/ finds no trade-status selection (scripts/recover-sell-ladys.ts and scripts/deliberate-buy.ts sign directly and do not read the trades table): none. (7) Contrast sites that DO include failed-held positions: getResumeExitMonitorTrades and getResumeAntiRugTrades (db.ts:597-620) used on restart (bot.ts:1904, :2063). Sub-case recorded for 22-28: a still-held failure that ends through the success-but-still-held path (exitEngine.ts:1110) or the inconclusive path (:995) keeps trades.status = 'pending', so it IS selected by both controls, but once its exit_failure_count reaches EXIT_ROUTINE_MAX_FAILURES the routine pause refuses the dashboard sell (AUD-EXIT-008); either way a failed-held position cannot be sold from the dashboard.
- **Escalation:** ESC-PRE-04
- **Decision card:** OD-64
- **Related:** AUD-DB-003, AUD-EXIT-008, AUD-EXIT-007, AUD-EXIT-013, AUD-API-004
- **Tags:** capital, d-stop-the-line, cross-class
- **Pre-phase key:** failed-held-sell-selection
- **Traces:**
  - 1. A still-held position whose exit throws (the catch path): executeFullSell runs for the position (any reason: trailing-stop, stop-loss, urgency, anti-rug, or a dashboard sell) and something inside the try throws: a reverting public-fallback sell, an approval failure, a bundle or RPC error (src/exitEngine.ts:837-1111), the catch re-fetches balanceOf; the tokens are still in the wallet (balance > dust), or the re-fetch fails and the -1n sentinel means "assume held" (src/exitEngine.ts:1126-1143), updateTradeStatus.run('failed', ...) sets trades.status = 'failed' on every pending row of that token and chain (src/exitEngine.ts:1163; src/utils/db.ts:325-327), keepMonitoringFailedHeld -> markExitFailedHeld sets exit_state.exit_status = 'exit_failed_held' and increments exit_failure_count (src/exitEngine.ts:700; src/utils/db.ts:540-545); anti-rug stays registered and the poll timer is re-armed (src/exitEngine.ts:723-732) -> The position is still held and still monitored by the bot, but its buy row now says status='failed' and its exit_state says exit_failed_held.
  - 2. The operator presses Emergency Sell All (POST /emergency-sell): the route runs getAllPendingTrades.all('pending', 'buy') (src/api/routes/controls.ts:54-56, :126): the failed-held position is not selected because its status is 'failed', if the failed-held positions are the only ones left, the answer is { ok: true, sold: 0, failed: 0, message: 'No open positions to sell' } (controls.ts:128-131), if there is a mix, the loop sells the pending positions only (controls.ts:140-199) and, when those succeed, answers { ok: true, sold: n, failed: 0, errors: [] } (controls.ts:212-219); the skipped failed-held positions are not mentioned, the dashboard shows a message only when failed > 0 (dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:98-103), so in both cases the operator sees no warning -> Emergency sell reports 'No open positions to sell' (or a clean success) while the failed-held tokens stay in the wallet.
  - 3. The operator tries POST /force-sell/:tradeId for that trade: the dashboard has no button for it: the Open Positions table is built from buy_status === pending rows only (src/api/helpers/positions.ts:56; dashboard/src/pages/Overview.tsx:162-170), a direct request runs getPendingTrade.get(tradeId, 'pending', 'buy') (controls.ts:51-53, :70) and finds no row, the route answers 404 { error: 'Trade not found or already closed' } (controls.ts:71-74) -> force-sell refuses the position as 'not found or already closed' although it is open on-chain.
  - 4. Contrast: what the bot itself treats as open on restart: getResumeExitMonitorTrades selects (status = 'pending' AND action = 'buy') OR exit_state.exit_status = 'exit_failed_held' (src/utils/db.ts:597-604); getResumeAntiRugTrades does the same with the LP baseline (db.ts:612-620), resumeMultiChainMonitoring uses it on every boot (src/bot.ts:1904), with a comment naming this exact class of drop (bot.ts:1893-1903) -> The bot's own recovery counts a failed-held position as open; the operator's emergency controls and position list do not. The two definitions of 'open' disagree.
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] force-sell answers 404 'Trade not found or already closed' for a failed-held position (evidence: src/api/routes/controls.ts:51-53@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/routes/controls.ts:70-74@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:1163@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] emergency-sell does not select failed-held positions: 'No open positions to sell' when only those remain, a silent partial sale when mixed (evidence: src/api/routes/controls.ts:54-56@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/routes/controls.ts:126-131@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/routes/controls.ts:203-219@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:98-103@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] API-owned display sibling: the dashboard Open Positions table and the positions_update broadcast omit failed-held positions (no Force Sell button, Open Positions count excludes them, the empty-state text says the bot 'has not entered any positions yet') (evidence: src/api/helpers/positions.ts:55-56@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/helpers/positions.ts:73@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, dashboard/src/pages/Overview.tsx:63@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, dashboard/src/components/PositionTable.tsx:24-33@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] API-owned display sibling: trade history labels a failed-held position 'closed' (buy_status !== 'pending') with realized_pnl = minus the whole buy cost (evidence: src/api/routes/trades.ts:103@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/utils/db.ts:351-384@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, dashboard/src/components/TradeTable.tsx:189-194@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] API-owned display sibling: /api/risk/limits position count, /api/risk/exposure totals and /health open count and exposure leave failed-held positions out (display; enforcement is AUD-DB-003) (evidence: src/api/routes/risk.ts:85-88@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/routes/risk.ts:37@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/routes/health.ts:59-60@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/utils/db.ts:420-438@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/riskManager.ts:48-63@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Select 'open' the way the bot's own recovery does: the dashboard sell controls, the position list and the open/closed label should use one shared definition of an open position (status='pending' buys UNION exit_state.exit_status='exit_failed_held', as getResumeExitMonitorTrades already does), with balanceOf as the final truth inside executeFullSell. Emergency sell must report every position it did not sell and why. Real-path test: drive a position through the catch path (a sell that throws while the balance stays) and assert that force-sell and emergency-sell both reach it. The behaviour change is card API-01, owned by the Phase 24 capital discussion (AUDIT-05); nothing is changed in Phase 22 (NAC-13).
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** codex-review, orchestrator-trace, claude-audit / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-API-002: RC-12 dashboard "Stop chain" calls ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners(), which also removes the anti-rug rug-log subscription that shares the provider; "Start" only re-runs startDexListener, so anti-rug stays disarmed on that chain while the health indicator still shows connected

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill)
- **Research candidates:** RC-12 (research suggested S1)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 STRAND, equal to the research suggestion: one dashboard click that the UI describes as safe for open positions silently turns off the rug-pull exit for every position on that chain, and Start does not bring it back; the WS health indicator keeps showing connected, so the operator has no signal. A rug during that window is not detected (the routine stop-loss poll still runs, so not S0). The same mechanism was already shown to the operator as part of AUD-ANTIRUG-001 (ESC-ANTIRUG-01); it is presented again in the API batch as its own RC-12 item. Bot OFF, no live exposure.
- **Files:** `src/api/routes/chains.ts`, `src/bot.ts`, `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/api/routes/chains.ts:136-142@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - POST /:name/stop: stoppedChains.add, then ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners() with no event argument; the comment says the provider is kept for exit monitors
  - command: `sed -n 1159-1176p node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js (ethers 6.16.0, the installed version)` - removeAllListeners() without an event stops every started subscriber and deletes every subscription tag: factory listeners, the anti-rug log filter and any in-flight V3 Mint wait alike
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:643-657@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the anti-rug dispatcher is installed with ctx.wsProvider.on(filter, dispatcher) on the same shared provider; state.activeFilter / activeDispatcher keep pointing at the now-removed subscription
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:678-679@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - state.wsProvider and healthState = 'connected' are set at subscribe time; nothing in the stop route changes them, so the dashboard WS-health indicator keeps showing connected
  - code: `src/api/routes/chains.ts:172-176@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - POST /:name/start: stoppedChains.delete, then onRestart(ctx)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1808-1852@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - onRestart: replaces the provider only if it is missing or destroyed (:1812-1821, not the case after a stop), runs a MEV health check, then startDexListener per DEX (:1836-1845); it never re-subscribes anti-rug
  - code: `src/bot.ts:163-172@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - an in-flight V3 Mint wait listens on the same provider; it is removed too and the 30 s timeout then drops that opportunity (no buy, harmless)
  - code: `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:175@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the Stop dialog tells the operator: "Existing positions will continue being monitored by the exit engine." Anti-rug is not mentioned
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every removeAllListeners and provider re-subscription site at the base SHA (git grep -n removeAllListeners and "wsProvider.on(" over src/): chains.ts:141 (this finding, argument-less, shared provider), bot.ts:165/:172 (per-contract Mint, scoped, correct), bot.ts:2335 (shutdown, followed by destroy, correct). Re-subscription paths for the anti-rug filter: the detector subscribe path (detector.ts:643-657) runs on a new position registration and on the anti-rug reconnect (handleWsClose, detector.ts:916-944); onRestart (bot.ts:1808-1852) does neither. So after Stop the chain's held positions have no rug-log subscription until the next buy registers on that chain (Stop does not stop HTTP-polled buys, AUD-BUY-011), a WebSocket reconnect, or a bot restart; and no backfill covers the gap. The three-writer ownership problem of ctx.wsProvider (RC-13) is AUD-ANTIRUG-001, which records this same stop consequence from the anti-rug side; the DEX-listener side (duplicate listeners, no backfill, leaked providers) is AUD-BUY-008; Stop not stopping buys is AUD-BUY-011. This entry is the canonical RC-12 (H1) entry.
- **Escalation:** ESC-API-01
- **Decision card:** OD-11
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-001, AUD-BUY-008, AUD-BUY-011, AUD-ANTIRUG-002
- **Tags:** capital
- **Traces:**
  - Operator stops a WebSocket chain with one open position, later starts it again: POST /api/chains/eth/stop -> removeAllListeners() on ctx.wsProvider (chains.ts:141): the anti-rug filter subscription is stopped (eth_unsubscribe) and deleted, the position keeps its 5 s exit poll (HTTP provider); anti-rug state still says 'connected' (detector.ts:678-679), POST /api/chains/eth/start -> onRestart: provider is not destroyed, so it is kept; startDexListener per DEX re-adds factory listeners only (bot.ts:1812-1845), an LP removal on the held token emits a log that no subscriber receives; no backfill runs for the stopped window -> The rug is not detected; the position is only protected by the routine stop-loss poll until a new position registers, the socket reconnects, or the bot restarts.
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] Stop removes the anti-rug log subscription with all other provider listeners (evidence: src/api/routes/chains.ts:140-142@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:655@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, sed -n 1159-1176p node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js (ethers 6.16.0))
  - [confirmed] Start (onRestart) re-attaches only DEX listeners; anti-rug is re-subscribed only by a later position registration, a reconnect or a restart (evidence: src/bot.ts:1812-1821@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1836-1845@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:643-657@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] Nothing tells the operator: health stays connected and the Stop dialog says positions keep being monitored (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:678-679@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:175@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Never call an argument-less removeAllListeners on a shared provider. Under card OD-11 (one WebSocket owner per chain that notifies subscribers) Stop pauses only the chain's DEX factory subscribers by handle, anti-rug is never touched by Stop/Start, and Start resumes the same subscribers with a backfill from the last seen block. The Stop dialog text should say exactly what keeps running. Real-path test: Stop then Start a chain with a registered position and assert a rug log still reaches dispatchEvent. Phase 24 (capital), nothing changed in Phase 22.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-22 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-API-008: One unauthenticated request with a malformed Host header and an Upgrade header kills the bot process: the WebSocket upgrade handler parses the Host with new URL() outside any try, and nothing catches the exception

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / independent
- **Classes:** C11 (unhandled rejections), C19 (API auth/CORS)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 STRAND: in the documented remote-access mode any host that can reach the dashboard port can stop the whole bot with one short request and no credentials; the process exit stops every exit monitor, the ExitWorker and anti-rug for all chains until a human restarts it, leaving every open position without an exit. Same impact class as AUD-ANTIRUG-002 (S1). At the default 127.0.0.1 bind only a local process can do it (S2-equivalent there). Not S0: it needs a hostile or broken client, and a restart resumes monitoring. Reproduced on loopback with the exact line from the base snapshot.
- **Files:** `src/api/ws/handler.ts`, `src/api/server.ts`, `.env.example`, `docs/operations/going-live.md`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/api/ws/handler.ts:43@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - const url = new URL(req.url || '/', `http://${req.headers.host || 'localhost'}`) runs first, before the path and session checks, with no try/catch
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:183@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - server.on('upgrade', handleUpgrade(wss, sessions)): a synchronous throw in an 'upgrade' listener escapes Node's http server as an uncaught exception
  - command: `git grep -n "uncaughtException\|unhandledRejection" 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src scripts` - no output: there is no process-level handler, so the exception ends the process (same fact as AUD-ANTIRUG-002 / AUD-BUY-005)
  - command: `node ws-host-crash.js <snapshot>/src/api/ws/handler.ts <host> (scratch folder outside the repo (Node 22.16.0 by absolute path; no src/ import, no .env, no data/, no live DB; loopback 127.0.0.1 only); the handler.ts:43 line read verbatim from the audit-base snapshot and run in a plain Node http 'upgrade' listener; raw TCP request GET /ws with Upgrade: websocket)` - output: Host "127.0.0.1:8080" -> 401, server alive; Host "a b" -> server process EXITED code=1 TypeError: Invalid URL; Host "[" -> EXITED code=1 Invalid URL; Host "x:99999999" -> EXITED code=1 Invalid URL
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:208-213@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - binds DASHBOARD_HOST (default 127.0.0.1) and DASHBOARD_PORT
  - code: `.env.example:75-76@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0 documented "for remote access"
  - code: `docs/operations/going-live.md:153@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the recommended remote setup is DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0 behind a TLS proxy; the bot port itself then listens on every interface
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every Host/URL parse in src/api: server.ts:111-117 and :125-131 (inside try, correct), handler.ts:43 (this finding, no try); every synchronous code in the 'upgrade' path: parseCookies (:18-29, cannot throw on a string), validateSession (map lookup), wss.handleUpgrade (ws answers a bad handshake with 400 itself). Express routes are not affected (express 5 catches handler errors). A browser cannot send a malformed Host (it builds Host from the URL), so this needs a raw client: any local process at the default bind, any host that can reach the port in remote mode. A second, authenticated crash path on the same socket layer (an invalid frame on an open WebSocket) is AUD-API-009.
- **Escalation:** ESC-API-01
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-002, AUD-BUY-005, AUD-API-009
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Parse the upgrade URL inside try/catch (or use url.parse on the path only) and answer 400; wrap the whole upgrade handler so any throw destroys only that socket. Decide the process-level uncaught-exception policy with card OD-6 (AUD-BUY-005). Real-path test: send the malformed request to a running server and assert it stays up. Phase 24 (a pure bug fix, no behaviour decision).
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-22 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-BUY-002: A buy that has landed, or can still land, can end up with no trades row, a trades row flipped to failed, or no exit and anti-rug monitoring, because one catch treats every error after submission as a clean zero-spend failure

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C07 (nonce management), C09 (receipt status), C11 (unhandled rejections), C13 (SQLite transaction boundaries and crash consistency), C14 (idempotent exits), C16 (gas/fee ceilings)
- **Research candidates:** RC-01 (research suggested S0)
- **Severity rationale:** Graded S1, one step below the research suggestion (S0/S1, the higher end taken as the suggestion). Rubric reason: every traced failure point needs a non-default condition (a single RPC or SQLite error after inclusion, a stale load-balanced node, a multi-block inclusion timing, a revert, or a concurrent same-token handler); none fires on the ordinary success path, so it is "plausible condition" (S1), not "no unusual condition" (S0). Within S1 it is the worst kind: in the post-mine and monitoring-setup traces the held position is never re-armed, not even by a restart (the resume queries need status pending or exit_failed_held, db.ts:597-604, and anti-rug resume needs an lp_baseline row), and the operator is told "zero ETH spent". The broad catch (bot.ts:1177-1191, V3 :1508-1516) and its "fail-clean" comments (bot.ts:345-358, :1178-1187) were traced, not taken at their word.
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts`, `src/utils/db.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/utils/notifier.ts`

  - code: `src/bot.ts:1100-1112@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Buy submission precedes any recoverable trade record

The deliberate path (executeDeliberateBuy, :485-761) records and arms outside any catch (its own defect is AUD-BUY-001). Every submit strategy reachable from submitBuyTx was traced for "throws after a broadcast": flashbots fanout (flashbots.ts:303-309), shared reconcile loop (reconciliation.ts:476-497, :576-628), passthrough send (passthrough.ts:130); bloxroute.ts was traced by the TX slice (sweep/TX.json cell C07): a relay transport failure defers to reconciliation (bloxroute.ts:179-190), and after a not-landed attempt the next attempt re-signs the same nonce and only the latest hash is reconciled (reconciliation.ts:476-497, :576-603), so an earlier accepted attempt that mines reads as landed-not-ours, the same mechanism as sub_claim 3. Recorded at 22-28. Both resume queries were read (db.ts:597-604 and the lp_baseline INNER JOIN used at bot.ts:2043). The pause read, recordSnipe, insertTrade, alert, balanceOf, trade-id lookup and both arming helpers were each checked as separate throw points.
- **Escalation:** ESC-BUY-02
- **Decision card:** OD-27
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-001, AUD-BUY-004, AUD-BUY-005, AUD-BUY-020, AUD-EXIT-002
- **Tags:** capital, cross-class
- **Traces:**
  - Failure point 1, before submission: the affordability gate (or a call just before submit) throws: V2: enforceEntryExitAffordability (bot.ts:1083) is outside the try; if it (or sendCtxAlert/broadcast inside it) throws, the rejection leaves handleNewPairForChain, which no caller awaits (bot.ts:1583, :1644) -> unhandled rejection (AUD-BUY-005), V3: the same gate (bot.ts:1417) is inside the try; a throw runs the catch: emitSnipeFailClean + updateTradeStatus.run(failed, token, chain) (bot.ts:1513-1515), updateTradeStatus matches every pending row of that token on that chain (db.ts:325-327); if a concurrent same-token handler (V2 pair and V3 pool for one token, AUD-BUY-004) has already landed and inserted its pending row, that live row is flipped to failed -> This handler spent nothing and holds nothing. trades: no row of its own, but a concurrent handler's live row can become failed. exit_state: untouched. The other handler's tokens ARE held; its in-process monitor keeps running, but after any restart the failed row is not resumed (db.ts:597-604), so the position is then stranded with no exit monitor or anti-rug.
  - Failure point 2, after submission but before (or without) a confirmed mine: the strategy throws although a broadcast tx can still land: Flashbots: the bundle is sent for block tb, then a relay error for target block tb+i throws (flashbots.ts:303-309); the bundle already sent for tb can still be included, Multi-attempt: attempt k and attempt k+1 share a nonce but differ in fee and hash; reconcile checks only the latest hash (reconciliation.ts:476-497, :576-603); if attempt k mines (multi-block targeting keeps it eligible), the latest hash has no receipt while the nonce advanced -> landed-not-ours -> throw, Passthrough: if an earlier attempt mines first, the next sendTransaction can fail with nonce-too-low and throw (passthrough.ts:130), Reverted: the tx mined with status 0 -> throw (reconciliation.ts:592-597); gas was spent, Ceiling-hit: the helper throws after the last not-landed reconcile (reconciliation.ts:606-614) while a passthrough public tx can still be pending and mine later, Every one of these throws reaches the snipe catch (bot.ts:1177-1191 / :1508-1516): no insertTrade, updateTradeStatus finds no own row (or flips a concurrent one), and the operator is told "zero ETH spent, no trades row" (bot.ts:384) -> Tokens: held whenever an earlier attempt or the already-sent bundle landed, or the pending public tx mines later (not held for a revert, but gas is lost). trades: no row. exit_state: none. No exit monitor, no anti-rug, never resumed at restart (no row to resume), and isTokenSniped (any row) stays false, so dedup is broken and the same token can be bought again on a later event.
  - Failure point 3, after mining, while persisting the trade row: submitBuyTx returned the real hash, so the buy is mined (bot.ts:1100-1112), getPauseState.get (bot.ts:1118), recordSnipe (:1125) or insertTrade.run (:1127) throws (for example SQLITE_BUSY or disk full): catch -> no row written, or the insert succeeds, the awaited alert at :1147 hangs (no axios timeout, notifier.ts:80) and delays everything after it, or balanceOf (bot.ts:1159) throws on one RPC error: catch -> updateTradeStatus flips the just-inserted row to failed, alert "TX failed" -> Tokens: held. trades: either no row, or a row with status failed. exit_state: none. No exit monitor and no anti-rug; the failed row is not in getResumeExitMonitorTrades (db.ts:597-604) and has no lp_baseline, so not even a restart re-arms it. The operator is told the buy failed and cost nothing.
  - Failure point 3b, after mining: the balance read succeeds but is stale (lagging node behind a load-balanced RPC): balanceOf at bot.ts:1159 returns 0 because the node serving the call has not seen the inclusion block, nothing rejects 0: armPositionMonitoring/startExitMonitor are called with originalTokenAmount = 0, computeDustThreshold(0) uses only the 1000-wei absolute floor (exitEngine.ts:615-621); partial-sell sizes are computed from 0 (exitEngine.ts:1736) -> Tokens: held. trades: pending (correct). exit_state: written with original amount 0. The exit monitor runs, but partial-sell tiers sell 0 tokens and the stored denominator is wrong for the life of the position.
  - Failure point 4, while setting up monitoring: trade-id lookup misses (bot.ts:1162-1176): logs only, no monitor; row stays pending, startExitMonitor: queryPrice returns null -> returns without arming (exitEngine.ts:1869-1873); anti-rug is still attempted (bot.ts:431-451), startExitMonitor: upsertExitState.run throws (exitEngine.ts:1891) -> propagates out of armPositionMonitoring before anti-rug -> snipe catch flips the row to failed, snapshotLpBaseline / registerAntiRugPosition throws -> caught and logged only (bot.ts:441-451); no lp_baseline row, V3 twin arms inline (bot.ts:1481-1507) with the same shape -> Tokens: held in every branch. Lookup miss or null price: trades pending, exit_state none, unmonitored for exit until the next boot (resume re-arms it). upsertExitState throw: trades failed, exit_state none, no exit monitor and no anti-rug, never resumed. Anti-rug failure: exit monitor runs but anti-rug is absent now and after every restart (no lp_baseline row for the INNER JOIN).
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] A single balanceOf RPC error after a mined buy flips the trade row to failed and the position is never re-armed, even after restart (evidence: src/bot.ts:1158-1159@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1189@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/utils/db.ts:597-604@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] A SQLite error in the post-mine bookkeeping leaves a mined buy with no row, no monitor and broken dedup (evidence: src/bot.ts:1118-1146@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1177-1191@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] An earlier same-nonce attempt that mines is reported as landed-not-ours and the snipe path records nothing (evidence: src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts:476-497@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts:576-603@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, test/realpath/triage/AUD-BUY-002.test.ts (knownBug claim earlier-attempt-lands-no-trade-row, plan 23-05))
  - [confirmed] A Flashbots fanout error after the first send throws while the sent bundle can still land (evidence: src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts:303-309@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, test/realpath/triage/AUD-BUY-002.test.ts (knownBug claim fanout-error-after-send-no-trade-row, plan 23-05))
  - [confirmed] The V3 catch can flip a concurrent same-token handler's live pending row to failed (evidence: src/bot.ts:1417-1419@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1514@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/utils/db.ts:325-327@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [candidate] A stale balanceOf of 0 is accepted as the original token amount (evidence: src/bot.ts:1159@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:615-621@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:1736@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24 (after a Phase 23 real-path proof of at least the balanceOf-throw and earlier-attempt-landed traces): separate "did money leave the wallet" from "did bookkeeping succeed". Once a submit may have broadcast, never run the zero-spend branch: reconcile against chain truth (token balance delta plus nonce, like the deliberate guard at bot.ts:617-662), record the row, and arm monitoring with retries; on any post-landing failure alert loudly that a position is held and unprotected. The direction (intent row before broadcast vs reconcile-on-throw, retry policy) is a behaviour decision on card BUY-02. Nothing is changed in Phase 22.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-17 executor), codex / 2026-11-06 / 23a6461

##### AUD-BUY-003: Snipe buy minOut fails open: when the quote fails the buy is still sent with amountOutMin = 0

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / LOSS / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C01 (BigInt/Number mixing), C02 (|| vs ?? with 0n/''/0), C04 (slippage/minOut)
- **Research candidates:** RC-02 (research suggested S1)
- **Severity rationale:** S1, equal to the research suggestion. The code alone proves the fail-open: on any quote error minOut stays 0n and the buy proceeds. Plausible condition: one RPC error or a quoter revert during a launch block. The private routing prevents a sandwich but not buying at the top of a launch block behind other snipers, so the loss is bounded by the snipe amount, not prevented.
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`, `src/config.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1048-1056@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2: let minOut = 0n; try { getAmountsOut ... } catch { warn "defaulting to 0" } — then the swap is built with that minOut (:1104-1109)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1362-1377@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3: same pattern on quoteExactInputSingle; amountOutMinimum: minOut (:1390)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1053@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - minOut = expectedOut - expectedOut * BigInt(slippage) / 100n: BigInt() of a fractional percent throws RangeError, which the same catch turns into minOut = 0
  - code: `src/config.ts:282@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - slippagePercent is hard-coded 5, so the fractional crash is latent today; CONFIG.slippagePercent || 5 at bot.ts:1050/:1373 also makes 0 impossible
  - code: `src/bot.ts:711-729@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - sibling in the same file already fails CLOSED: the deliberate public leg returns null on a quote failure
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1048-1055@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Quote or slippage-conversion failures turn into unrestricted buys
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1050@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): A configured zero-slippage limit becomes five percent
- **Sibling sites checked:** V2 snipe (bot.ts:1048-1056) and V3 snipe (:1362-1377) both fail open. Deliberate private leg (:527-543) also defaults privMinOut to 0 on a quote failure; that is documented intent (comment :533-538: private, un-sandwichable routing) and is recorded here as a sibling for card OD-15, not as a separate defect. Deliberate public leg (:711-729) fails closed (correct). tokenSafety simulateSwap/simulateSwapForChain use amountOutMin 0 only inside .staticCall (simulation, no money). Exit-side minOut belongs to the EXIT slice (RC-03).
- **Escalation:** ESC-BUY-02
- **Decision card:** OD-15
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-002
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Decide on card OD-15 whether a snipe whose quote fails is skipped (fail closed) or sent unprotected. Separately keep the slippage math in bigint basis points so a fractional percent can never throw into the fail-open catch. Phase 24, after a Phase 23 proof; nothing is changed in Phase 22.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-17 executor), codex / 2026-11-06 / 23a6461

##### AUD-BUY-004: Double-buy race: the already-sniped check runs many awaits before the row is written and is never repeated inside the nonce lock, so two concurrent handlers for one token both buy

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / OVERSPEND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C07 (nonce management), C15 (TOCTOU)
- **Research candidates:** RC-04 (research suggested S1)
- **Severity rationale:** S1, equal to the research suggestion. The check-then-act gap and the concurrent dispatch sources are visible in code; a double buy spends twice the configured amount on one token (OVERSPEND), and the second position is then mis-linked (AUD-BUY-020).
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`, `src/telegramListener.ts`, `src/alphaDrop.ts`, `src/utils/db.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:881-885@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 dedup: isTokenSniped is read once at handler start
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1210-1214@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 dedup: same read
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:341-347@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - isTokenSniped = SELECT 1 FROM trades WHERE token=? AND chain=? — true only once a row exists
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1127@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 row is inserted only after submitBuyTx returned (many awaits after the check)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1451@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 row is inserted only after submit
  - code: `src/bot.ts:263-268@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - submitBuyTx serializes submits through withNonceLock but nothing re-checks isTokenSniped inside the lock: the second handler waits for the lock, then buys again
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1225@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 handler awaits waitForLiquidity (up to 30 s) before its buy, widening the window against a V2 handler for the same token

  - code: `src/alphaDrop.ts:47@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - same for V3

##### AUD-BUY-008: DEX WebSocket reconnect: replaced providers are not destroyed, one reconnect loop per DEX races on ctx.wsProvider, no backfill, no heartbeat, and dashboard restart stacks a second close handler that later doubles every event

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / OVERSPEND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill), C12 (timer leaks)
- **Research candidates:** RC-20 (research suggested S2)
- **Severity rationale:** Graded S1, above the research suggestion (S2, "S1 if it breaks anti-rug's consumer"). Reason: besides the S2 robustness defects (leaks, missed events, silent half-open socket), the code shows a path to a double buy: after a dashboard stop/start the raw socket carries two close handlers for one DEX; the next disconnect runs two reconnect loops, each subscribing the same listener on its own new provider, so every PairCreated reaches two concurrent handlers, which AUD-BUY-004 lets both buy. Status candidate until a Phase 23 run shows the duplicate dispatch. The anti-rug interaction (shared ctx.wsProvider) is RC-13, owned by the ANTIRUG slice.
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`, `src/utils/provider.ts`, `src/api/routes/chains.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1549-1576@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 reconnect: removeWsProvider, then a while(true) loop creating new WebSocketProvider (:1561), assigning ctx.wsProvider (:1562), re-subscribing, adding a close handler on the new socket (:1568)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1590-1618@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 reconnect: same shape
  - code: `src/utils/provider.ts:46-51@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - removeWsProvider destroys only the provider cached in the map; providers created at bot.ts:1561/:1603 are never put in the map, so after the first reconnect nothing destroys the replaced provider
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1576@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - one close handler is added per DEX on the same raw socket: N DEXes on a chain = N independent reconnect loops, last writer wins ctx.wsProvider
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1557@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - while(true) has no shutdown check
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1836-1845@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - onRestart calls startDexListener again for every DEX, which adds another close handler on the still-open socket
  - code: `src/api/routes/chains.ts:140-142@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - dashboard stop removes provider listeners but not the raw-socket close handlers
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1561-1569@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): DEX reconnects never backfill events missed during disconnection
- **Sibling sites checked:** V2 and V3 reconnect loops both checked (identical shape). provider.ts getWsProvider/removeWsProvider read. onRestart (:1808-1852) and the dashboard stop/start routes (chains.ts:121-190) read for listener stacking. No PairCreated/PoolCreated backfill exists anywhere in bot.ts (searched queryFilter: only the HTTP pollers use it). No ping/heartbeat in the DEX listener path. The anti-rug detector has its own reconnect (detector.ts ~918-926, ANTIRUG slice, RC-13); not edited here.
- **Escalation:** ESC-BUY-02
- **Decision card:** OD-11
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-004, AUD-BUY-011, AUD-ANTIRUG-001
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Fix together with RC-13 under card OD-11 (one per-chain WebSocket owner that notifies subscribers, destroys what it replaces, backfills the gap, detects half-open sockets and stops on shutdown); make listener registration idempotent so restart cannot stack handlers. Phase 24; nothing is changed in Phase 22.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-17 executor), codex / 2026-11-06 / 23a6461

##### AUD-BUY-015: The V3 minimum-liquidity check only proves the quoter did not revert, which an exact-input quote does not do on thin liquidity, so it does not enforce the threshold

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** none
- **Severity rationale:** S1 (raised from S2 by the 22-28 re-grade of codex-BUY-12, read at the base). checkMinLiquidity treats "quoteExactInputSingle(amountIn = threshold) did not revert" as proof of depth. An exact-input quote with no price limit returns what the pool could fill and does not revert (QuoterV2 only reverts when nothing fills), so every V3 pool with any active liquidity passes the gate on an ordinary condition. The earlier S2 reasoning named two bounds that do not hold: minOut is derived from the same quote at the same depth, and the honeypot roundtrip measures tax against the quote at trade size, so neither limits how thin the pool is. A configured capital risk limit is therefore bypassed on every V3 snipe: S1, candidate until a Phase 23 fork run shows a sub-threshold pool pass the gate. codex-BUY-13 (V2 hardcodes 1 native) is a sibling recorded here; on its own it would grade S3 because defaults are at or below 1 native on every chain. See AUD-BUY-033 for the loss the partial fill causes.

##### AUD-BUY-033: A V3 snipe sends the whole amount as ETH value and never refunds it: if the pool can only fill part of the buy, the unspent ETH stays inside the swap router, where anyone can take it

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / LOSS / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** C04 (slippage/minOut)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 LOSS, candidate until a Phase 23 fork test shows it on a real pool. Mechanism (standard, documented Uniswap behaviour, not provable from this repository since the router and pool contracts are not vendored): the V3 pool swap stops when it reaches the price limit (here the extreme bound) and charges only the input it consumed; SwapRouter02 wraps only that amount and leaves the rest of msg.value in the router; refundETH on the router is public and sends the router balance to its caller. So when a pool cannot absorb the whole snipe, the bot pays the unspent part and any sweeper can take it. The buy still passes minOut (the quote reflects the same partial fill). AUD-BUY-015 means a thin pool is not refused, and an attacker can build a pool to be exactly that thin, so the condition is plausible on V3 snipes rather than exotic. Loss is capped by the snipe amount per position, which is why it is S1 and not S0 (it needs a pool thinner than the snipe size).
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`, `src/utils/abis.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1381-1392@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 snipe: exactInputSingle with amountIn = the snipe amount, sqrtPriceLimitX96 0 (no price limit), recipient the wallet
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1431-1437@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - The tx sent is multicall(deadline, [swapData]) with value = amountIn; the only call in the multicall is the swap
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1362-1377@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - minOut = quote minus slippage; the quote is computed at the same amount and reflects the same partial fill, so a partial fill still satisfies amountOutMinimum
  - code: `src/utils/abis.ts:68-71@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - The V3 router ABI has only exactInputSingle and multicall: refundETH is not available to the bot
  - command: `git grep -n -E "refundETH|unwrapWETH9|sweepToken" 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src contracts` - One line of output, and it is a comment: contracts/honeypot/HoneypotChecker.sol:383 mentions unwrapWETH9 in a comment. That is the only hit; no code in src/ or contracts/ calls the router refund, so unspent ETH is never recovered
  - code: `contracts/honeypot/HoneypotChecker.sol:298-325@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - The honeypot checker also buys through exactInputSingle{value:amountIn} with the same shape; it records received tokens and tax, not unspent ETH, so the gate cannot see this
- **Sibling sites checked:** V2 snipe path (bot.ts:1100-1110): swapExactETHForTokens spends the whole msg.value, no leftover. Deliberate public buy (bot.ts:747-748): V2 FoT variant, same. V3 sell path (exitEngine.ts:375-400): sends tokens, no ETH value. Dashboard and scripts: none send V3 ETH value. The only site with a value-bearing V3 multicall is bot.ts:1436, and it has no refund call in the batch.
- **Escalation:** ESC-BUY-05
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-015
- **Tags:** capital, d-stop-the-line
- **Traces:**
  - A V3 pool whose liquidity above the current price can absorb less than the snipe amount: checkMinLiquidity passes (quoter does not revert on a thin pool; AUD-BUY-015), honeypot roundtrip passes (buy, sell and tax are read against the quote at the same size), minOut is set from a quote that already reflects the partial fill, multicall(deadline, [exactInputSingle]) is sent with value = the full snipe amount, the pool swaps until it reaches the price limit and charges only the input it took; the router wraps only that amount, the remaining ETH sits in the router; the next caller of refundETH collects it -> The position is opened for less than was paid; the unspent ETH is lost to whoever sweeps the router first.
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24: add refundETH to the snipe multicall, or wrap only the amount the quote says will be consumed and revert if less than the full amount is taken, and treat a partial fill as a skipped snipe. Prove the behaviour first on a Phase 23 fork with a deliberately thin single-sided V3 pool. No behaviour trade-off, so this needs no decision card; nothing is changed in Phase 22.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-28 consolidation executor, found while re-grading codex-BUY-12) / 2026-11-09 / 23a6461

##### AUD-CENSUS-002: D-NONCE-AUTHORITY-ALL violation candidate: src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:277 sends a real approve of the whole token balance with the bot wallet and no withNonceLock (simulateSell); the function is exported and imported by src/bot.ts:17 but has no caller at the base (duplicate of AUD-BUY-007)

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S1 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** CENSUS / independent
- **Classes:** C07 (nonce management), C06 (approvals)
- **Severity rationale:** S1 by the 22-26 census rule: every src transaction-signing site that is not proven to run under the nonce lock is a D-NONCE-AUTHORITY-ALL violation candidate graded S1 or above. If it runs while the bot is trading, the approve can take the same nonce as a buy or sell of the same wallet; one of the two is then dropped or replaced, and a dropped sell leaves the position held (STRAND). Mitigating fact, recorded honestly: the site is unreachable at the base (no caller; imported but never called; tests mock it), which is why AUD-BUY-007 graded the same defect S2 as a re-introduction hazard. Merge: duplicate of AUD-BUY-007 (same site, same defect); the canonical must carry the higher severity, the union of evidence and this escalation at consolidation (22-28) unless the operator rules otherwise at ESC-CENSUS-01. Consolidated at 22-28: AUD-BUY-007 is the canonical entry and carries S1 and ESC-CENSUS-01.

- **Evidence:**

  - command: `PATH=/c/Users/jackc/AppData/Local/nvm/v22.16.0:$PATH node node_modules/ts-node/dist/bin.js .planning/audit/tools/signing-census.ts --root <git archive 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src scripts tsconfig.json tsconfig.bot.json package.json, node_modules = per-entry junctions> --sha 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 --out .planning/audit/census/signing-sites.json --manual .planning/audit/census/manual-inventory.json` - census site SIG-049: kind tx-signing, api contract.approve, runner signer (traced to :274), mutability nonpayable (ERC20_ABI src/utils/abis.ts:31), lock_status unlocked: "simulateSell is exported with no in-program caller (entry: an importer can call it outside any lock)"
