  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1735-1742@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - probeAmount is the wallet token balance (token base units)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1750-1764@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - quotedRatioBps = quotedOut * 10000 / probeAmount, where quotedOut is WETH base units; signal 3 trips when the ratio is below 50 %
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1533-1546@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 Burn and Collect destination = topics[1], the owner field
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1698-1704@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - owner checked against allowlistV3 through isAddressAllowlisted (allowlist.ts:72-83)
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:515-579@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the V3 allowlists hold locker contracts (UNCX V3 Locker, TeamFinance proxy); the comment at :523-527 says the locker holds NonfungiblePositionManager NFTs
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1685-1696@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - signal 1 on V3 uses pool.liquidity(), the active liquidity at the current tick
  - code: `test/fork/fixtures/rugs/eth-v3-CANDIDATE.json:24@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the V3 rug fixture is not block-pinned ("Block-pin pending"), so V3 detection has never been replayed against a real rug
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1754-1764@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): V3 slippage compares raw amounts of different assets
- **Sibling sites checked:** V2 path read for the same faults: signal 3 there compares each reserve with its own baseline (detector.ts:1618-1631, same units), so no unit mismatch; but either reserve under 50 % also trips on a 4x price move in either direction (constant product), which makes it redundant with signal 1 rather than wrong. V2 signal 2 uses the Burn or Transfer to field (:1521-1532); a lock is an LP Transfer to the locker, which does not reduce totalSupply, so signal 1 does not trip on it anyway. raceTelemetry.ts:206-243 has a V3 quote too but is dead code (AUD-ANTIRUG-014).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-49
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-001, AUD-EXIT-003
- **Tags:** capital
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] (1) Unit mismatch: for an 18-decimal token worth less than 0.5 WETH per whole token, the ratio is below 50 % with no slippage at all, so signal 3 is always tripped and carries no information about sell feasibility. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1750-1764@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [candidate] (2) For liquidity managed through the NonfungiblePositionManager (the lockers hold such NFTs, chainRegistry.ts:523-527), the pool emits Burn and Collect with owner = the position manager, not the locker, so the V3 allowlist cannot match those events and signal 2 always trips; locking itself is an NFT transfer that emits no pool log. (evidence: src/chainRegistry.ts:523-527@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1533-1546@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [candidate] (3) Active liquidity also falls when the price leaves a concentrated range. A later fee Collect then meets signal 1, and with signals 2 and 3 always tripped the bot fires an emergency exit with minOut 0 (AUD-EXIT-001) and the anti-rug gas multiplier on a pool that was not rugged. (evidence: src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1685-1696@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/anti-rug/detector.ts:2054-2071@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Make signal 3 a real sell-impact check in one unit (the quote for the held amount compared with its value at the pool price), and decide what locked means on V3 (follow NFT transfers to lockers, or drop signal 2 on V3 and document it). Card ANTIRUG-03. Phase 24, with a fork replay of a real V3 rug and of a concentrated-range pool that is not a rug.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-007: Without a WebSocket URL every anti-rug (re)arm starts another HTTP poller that is never stopped, and each poller is a setInterval(async) with no in-flight guard, so every rug log is dispatched once per poller and slow ticks can repeat a block range

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C12 (timer leaks), C14 (idempotent exits), C10 (WS reconnect/backfill)
- **Severity rationale:** S2. With N registrations on a chain without a WS URL, each rug log is evaluated N times and N confirm gates fire. The sell lock keeps the sells serialized, so there is no double sell, but each extra dispatch is a circuit-breaker count (AUD-ANTIRUG-003 carries the S1 consequence) and RPC load grows with every buy until rate limits make every poll fail. Linked to the RC-21 entry AUD-EXIT-005.
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:587-601@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - with no ctx.wsProvider, every startChainAntiRugListener call runs startHttpPollingAntiRug
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1261-1317@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - setInterval(async) with its own closure lastBlock; the handle is not stored and never cleared
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:447@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - every registration re-arms
  - code: `src/bot.ts:2120-2144@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - resume arms once per position and once more per chain
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1263-1300@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - lastBlock advances only after every dispatch of the tick has been awaited; a tick longer than 2 s overlaps the next, which reads the same lastBlock
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1242-1249@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - healthState connected is set once at start, before any poll succeeds; poll errors only log (:1307-1316)
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:587-600@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Every HTTP-mode registration starts another polling interval
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1261-1264@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Async HTTP polling cycles overlap and replay the same events
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every setInterval in the slice: detector.ts:782 (heartbeat, cleared on close and replaced on re-arm) and :1261 (this poller, never cleared). RC-21 owns the setInterval(async) overlap pattern; the exit-engine sites are AUD-EXIT-005 and the bot.ts factory pollers are AUD-BUY-011 (start adds a second poller); this is the anti-rug site named in RC-21 (detector.ts:1261).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-005, AUD-ANTIRUG-003, AUD-BUY-011
- **Tags:** none
- **Recommendation:** One poller per chain (store the handle, start it once, stop it on shutdown), an in-flight guard per tick, and a health state that reflects the last successful poll. No behaviour decision needed; Phase 24 together with the ANTIRUG-01 dedupe, because the breaker count depends on it.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

  - code: `src/config.ts:83@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - documented rule: flip to true ONLY after a 7-day dry run with 0 confirmed false positives; the false-positive review is not in code
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every reader and writer of antirug_dry_run_started (db.ts:186-188 column, :702-709 statements; detector.ts:585; preflight.ts:640-655). No dashboard or Telegram path flips it at runtime.

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-010: Circuit-breaker state lives only in module memory: a restart silently clears a trip and its acknowledgement trail, so the protection against a misfiring detector is lost on every restart

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C13 (SQLite transaction boundaries and crash consistency), C14 (idempotent exits)
- **Severity rationale:** S2. The breaker exists to stop a misfiring detector from selling one position after another (exitTrigger.ts:32-35). After a restart the same code and config run with an empty history, so up to `threshold` more emergency sells at minOut 0 can go out before it trips again. Bounded per position; live mode only. The opposite effect (a restart re-enables anti-rug after a trip caused by AUD-ANTIRUG-003) is today the only reset besides the dashboard.
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts`, `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts`, `src/api/routes/antiRug.ts`, `src/utils/db.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:72-83@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - triggerHistory, trippedChains and recentTriggerEvents are in-memory Map/Set; the module has no DB read or write
  - code: `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:5-7@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - header: exits stay disabled "until the operator resets the breaker through the dashboard (Plan 19-06) or CLI"
  - code: `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:183-203@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a real reset logs resetByOperatorTs and broadcasts cb_reset; a restart produces neither
  - code: `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:30-36@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the ring buffer exists so the reset modal shows exactly the events that tripped the breaker
  - code: `src/api/routes/antiRug.ts:59-67@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the reset route refuses unless tripped; :88 serves the ring buffer
  - code: `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:107-127@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - evaluation filters in-memory timestamps; after a restart the history is empty
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:691-696@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - contrast: the dry-run start stamp is persisted precisely so that a restart does not reset it
  - command: `git grep -n resetCircuitBreaker 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src scripts` - only api/routes/antiRug.ts calls it; the CLI reset named in the header does not exist
  - code: `src/anti-rug/circuitBreaker.ts:73-83@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Restarting the process clears a manual-reset-only breaker
- **Sibling sites checked:** All module-local anti-rug state: circuitBreaker.ts:73-83 and detector.ts:192 (positionRegistry), :197 (chainState), :247 (pendingV3Burn). The registry and pending maps are rebuilt at boot by resumeAntiRugMonitoring (bot.ts:1989-2145); the breaker is not. A duplicate module load would split all of these maps (RC-17, owned by the TX slice, noted here only). _resetRegistryForTesting (detector.ts:301) and _resetForTesting (circuitBreaker.ts:228) have no production caller (git grep at the base).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-50
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-003, AUD-ANTIRUG-002, AUD-BUY-005
- **Tags:** capital
- **Traces:**
  - Restart after the circuit breaker tripped (is the reset intended, or a lost protection?): Live mode. The threshold-th incrementCircuitBreaker on a chain (circuitBreaker.ts:110-128) adds the chain to trippedChains, logs fatal, broadcasts cb_tripped and sends [ANTI-RUG HALTED] (:130-161)., Every later trigger on that chain returns at exitTrigger.ts:221-232 with a log.fatal only., The bot exits: an operator restart, a SIGINT, or a crash such as AUD-ANTIRUG-002 or AUD-BUY-005. Nothing in circuitBreaker.ts is written to disk., Boot: module load creates empty maps (circuitBreaker.ts:73-83). resumeAntiRugMonitoring re-registers positions and arms the listeners (bot.ts:2074-2144). isCircuitBreakerTripped returns false for every chain (:171-173); getRecentTriggers returns [] (:215-218), so the dashboard has no halted state and the reset modal has nothing to acknowledge. Nothing at boot reports that a chain had tripped., The next trigger on that chain sends a live exit. The breaker trips again only after `threshold` new triggers, and the threshold-th exit has already been sent by then (increment after the exit, exitTrigger.ts:312-319). -> Judgment: the restart reset loses a protection the design relies on; it is not an intended reset. Evidence: the header promises the trip lasts "until the operator resets" it (circuitBreaker.ts:5-7); the acknowledgement trail is built for that reset (ring buffer :30-36, reset log and broadcast :183-203, reset route and modal data antiRug.ts:59-67, :88); and the codebase persists gate state it means to survive restarts (db.ts:691-696). A restart is not an acknowledgement: it can follow a crash, and nothing tells the operator after boot that a chain had tripped.
- **Recommendation:** Persist the trip (chain_state or its own table), restore it at boot, require the dashboard reset to clear it, and alert at boot when a chain starts tripped; either build the CLI reset the header promises or remove the claim. Card ANTIRUG-04. Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-017: Anti-rug numeric settings: an empty LP_REMOVAL_PCT or CONFIRM_BLOCKS silently becomes 0, GAS_MULTIPLIER has no upper bound, and WATCHDOG_BUDGET_MS turns a unit suffix into a tiny number

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C02 (|| vs ?? with 0n/''/0), C18 (env validation), C16 (gas/fee ceilings)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: needs an operator configuration mistake, but the mistakes are ordinary (an empty line in .env, a unit suffix) and the effects are silent: emergency sells on any LP movement, no confirmation, an unbounded gas bid, or every exit reported failed. Bounded per position.
- **Files:** `src/chainRegistry.ts`, `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:726-745@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - process.env[KEY] ?? default keeps an empty string; Number("") is 0, accepted by the 0..100 check, so signal 1 trips on any LP decrease
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:746-765@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - CONFIRM_BLOCKS "" becomes 0, accepted, so dispatch is immediate with no confirmation
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:806-824@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - GAS_MULTIPLIER must be >= 1.0 and has no upper bound
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:786-805@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the breaker window must be an integer number of hours
  - code: `src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:77-81@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - parseInt("60s") is 60, so WATCHDOG_BUDGET_MS=60s gives a 60 ms budget: every live anti-rug exit is reported failed at once and counted by the breaker while the sell runs unbounded in the background
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every anti-rug env read: chainRegistry.ts:721-861 (LIVE_EXECUTE, LP_REMOVAL_PCT, CONFIRM_BLOCKS, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIGGERS, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_WINDOW_HOURS, GAS_MULTIPLIER, BACKFILL_CAP_BLOCKS, MAX_BACKFILL_BLOCKS), :881-932 (ALLOWLIST_EXTRA, _V2, _V3), exitTrigger.ts:78 (WATCHDOG_BUDGET_MS, also read by the worker watchdog in bot.ts, BUY row TH-BUY-14). Empty TRIGGERS, WINDOW, GAS_MULTIPLIER, BACKFILL_CAP and MAX_BACKFILL become 0 and fail loud (exit 1), which is correct.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-53
- **Related:** AUD-ANTIRUG-003
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Treat an empty value as unset or reject it; reject 0 for LP_REMOVAL_PCT; cap GAS_MULTIPLIER; parse durations strictly (Number and an integer check) and fail loud. How strict is card ANTIRUG-07. Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-19 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-API-004: Section C SC-07: dashboard force-sell and emergency-sell run inside the HTTP request with no time bound, no idempotency and no progress; a double submit starts a second sell loop, and every "false" from executeFullSell is reported as "sell already in progress / lock held"

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / independent
- **Classes:** C07 (nonce management), C14 (idempotent exits), C15 (TOCTOU)
- **Severity rationale:** S2 LOSS: in an emergency the sell-all can be slow (routine attempt budget per position, one after another) and can stall entirely behind one position whose submit never settles, with no progress shown and no answer to the browser, and its report can say 'lock held / in progress' for positions that actually failed. The tokens are not sold twice (sell lock and balanceOf), so this is bounded; the never-settling wait and the head-of-line block that turn it into a stall are already S1 entries (RC-10 on ESC-PRE-02, RC-11 AUD-TX-003 on ESC-TX-01) and are not double-counted here.
- **Files:** `src/api/routes/controls.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/bot.ts`, `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx`, `dashboard/src/pages/Overview.tsx`, `dashboard/src/components/ConfirmDialog.tsx`

  - code: `src/api/routes/controls.ts:59-119@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - force-sell awaits one executeFullSell inside the request
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:453-456@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - privateAttemptBudget: the dashboard reason 'urgency-market-sell' is routine, so each position gets MEV_SELL_FALLBACK_ATTEMPTS (default 2) private attempts plus the reconcile window before the public fallback; only 'anti-rug' gets 1
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1876-1879@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the exit watchdog bounds only the ExitWorker submit; the dashboard calls executeFullSell directly and has no bound (RC-10 wait() with no timeout inside withNonceLock, AUD-EXIT-009 / AUD-TX-002, can park it forever)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1184-1199@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the ExitWorker is the serial sell drainer; the dashboard sells bypass it and contend with it and with buys on withNonceLock at each signing site (:871, :874, :909)
  - code: `src/api/routes/controls.ts:106-112@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - force-sell: success false -> 409 'Sell already in progress for this position'
  - code: `src/api/routes/controls.ts:179-189@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - emergency-sell: success false -> failure 'Sell lock held by another operation'
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:824-835@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - executeFullSell returns false for a routine-paused position (:824-830) and for a held sell lock (:832-835)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:876-879@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - and for an unknown dex type
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1022-1037@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - and for a V3 position whose private sell did not land
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1110-1111@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - and after a "successful" sell that left the position still held; also :995-996 (inconclusive) and :1163-1167 (catch, still held)
  - code: `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:85-111@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - Emergency Sell All closes its dialog at once (:86), shows no in-flight state and leaves the button enabled (:121-126), so a second click can start a second request while the first runs
  - code: `dashboard/src/components/ConfirmDialog.tsx:94-102@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the Force Sell confirm button stays enabled while its request is pending (disabled only for the CONFIRM text check)
- **Sibling sites checked:** Both money-moving dashboard routes (force-sell, emergency-sell) and their callers in the dashboard (Overview.tsx:75-99, ChainControls.tsx:85-111); the other POST routes (pause, resume, chain stop/start, circuit-breaker reset) are idempotent or refuse a repeat (stop/start answer 400 on a repeat; CB reset answers 409 when not tripped). Duplicate execution of the same tokens is prevented by the per-position sell lock (exitEngine.ts:832-835) and the balanceOf checks (:839-846, :1002-1015): a second loop that reaches an already-sold position finds a zero balance and tears down, it does not sell twice; a still-held failed position gets one more real attempt, which increments exit_failure_count (exitEngine.ts:700) towards the routine pause (AUD-EXIT-008). Clearing the exit timers before the sell is known to run (controls.ts:92, :167) is AUD-EXIT-007 and is linked, not repeated. The 409 mapping for the routine-paused case specifically is AUD-EXIT-008; this entry records that every false is mapped that way. Neither route pauses buying (AUD-API-015).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-65
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-008, AUD-EXIT-007, AUD-EXIT-009, AUD-TX-002, AUD-TX-003, AUD-API-001, AUD-API-015
- **Tags:** none
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] emergency-sell is serial and unbounded inside the HTTP request; one stuck position delays or blocks every later one and the browser gets no answer (evidence: src/api/routes/controls.ts:140-199@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/bot.ts:1876-1879@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:453-456@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] no idempotency: a second POST runs a second loop over a list captured at its own start; locked positions are reported as failures while being sold, finished ones are retried (zero balance, harmless) and failed-held ones get another attempt (evidence: src/api/routes/controls.ts:126@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/routes/controls.ts:179-189@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:832-846@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:85-126@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] every false from executeFullSell (paused, unknown dex, V3 not landed, still held after failure) is reported as 'in progress' / 'lock held' (evidence: src/api/routes/controls.ts:106-112@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/routes/controls.ts:179-189@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:824-835@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:876-879@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:1022-1037@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:1110-1111@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] dashboard sells bypass the ExitWorker queue and wait on withNonceLock behind any buy or sell holding it (evidence: src/exitEngine.ts:1184-1199@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:871@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/exitEngine.ts:909@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Run a dashboard sell as a server-side job with an id: refuse a second emergency job while one runs (idempotency), stream or poll per-position progress, bound each position by a wall-clock budget (as the worker watchdog does), and report the real reason for every position not sold. Disable the confirm buttons while a request is pending. Which reason and speed an operator sell should use is card EXIT-07 (AUD-EXIT-008); whether emergency sell should pause buying first is card API-02. Phase 24 with the RC-10/RC-11 fixes.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-22 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-API-005: CORS: "same origin" is derived from the request's own Host header with no list of expected host names, so a DNS-rebinding page passes the CORS gate and can read /health and send unlimited login guesses from the operator's browser

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / independent
- **Classes:** C19 (API auth/CORS)
- **Severity rationale:** S2 EXPOSURE: the trust boundary (only the dashboard itself may drive the API from a browser) can be crossed by any web page the operator visits while the bot runs, without network access to the bot: the page reads /health (positions, exposure, 24 h P&L) and can guess the key at browser speed with no limit. Taking control (emergency-sell, resume, chain stop, CB reset) needs a correct key; preflight refuses keys shorter than 16 characters (docs/operations/going-live.md:147), so a random key makes that impractical, while a human-chosen 16-character phrase may not. Not S1 because control needs the key; the code half is proven on loopback, the browser half (rebinding) is not run here.
- **Files:** `src/api/server.ts`, `src/api/middleware/auth.ts`, `src/api/routes/health.ts`, `dashboard/vite.config.ts`, `.env.example`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:97-144@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - per-request cors(): Origin absent -> allow (:122); Origin whose URL.origin equals scheme://<request Host header> -> allow (:101, :113, :126); allowlist (:133); otherwise 403 (:138-140)
  - command: `node cors-host.js <snapshot>/src/api/server.ts <repo>/node_modules (scratch folder outside the repo (Node 22.16.0 by absolute path; no src/ import, no .env, no data/, no live DB; loopback 127.0.0.1 only; audit-base snapshot from slice-files.ts --snapshot API,DASH); the exact text of server.ts:97-144 transpiled with the repo typescript and mounted in a bare express 5.2.1 app with cors 2.8.6, empty env = shipped defaults)` - output: Host=evil.example:8080 + Origin=http://evil.example:8080 -> 200 {"reachedRoute":true}; Host=127.0.0.1:8080 + Origin=http://evil.example:8080 -> 403; Host=127.0.0.1:8080 + Origin=http://127.0.0.1:3000 -> 403; no Origin -> 200
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:148-152@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - /health and /api/auth/login are mounted before authMiddleware (no session needed)
  - code: `src/api/middleware/auth.ts:40-59@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - loginHandler: no attempt counter, delay or lockout; a failure only logs warn (:56)
  - code: `src/api/middleware/auth.ts:61-71@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a correct key sets the session cookie for whatever host the browser used, so a rebinding hostname gets its own valid session, which then passes authMiddleware (:101-110) for every control route
  - code: `dashboard/vite.config.ts:9-16@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the dev proxy forwards without changeOrigin, so Host stays localhost:5173 and the same Host-match lets dev requests through; any Host allowlist must keep this working
  - code: `.env.example:75-77@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - default bind 127.0.0.1; 0.0.0.0 documented for remote access
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every request-origin decision in src/api: server.ts:97-144 (HTTP, this finding); ws/handler.ts:37-66 (WebSocket upgrade, no Origin check at all, AUD-API-006); no Host allowlist anywhere (grep 'host' over the snapshot: server.ts:101/:113/:208, handler.ts:43). Express trust proxy is off and X-Forwarded-Proto is honoured only with DASHBOARD_TRUST_PROXY_PROTO=1 (server.ts:99, :105-108), correct. A rebinding hostname does not receive the existing 127.0.0.1/localhost session cookie, so an already logged-in operator session is not reused (mitigating). Login without rate limit is also listed under authentication handling (AUD-API-007); /health content is AUD-API-010.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-66
- **Related:** AUD-API-006, AUD-API-007, AUD-API-010
- **Tags:** none
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] Any request whose Origin equals its own Host passes the CORS gate; there is no host allowlist (evidence: src/api/server.ts:100-144@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, node cors-host.js (loopback repro, output in evidence))
  - [candidate] A DNS-rebinding page can therefore read /health and POST login guesses without limit from the operator's browser (evidence: src/api/server.ts:148-152@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/middleware/auth.ts:40-59@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [candidate] A correct guess yields a session for the rebinding hostname that passes authMiddleware on every control route (evidence: src/api/middleware/auth.ts:61-71@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/middleware/auth.ts:101-110@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Check the Host header against an allowlist (DASHBOARD_HOST:PORT, 127.0.0.1/localhost/[::1] on the configured port, any configured public name, the vite dev host) before CORS and reject others (421/403), and derive "same origin" from that configured list rather than from Host; add login rate limiting with backoff. Card API-03 (it changes which requests are accepted). Phase 29 unless the dashboard is exposed beyond 127.0.0.1 earlier.

- **Related:** AUD-API-008, AUD-ANTIRUG-002, AUD-API-007

##### AUD-BUY-012: Dead checkHoneypot passes the wallet private key as the swap recipient address; ethers would put the value into an error message that the function logs

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** C17 (key handling)
- **Severity rationale:** S2, latent: the function has no caller at the base, so no key has been exposed by it. If it were ever called and the honeypot API failed, the fallback staticCall resolves the recipient argument: a 64-hex string is not an address, so ethers tries ENS, the name does not resolve, and ethers raises UNCONFIGURED_NAME with value=<the key> in the message, which line 47-48 logs at warn level. Not escalated: no secret value was found or exposed (PROTOCOL immediate tier covers a found non-public secret), and nothing was printed during this audit.
- **Files:** `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:37-44@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - router.swapExactETHForTokens.staticCall(0, path, CONFIG.walletPrivateKey, deadline, {value}) — the key is passed where the recipient address belongs
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:46-48@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the error message is logged: log.warn({ error: fallbackMessage })
  - code: `src/config.ts:271@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - CONFIG.walletPrivateKey is the PRIVATE_KEY env value
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/address/checks.js:103-109` - resolveAddress: a string that is not 0x+40 hex goes to resolver.resolveName (ENS)
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/address/checks.js:61` - checkAddress: an unresolved string raises UNCONFIGURED_NAME with info {value: target}
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/utils/errors.js:100-124` - makeError appends every info key as key=value to the message
  - command: `git grep -n -F "checkHoneypot(" 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src scripts` - only the definition at tokenSafety.ts:19: no caller
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:38-48@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Legacy honeypot fallback can write the wallet private key to logs
- **Sibling sites checked:** All key references in the slice: only tokenSafety.ts:41. Signers elsewhere in the slice come from ctx.wallet (getWallet, src/utils/provider.ts:59, DB/infra slice). The other legacy single-chain helpers are dead too (AUD-BUY-026). Test files only mock checkHoneypot (vi.fn), they do not call it.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-007, AUD-BUY-026
- **Tags:** key-handling, latent, dead-code
- **Recommendation:** Delete checkHoneypot (no caller, so no behaviour change), and add a static check that CONFIG.walletPrivateKey is referenced only where the Wallet is constructed. Phase 29 hygiene, or earlier if Phase 24 touches tokenSafety.ts.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-17 executor), codex / 2026-11-06 / 23a6461

##### AUD-BUY-013: Two token-screening gates can never fire: the anti-bot selector scan matches "0x"-prefixed selectors that cannot occur inside bytecode, and the blocklist is always empty

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** none
- **Severity rationale:** S2: two gates in the buy path are no-ops, so the alert line "Blacklist Function: No" is printed for every token and the "known bad token" gate only rejects addresses with no code. The bytecode mutability scan (honeypot/bytecodeScan.ts) independently covers setBlacklist-style selectors, which bounds the effect.
- **Files:** `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts`, `src/utils/blocklist.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:331-340@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - isBlacklistedTokenForChain: bytecode.includes("0xdd62ed3e") etc. The bytecode string has a single "0x" at its start, so the test is false for every real token (true only on an RPC error)
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:332@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - 0xdd62ed3e is allowance(address,address), which every ERC20 has; simply stripping the prefix would make the gate block every token
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:56-61@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - legacy twin isBlacklistedToken: same defect (dead)
  - code: `src/utils/blocklist.ts:5-8@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - BLOCKLIST tokens/pairs are empty Sets; nothing in src adds to them
  - code: `src/bot.ts:889-899@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 blocklist checks against the empty sets
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:433-451@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - isKnownBadTokenForChain: only "no code" or the empty blocklist; the creator check is skipped
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1023@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - alert prints "Blacklist Function" from the no-op gate
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:332-335@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): Blacklist selector scanning includes an impossible interior 0x prefix
- **Sibling sites checked:** Both blacklist scanners (tokenSafety.ts:56-61 legacy, :331-340 chain) and every BLOCKLIST use (bot.ts:889, :895, :1218; tokenSafety.ts:204, :441) checked; git grep found no code that adds to BLOCKLIST. The bytecode scan is AUD-BUY-014.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-30
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-009, AUD-BUY-014
- **Tags:** safety-gate
- **Recommendation:** Either make each gate test what it is named for (strip the prefix, drop the allowance selector, give the blocklist a data source) or remove it and stop printing its result. Fixing it would block more tokens, so it is a behaviour change on card BUY-05. Phase 24 or 29 per the card.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-17 executor), codex / 2026-11-06 / 23a6461

- **Related:** AUD-BUY-002, AUD-BUY-004
- **Tags:** section-c:SC-06

##### AUD-DB-006: RC-25 no newer-schema guard: importing db.ts migrates and then writes user_version = 7 unconditionally, so an older build opened on a newer database silently downgrades its version, and every import (including the read-only preflight command) writes the live database

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** DB / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C13 (SQLite transaction boundaries and crash consistency)
- **Research candidates:** RC-25 (research suggested S2)
- **Severity rationale:** S2, equal to the research suggestion. Effects of an older build on a newer database: user_version drops to 7, so the next newer boot re-runs its migrations (a non-idempotent ALTER then fails and the bot cannot boot); a removed column makes a prepared statement fail at import (refuses to start); a newly required column makes the buy-row insert fail after the buy has landed (stranded position). Needs a rollback to an older build after a schema change, which D-ROLLBACK makes plausible but not routine. Mitigated by the 22-09 rail; status stays confirmed until 22-29 verifies it.
- **Files:** `src/utils/db.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:27-30@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 7; version read with no upper-bound check
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - db.pragma(`user_version = ${CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION}`) runs on every import, whatever version was found
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:17-24@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - new Database(DB_PATH) (creates the file if missing), then WAL and synchronous pragmas, all at import
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:303-316@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - normalizeLegacyMainnetRows runs an UPDATE on every import
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:320-709@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - all prepared statements are compiled at import against whatever schema is on disk
  - code: `src/preflight.ts:49@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the preflight module imports './utils/db', so any process that loads preflight opens, migrates and writes the database
- **Sibling sites checked:** The forensic copy showed 40 page-1 header writes with user_version 7 and no row changes, the fingerprint of this import path (AUD-FORENSIC-001, AUD-RAIL-002; linked, not repeated). scripts/preflight.ts and scripts/pause.ts / resume.ts (SCRIPTS slice) load db.ts the same way. The 22-09 rail (D-08, D-24) adds a read-only version probe before any pragma and refuses a CURRENT+1 database; 22-29 re-audits that diff.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-RAIL-002, AUD-FORENSIC-001, AUD-DB-012
- **Tags:** mitigation-planned-22-09
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] user_version is written unconditionally, downgrading a newer database (evidence: src/utils/db.ts:232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] Prepared statements compiled at import assume the schema-7 columns (evidence: src/utils/db.ts:320-323@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/utils/db.ts:505-518@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] Every import of db.ts writes the database (pragma user_version and an UPDATE), including the read-only preflight command (evidence: src/utils/db.ts:232@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/utils/db.ts:315-316@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/preflight.ts:49@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Mitigated by the planned 22-09 rail (read-only user_version probe before any write; refuse version > CURRENT with the file hash unchanged). 22-29 re-audits the db.ts diff; no further behaviour decision.

##### AUD-DB-009: The Telegram bot token is written to the logs on every failed alert: the token is part of the request URL, the axios error is logged whole as err, and its config.url carries the URL (reproduced offline); a token symbol that breaks the Markdown is enough to cause a failure

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** DB / independent
- **Classes:** C17 (key handling), C20 (Telegram trust)
- **Severity rationale:** S2 EXPOSURE, the same class and grade as AUD-TX-014: a credential crosses into the logs under ordinary failures, and an outsider can trigger the failure through a token name. The bot token lets whoever reads the logs send messages as the bot and read the bot chat; it does not move funds.
- **Files:** `src/utils/notifier.ts`, `src/utils/logger.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/notifier.ts:10@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - TELEGRAM_API = `https://api.telegram.org/bot${process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}/sendMessage`
  - code: `src/utils/notifier.ts:43-51@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - axios.post(TELEGRAM_API, ...) and on any error log.warn({ err: error }, 'Telegram alert error')
  - code: `src/utils/notifier.ts:79-87@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - sendCtxAlert: the same
  - code: `src/utils/logger.ts:6-10@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - no redact configuration; pino serializes err with its enumerable properties
  - command: `node tg-log-repro.js (scratch folder outside the repo (Node 22.16.0; no src/ import, no .env, no live DB; loopback 127.0.0.1 only); axios 1.10.0 CJS build and pino 10.3.1 from the repo node_modules with the logger.ts options; fake sentinel token; POST to 127.0.0.1:1)` - output: token present in log line: true; the line carries "url":"http://127.0.0.1:1/bot<fake token>/sendMessage" inside err.config
  - code: `src/utils/notifier.ts:49-50@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Telegram request failures disclose the bot token in logs
- **Sibling sites checked:** Both Telegram send sites in the slice (notifier.ts:44 and :80) use the same URL and the same err logging. Ways a send fails: network errors, Telegram 429, and HTTP 400 when parse_mode Markdown meets an unbalanced * or _ (the deployer-chosen token symbol goes in unescaped, AUD-BUY-022). Where logs go: stdout, persisted when the operator redirects it (the data/*capture*.log files; AUD-TX-014 records that the backup copies passed the D-22 exact-value check, which includes TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN). No axios timeout is set (AUD-EXIT-021).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-57
- **Related:** AUD-TX-014, AUD-BUY-022, AUD-EXIT-021, AUD-DB-008
- **Tags:** credential-exposure
- **Recommendation:** Log only error.message / code / response status for Telegram failures and add logger-level redaction (card TX-04); check persisted logs and rotate the bot token if any contains it.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-21 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

  - code: `src/preflight.ts:974-990@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - preflight(): log.fatal with reason + details, then sendTelegramAlert(`*PREFLIGHT FATAL* [...] ${r.reason}`)

Only preflight() forwards reasons to Telegram (:986-990); the mid-run wallet check reuses checkWalletBalance (bot.ts, BUY slice). Hosted RPC URLs carry the key in the path (.env.example:13, :54).

##### AUD-DB-013: Beyond the unit mix-up, the risk formulas are wrong: each partial sell is charged the full buy cost in the daily-loss sum, exposure subtracts sale proceeds instead of the cost sold (it goes negative on a profitable partial), buy gas is never recorded, and ETH and BNB amounts are added into one total against one cap

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** DB / independent
- **Classes:** C01 (BigInt/Number mixing)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: the double charge makes the breaker trip early (fail-closed direction); the proceeds-based exposure and the cross-currency total let the exposure cap be exceeded by bounded amounts (fail-open direction); buy gas is a small understatement. Bounded effects, so below the S1 of AUD-DB-002.
- **Files:** `src/utils/db.ts`, `src/riskManager.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:441-459@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - one row per sell joined to its buy: s.amount_out - b.amount_in - b.gas_cost - s.gas_cost; with two partial sells and a final sell the buy cost is subtracted three times
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:425-438@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - exposure = amount_in - SUM(partial_sell amount_out): proceeds, not the share of cost sold
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1140@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - buy rows write gasCost: null (also :1464, :782), so buy gas never enters any loss figure
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:425-438@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - no chain filter: BSC amounts (BNB) and ETH/Base/Arbitrum amounts (ETH) are summed into one number compared with MAX_TOTAL_EXPOSURE
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:449@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - join on token + chain + s.timestamp >= b.timestamp: a second buy of the same token joins every earlier sell (same-token rebuys, AUD-EXIT-018)
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:443-449@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): Daily loss subtracts the entire buy cost for every partial sale
- **Sibling sites checked:** getPnLQuery (:351-384) and getPnLChartDataQuery (:463-485) use the same join; api/routes/risk.ts:66 pro-rates the buy cost per event for its chart (API slice), so the dashboard and the breaker compute loss differently. These defects remain after AUD-DB-002 is fixed, so they are a separate entry.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-58
- **Related:** AUD-DB-002, AUD-DB-014, AUD-EXIT-018
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Define realized loss per position (proceeds minus cost of the part sold minus all gas), exposure as remaining cost basis, and keep totals per currency (or convert explicitly). Card DB-01. Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-21 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-DB-015: Two bots with different wallets can share one database (nothing records the wallet on a trade and nothing locks the database file), and on its next start each bot marks the other bot's open positions failed because its own wallet holds none of those tokens, so the owner stops monitoring them after its own restart

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / STRAND / candidate
- **Slice / origin:** DB / independent
- **Classes:** C13 (SQLite transaction boundaries and crash consistency), C15 (TOCTOU)
- **Severity rationale:** S2 STRAND: a deliberate but unsupported setup (one database, two wallets) silently drops the other bot's positions out of restart-resume after a restart of each; candidate because the setup is not used today and the trace is by code reading. Registered because the CONTEXT deferred idea asked for it and the code allows it.
- **Files:** `src/utils/db.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:33-47@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - trades has no wallet column (nor do exit_state, lp_baseline, pause_state, chain_state at :67-190)
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:9-24@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - DB_PATH alone picks the file; WAL + busy_timeout let several processes open it at once; no file lock
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1933-1938@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - restart: for every pending buy, balanceOf(this bot's wallet) === 0 -> updateTradeStatus.run('failed', token, chain)
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:597-604@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the resume scan reads every pending buy regardless of who bought it
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:420-459@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - open-position count, exposure and daily loss are shared totals across both wallets; pause_state is one row for both
- **Sibling sites checked:** Scope boundary: the same-wallet second process is AUD-TX-005 / RC-18, closed by the 22-13 process lock keyed by wallet address; that lock does not see a second bot on a different wallet, so this entry stays separate. How two bots end up on one file: a second process started from the same checkout with PRIVATE_KEY overridden in the shell (dotenv never overrides shell values) or any process with the same absolute DB_PATH. Dedup (isTokenSniped, db.ts:341-347) is shared, which blocks the second bot from buying a token the first one holds. Exit monitors at runtime are in memory per process; the damage lands on the owner's next restart.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-59
- **Related:** AUD-TX-005, AUD-DB-007
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Either record the wallet address on every trade and scope every query by it, or lock the database file for one wallet (a second lock keyed by DB path), or refuse a database whose recorded owner differs. Card DB-02. Phase 24 or 29.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-21 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-DB-021: SQLite runs WAL with synchronous=NORMAL, so a just-written position record can be lost on power loss or OS crash

- **Slice / origin:** DB / external
- **Classes:** C13 (SQLite transaction boundaries and crash consistency)
- **Research candidates:** RC-14 (research suggested S1)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: a power cut or OS crash in the small window after a buy is recorded, on a machine with no battery guarantee. The effect is a lost row for a real position. Linked at 22-28 to RC-14, whose text names synchronous=NORMAL under WAL; the RC is otherwise carried by AUD-DB-004. S2 is below the S1 suggestion because a loss here needs a host-level crash within the OS write-back window after a buy (a process crash cannot lose WAL commits).

- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:20-22@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - journal_mode WAL and synchronous NORMAL
  - command: `sed -n 19,23p of the base snapshot (22-27 merge)` - Claude verification: lines re-read. Not reproduced. A process crash alone does not lose committed data; only power loss or OS failure does.

- **Related:** AUD-DB-004, AUD-BUY-002

##### AUD-EXIT-004: Sell approvals go to the public mempool with ethers default fees, outside the sell fee ceiling, and are exact-amount so most exits first need a public approve

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C06 (approvals), C16 (gas/fee ceilings)
- **Research candidates:** RC-15 (research suggested S2)
- **Severity rationale:** S2, equal to the research suggestion. Proven: approvals are public, uncapped and per-exit. The capital effect is indirect and bounded: a public approve signals an imminent sell (another holder can sell first), costs gas outside the ceiling, and adds a mined public tx before every first exit, including anti-rug exits, whose private sell cannot start until the approve is mined (the wait has no timeout, AUD-EXIT-009).
- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:409-424@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - ensureApproval: allowance check, then token.approve(spender, amount) and approveTx.wait(); the doc comment says "Approval does not need MEV protection -- sent directly"
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:871@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 full exit: approval for exactly the current balance before the private sell
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:874@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 full exit: same
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1509@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 partial: approval for exactly the partial amount
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1512@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V2 partial: same
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:541-546@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - public fallback: approval for exactly heldBalance
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-signer.js:98-132` - a Contract call through the Wallet populates fees from provider.getFeeData() when none are given; no ceiling is applied
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js:619-625` - getFeeData: maxFeePerGas = baseFee*2 + priority fee (node suggestion, or 1 gwei)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:940@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the sell fee ceiling (buildReconcileConfig ... "sell", MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI) applies only inside the private escalation, not to approvals or the public fallback swap
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:553-555@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Direct approvals and public fallback bypass transaction fee ceilings
- **Sibling sites checked:** All five approve sites in the slice (:421 via :871/:874/:1509/:1512, and :544). The public fallback swap (:553-555) is also sent with ethers default fees and no ceiling or anti-rug gas multiplier (the multiplier at :862 is passed only to the private leg, :909). Because each approve is exactly the amount sold, a completed sell leaves allowance 0 and the next exit approves again. The buy-side dead simulateSell approve is AUD-BUY-007.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-37
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-009, AUD-EXIT-014
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Decide on card EXIT-03: approve at buy time (bounded or max allowance to the one router used), or bundle the approve with the private sell, and apply the sell fee ceiling to approvals and the public fallback. Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-EXIT-005: Per-position setInterval(async) poll has no in-flight guard and the price quote has no timeout, so slow RPC stacks overlapping cycles on one shared state object

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C12 (timer leaks), C15 (TOCTOU)
- **Research candidates:** RC-21 (research suggested S2)
- **Severity rationale:** S2, equal to the research suggestion. Overlap is proven by the code. Its money effect is bounded because the queue and sell locks absorb duplicate triggers; what remains is unbounded pile-up of pending cycles and sockets during an RPC stall, stale-ordered state writes, and no exit decisions until the stall clears (a stalled quote also skips the urgency exit, AUD-EXIT-003).
- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1906-1942@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - startExitMonitor: setInterval(async () => { await pollExitStrategy(...) }, 5000) with no running flag; a cycle slower than 5 s overlaps the next
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:2007-2042@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - resumeExitMonitor: identical loop
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:315-345@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - queryPrice awaits the RPC with no withTimeout; only the ethers FetchRequest default bounds it
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/utils/fetch.js:402` - FetchRequest default timeout is 300000 ms, so one stalled quote can stack up to about 60 pending cycles per position
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1705@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - all overlapping cycles mutate the same state object (highWaterMark :1717-1719, volatility samples :1720, trailingActivated :1776) and each persists it (:1829)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1918-1925@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the overrun telemetry is logged only when a cycle completes, so stacked cycles are invisible while they pile up
- **Sibling sites checked:** In the slice: the two exit intervals (:1906, :2007); exitWatchdog.ts and withTimeout.ts use setTimeout only, cleared in finally. Duplicate triggers from overlapping cycles are absorbed: enqueueExit dedupes per position (tryEnqueuePosition, exitManager.ts:66-71), and partial detection-to-lock is synchronous (:1732 -> :1822 -> tryAcquireSellLock :1483 with no await between), and tiers are marked before the sell lock is released (:1568-1575 before finally :1590), so no double partial was found. Same-pattern siblings outside the slice, named by path only (owned by their slices): src/bot.ts (:1636, :1660, :1740, :1774), src/anti-rug/detector.ts (:1261), src/api/server.ts (:186).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-38
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-003, AUD-EXIT-021
- **Tags:** none
- **Recommendation:** Run each position poll as a self-rescheduling setTimeout (or skip a tick while one is in flight) and bound queryPrice with withTimeout. Card EXIT-04 (exit-path liveness). Phase 29 unless Phase 24 folds it into the exit fixes.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1022-1037@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 has no fee-on-transfer-safe fallback ("V3 has no fee-on-transfer-safe public router analog wired here")
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts:220-249@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - strategies simulate before submit (also passthrough.ts:115-125, bloxroute.ts:131-141), so a reverting private sell is not sent and the ladder falls through quickly
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:363-365@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Transfer-tax tokens cannot execute the standard V2 partial-sale path
- **Sibling sites checked:** All three sell builders: buildV2SellTx (:351-372, non-FoT), buildV3SellTx (:378-407, exactInputSingle), executePublicFallbackSell (:508-564, FoT-safe). The buy side allows taxed tokens up to the per-chain max sell tax (TH-BUY-19), so taxed positions are reachable. Simulate-before-submit in all three strategies means no gas is burned on the reverting private attempts.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-39
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-007, AUD-EXIT-001
- **Tags:** capital
- **Traces:**
  - partial-exit: Tick: priceMultiple >= an unfilled tier multiple -> getUnfilledTiers (:1732); the partial is only detected here and dispatched at the end of the tick if no full exit fired (:1817-1826), dispatchPartialSell (:1621-1655) calls executePartialSell without awaiting; a .catch guards the detached promise, executePartialSell (:1473): per-token sell lock (:1483-1486; a held lock skips this cycle), balanceOf and clamp to the held balance (:1490-1497), Approval for exactly the partial amount under the nonce lock (:1509/:1512, public, no timeout on the wait) then the alert (:1521), then withNonceLock(sendTxWithRetry(txBuilder)) with amountOutMin 0 and, on V2, the non-FoT router call (:1531), decodeReceipt (:1545-1547), insertTrade(action partial_sell, status sold) (:1550-1565), tiers added to state.completedTierIndices (:1568-1570) and persisted synchronously (:1575); the dispatcher persists again on success (:1646), Failure (any throw, including a revert of the non-FoT call on a taxed token): warn only, the position stays open, the tier is re-detected on the next tick and retried (:1585-1588) -> State written on success: a trades row (action partial_sell, status sold) and exit_state.partial_tiers_completed updated; the high-water mark is not reset. On failure nothing is written and the same tier retries every 5 s with a new alert; for a transfer-taxed V2 token it never succeeds. A crash between the landed tx and the tier persist re-sells the tier after restart (AUD-EXIT-017).
- **Recommendation:** Use the supporting-fee-on-transfer variant on the private V2 leg and partial sells, and decide what a V3 taxed position does (refuse at buy time, or route its exit through a V2 pool). Card EXIT-05 (Phase 24, fork-proven).
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-EXIT-011: Public fallback quotes first, then waits for an approve with no timeout, then swaps with the old quote as its floor, so a draining pool makes the fallback revert

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / candidate
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C04 (slippage/minOut), C05 (deadlines), C15 (TOCTOU)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: the order is a code fact; whether the approve wait is long enough for the floor to go stale during a real drain needs a Phase 23 measurement. Effect: the guaranteed exit can revert exactly when liquidity is leaving, costing a full retry cycle at routine parameters.
- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:519-523@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - expectedOut from getAmountsOut, minOut = computePublicMinOut(expectedOut, slippagePct) computed before the approve
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:540-547@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - approve under the nonce lock and wait for it to be mined (no timeout); during an anti-rug exit this can be several blocks
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:549-555@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the swap is then sent with the pre-approve minOut and a 600 s deadline
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:464-476@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - routine slippage 5%, anti-rug max(15, 10, routine)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:470@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): A zero slippage setting silently becomes five percent
- **Sibling sites checked:** Only one public sell exists (:508-564). The private legs have no floor at all (AUD-EXIT-001). After a revert the catch keeps the position monitored and re-arms the timer; the retry then runs as a routine exit (routine slippage, two private attempts first), because anti-rug fires again only on a new pool event (ANTIRUG slice).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-43
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-001, AUD-EXIT-004
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Re-quote after the approve (or approve earlier, card EXIT-03) so the floor is computed right before the swap. Card EXIT-09. Phase 24.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-EXIT-016: Exit settings are not range-checked: a typo silently disables the trailing stop, and some values tear down protection on a still-held position or sell at once

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / independent
- **Classes:** C02 (|| vs ?? with 0n/''/0), C18 (env validation)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: misconfiguration-only (the defaults are sane), so bounded. The trailing NaN case is silent (no error at load) and leaves a 2x-plus position with only the 30-minute urgency exit; the dust case strips anti-rug from a still-held position after a failed exit.
- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/config.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/config.ts:300-302@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - TRAILING_STOP_PCT / TRAILING_MIN_PCT / TRAILING_MAX_PCT = parseFloat(env || default) with no NaN guard
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:220-230@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - computeEffectiveTrailingPct: Math.max(min, Math.min(max, NaN)) is NaN, so triggerPrice at :1751 is NaN and currentPrice <= NaN is never true: the trailing stop never fires, and stop-loss is already off once trailing activated (:1781)
  - code: `src/config.ts:290-293@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - STOP_LOSS_PCT has a NaN guard only: 0 sells at the first tick at or below entry, a negative value sells at once, 100 or more never sells
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:615-622@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - EXIT_DUST_THRESHOLD_BPS has no upper bound: 10000 or more makes any balance up to the original amount read as dust, so a failed exit is torn down as a genuine close (anti-rug unsubscribed, exit_state deleted, timers cleared, :1143-1153)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:599-602@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - EXIT_ROUTINE_MAX_FAILURES accepts 0 (n >= 0): routine retries pause after the first failure
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:80-101@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - PARTIAL_SELL_TARGETS accepts a multiple below 1 (for example 0.5x), which sells that tier at the first tick
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:615-617@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Unbounded dust configuration can disable protection for full holdings
  - code: `src/config.ts:300-302@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Exit settings can export unusable stop percentages
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every env-derived exit number (thresholds/EXIT.json TH-EXIT rows). Guarded: MEV_SELL_FALLBACK_ATTEMPTS and the two slippage knobs (never NaN, never negative, slippage clamped to 99% at :492), PARTIAL_SELL_TARGETS total < 100 and positive entries (throws at load). Unguarded: the trailing trio, the stop-loss range, the dust bps upper bound, the routine-failure floor. CONFIG.slippagePercent is hard-coded 5, so `|| 5` (:470) cannot hide a 0 today.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-46
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Validate every exit setting at load with explicit ranges and fail loud (stop-loss 0-100 exclusive, trailing min <= base <= max, dust bps well below 10000, routine failures >= 1, tier multiples > 1). Card EXIT-12 (it changes what the bot accepts at boot). Phase 24 for the capital ones.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-EXIT-017: Exit bookkeeping is not crash-consistent: a partial tier can be re-sold after a crash, a sold position is resumed as failed, and a sold row is written before the still-held check

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / candidate
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / independent
- **Classes:** C13 (SQLite transaction boundaries and crash consistency), C14 (idempotent exits)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: the orderings are code facts; a loss needs a crash or kill inside a short window. The capital part is the partial tier sold twice after a restart (selling more of the position than configured). The rest is P&L and status accuracy. Corrected at 22-28: the condition is wider than a crash. A single RPC error from decodeReceipt (receiptDecoder.ts:44, unguarded) or a SQLite error after the swap lands in the catch at exitEngine.ts:1585-1588, which leaves the tier incomplete and lets the next poll repeat the sale. The grade stays S2 because the repeat is a sale at market of tokens the wallet holds, and the proceeds return to the wallet: it over-liquidates a position above its tier; it does not lose principal.
- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1531-1575@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - partial: the tx lands (:1531), then await decodeReceipt (:1545-1547), then insertTrade (:1550) and only then the tiers are marked and persisted (:1568-1575); a crash during decodeReceipt leaves the tier unmarked, so a restart sells it again
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1073-1102@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - full: insertTrade(status sold) runs before the post-sell balance check, so a still-held position also gets a sold sell row (:1107-1111)
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1935-1938@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - resume: a zero balance marks the buy row failed, so a position that sold just before a crash (sell landed, teardown not reached) is recorded as failed
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1058-1059@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a decodeReceipt throw after a landed sell goes to the catch, which tears down correctly but inserts no sell row
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:667-675@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - teardownGenuineClose writes four separate statements with no transaction
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1531-1546@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Post-submission errors can repeat an already executed partial sale
  - code: `src/utils/receiptDecoder.ts:44@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - 22-28: getTransactionReceipt is unguarded, so one RPC error after a successful swap throws into the partial-sell catch
- **Sibling sites checked:** All exit writes: insertTrade (:1073, :1550), upsertExitState (:1575, :1646, :1829, :1891, :2001), markExitFailedHeld (:700), updateTradeStatus (:668, :1163), deleteExitState (:670). None is in a transaction. The re-sold-tier window is the decodeReceipt RPC call between the landed tx and the tier persist.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-42
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-010
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Persist tier completion (keyed by tx hash) before the receipt decode, insert the sell row after the balance check with the real outcome, and wrap teardown writes in one transaction. Card EXIT-08. Phase 29, or Phase 24 for the tier re-sell.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor), codex / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-EXIT-018: Exit monitors are keyed by chain and token, so a second open trade of the same token replaces the first trade's monitor and baseline

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / candidate
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / independent
- **Classes:** C12 (timer leaks), C14 (idempotent exits)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: needs two open trades of one token (itself a BUY S1 defect). Effect is wrong exit sizing and baselines plus an orphaned exit_state row, not a strand.
- **Files:** `src/utils/exitManager.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/exitManager.ts:161-176@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - registerExitMonitor clears any existing timers under chain:token and stores only the new interval
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1945@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - startExitMonitor registers per chain:token, not per tradeId (also :2044)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:667-670@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - teardownGenuineClose marks every pending row of the token sold but deletes only its own tradeId exit_state row
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1736@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - partial amounts come from the surviving trade state originalTokenAmount only
- **Sibling sites checked:** All per-token keyed state: sell lock, position queue, timer registry (exitManager.ts), routine pause set (:644). A second open trade of one token on one chain is reachable through the double-buy race (AUD-BUY-004) or through a re-buy while a failed-held position is open. The full sell sells the whole balance, so both trades exit together; partial tiers and the stop/trailing baseline follow only the newer trade.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-28
- **Related:** AUD-BUY-004
- **Tags:** none
- **Recommendation:** Fix at the source (one open position per token, card BUY-03); if two trades can coexist, key monitors by tradeId. Phase 24 with AUD-BUY-004.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-EXIT-021: Exits await Telegram alerts that have no timeout before sending the sell, and the watchdog awaits one after an overrun, so a hung Telegram request delays sells and the worker

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / independent
- **Classes:** C12 (timer leaks)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: proven by the code; the condition is a stalled Telegram API connection. Delaying an exit is a bounded loss, and the watchdog and anti-rug budgets cap the delay (while turning it into a failed exit).
- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/utils/exitWatchdog.ts`, `src/utils/notifier.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:893@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - await sendCtxAlert before submitPrivateSell (:909)
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:533-538@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - await sendCtxAlert before the public-fallback approve and swap
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1521@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - await sendCtxAlert before the partial submit
  - code: `src/utils/exitWatchdog.ts:75-80@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the watchdog awaits sendCtxAlert after an overrun before returning false, so the freed drain loop waits on Telegram
  - code: `src/utils/notifier.ts:75-87@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - sendCtxAlert: await axios.post(TELEGRAM_API, ...) with no timeout option
  - command: `axios@1.10.0 node_modules/axios/lib/defaults/index.js:132` - axios default timeout is 0 (none)
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every awaited sendCtxAlert in the slice: before the money action (:533, :893, :1521) and after it (:744, :751, :950, :966, :1010, :1031, :1104, :1155, :1166, :1583, exitWatchdog.ts:75). Errors are caught in notifier, so only a hang matters. The worker watchdog does bound the whole submit, so a hang there is capped at the budget; the anti-rug path is capped by its withTimeout, which then counts the exit as failed.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-38
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-005
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Never await an alert before a money action (fire and forget with a short timeout), and give the notifier a request timeout. Card EXIT-04. Phase 24 for the pre-sell awaits.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-TX-007: RC-22 base fee doubled: maxFeePerGas - maxPriorityFeePerGas from ethers getFeeData() is exactly 2x the latest base fee, so the affordability and sell-reserve math over-reserves; buys are refused early (safe) and on a thin wallet the private sell is refused before submit and the exit goes to the public mempool

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** TX / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C16 (gas/fee ceilings)
- **Research candidates:** RC-22 (research suggested S2)
- **Severity rationale:** S2, equal to the research suggestion. Direction measured from code: the doubled base fee only ever over-reserves. It never lets a buy spend more than configured and never blocks an exit outright. Its capital effect is indirect: a buy that is affordable can be refused, and on a thin wallet (balance between about gasLimit x (2 x base + tip) and gasLimit x (5 x base + tip)) the private sell is refused before submit and the position is sold on the public mempool, where it can be sandwiched; private sells accept any output (AUD-EXIT-001). It also lowers the clamped private priority fee (headroom / gasLimit), which lowers private inclusion odds.
- **Files:** `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts`, `src/preflight.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js:624-625` - maxPriorityFeePerGas = priorityFee ?? 1 gwei; maxFeePerGas = block.baseFeePerGas * 2 + maxPriorityFeePerGas, with block = latest (:601)
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts:169-172@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - baseFeeWei = feeData.maxFeePerGas - feeData.maxPriorityFeePerGas, i.e. 2 x latest base fee
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts:63-66@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - same derivation (Base/Arbitrum)
  - code: `src/preflight.ts:314-330@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - deriveFeeWei uses the same derivation for the buy-time entry gate (sibling, DB/CONFIG-adjacent file)
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts:280-286@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - reserve = sellGasLimit x (baseFeeWei x 1.5) = 3 x the real base fee per gas
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts:328-333@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - headroom = balance - value - reserve - gasLimit x baseFeeWei; headroom <= 0 -> unaffordable, the strategy throws before submitting (:527-543)
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts:210-211@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the submitted maxFeePerGas = baseFeeWei + priority: here the 2x is the usual ethers headroom against a rising base fee, which helps inclusion and is not an overspend (EIP-1559 charges the real base fee)
  - code: `src/utils/txManager.ts:201-214@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - a strategy throw on the sell leg becomes landed:false with an empty broadcast handle
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:909@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - executeFullSell then skips guard 2a (no hash) and goes to the balance check and the public-mempool fallback
- **Sibling sites checked:** All four derivations: flashbots.ts:169-172, passthrough.ts:63-66, preflight.ts:314-330 (deriveFeeWei), and the doc comments at reconciliation.ts:234/:255. bloxroute.ts:92 uses gasPrice (BSC legacy), so BSC is not doubled. The public fallback itself (exitEngine.ts:552-555) uses ethers default fees and is never refused by the bot; only the node can refuse it for insufficient funds.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-55
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-001, AUD-TX-010
- **Tags:** capital
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24 (card TX-02): use the real base fee (latest block baseFeePerGas, optionally projected one block ahead) for affordability and the sell reserve, keep 2 x base + tip only as the submitted maxFeePerGas cap, and do the same in preflight deriveFeeWei. Decide whether the sell leg should reserve gas at all (AUD-TX-010).
