##### AUD-TX-008: No RPC or relay timeout on the signing path: RPC_TIMEOUT_MS is documented (default 15000) but read nowhere, the providers use ethers' 300 s idle timeout, and every RPC and relay call of an attempt is awaited inside the wallet nonce lock

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** TX / independent
- **Classes:** C07 (nonce management), C18 (env validation)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: a hung RPC or relay node does not block forever (300 s idle timeout, 5 min bundle wait) but each hung call can hold the wallet lock for minutes, stacking with the RC-11 hold (AUD-TX-003) and delaying every exit of the wallet; and the documented RPC_TIMEOUT_MS gives the operator a false sense that calls are bounded at 15 s. Not S1 on its own because every call is eventually bounded.
- **Files:** `src/utils/provider.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts`, `src/config.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - command: `git grep -nE "RPC_TIMEOUT" 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src` - only src/config.ts:180 (registration with the description "Promise.race frees a hung call ... default: 15000") and .env.example:237: the value is never read
  - code: `src/utils/provider.ts:23@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - new ethers.JsonRpcProvider(url) with no options: no request timeout, no staticNetwork
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/utils/fetch.js:402` - FetchRequest default timeout 300000 ms; node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/utils/geturl.js:43 and :58-59 apply it as a socket idle timeout
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider-jsonrpc.js:478` - without staticNetwork a JsonRpcProvider that cannot detect its network retries every 1 s
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts:84-110@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - rawSendBundle builds its own FetchRequest with the default timeout, one call per target block
  - command: `@flashbots/ethers-provider-bundle@1.0.0 node_modules/@flashbots/ethers-provider-bundle/build/index.js:40` - bundle.wait() resolves on the target block event or rejects with the bare string "Timed out" after 5 minutes (:406-415)
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts:371-399@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - each confirm-window poll awaits getTransactionReceipt and getTransactionCount with no per-call bound; the deadline is checked only between calls, so one hung call stretches the window
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts:121@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - provider.call simulate with no bound
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every network await in the slice: provider.ts (no options), flashbots.ts (FlashbotsBundleProvider.create, getNetwork, getFeeData, getBalance, signBundle, simulate, sendBundle, rawSendBundle x N, bundle.wait, getBundleStatsV2), passthrough.ts (getNetwork, getFeeData, getBalance, call, sendTransaction, wait), bloxroute.ts (getFeeData, getBalance, call, axios with timeout 10000 at :165 and 5000 at :57, the only bounded calls), reconciliation.ts (getTransactionCount, getTransactionReceipt), receiptDecoder.ts (getTransactionReceipt x2). The only use of withTimeout under src is exitTrigger.ts:265 (whole anti-rug exit, frees the caller only). Callers outside the slice use the same providers (EXIT AUD-EXIT-005 notes the quote has no timeout).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-54
- **Related:** AUD-TX-003, AUD-TX-002, AUD-TX-006, AUD-EXIT-005
- **Tags:** capital, cross-class
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24 with card TX-01: wire RPC_TIMEOUT_MS (or delete its registration): construct providers with a bounded FetchRequest timeout and staticNetwork, bound each await inside the lock, and check the confirm-window deadline per call. Bounding the calls is not a behaviour change of trading logic, but the timeout value is, so it rides on TX-01.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-20 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-TX-010: The MEV strategies always run the buy model: private sells get the buy fee ceiling (MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI is never applied), the documented "load-bearing" MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI cap is read nowhere, a sell reserves gas for a further sell, and the alerts tell the operator to change knobs that do nothing

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / OVERSPEND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** TX / independent
- **Classes:** C16 (gas/fee ceilings), C18 (env validation)
- **Severity rationale:** S2 OVERSPEND: the operator-facing cap is 5 gwei while the enforced ceiling is 25 gwei on both legs, so private priority fees can be 5 times what the documentation promises (300k gas x 25 gwei = 0.0075 ETH per attempt vs 0.0015); the affordability clamp still bounds total spend against the wallet, so the effect is bounded. The sell-side effects are indirect: an operator who lowers MEV_BUY_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI to save on buys silently lowers the private sell ceiling too, raising the sell ceiling does nothing, and the phantom second-sell reserve refuses the private sell earlier on a thin wallet (public fallback instead, see AUD-TX-007).

  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts:321-328@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - on the sell leg (value 0, buyGasLimit = sell gas limit) the bound still subtracts a reserve for "the eventual sell", i.e. a second sell that does not exist

  - command: `node axios-log-repro.js and node rpc-url-log-repro2.js 500 (Node 22.16.0, scratch folder outside the repo; axios@1.10.0 CJS build and ethers@6.16.0 resolved through the repo package exports, pino@10.3.1 built with the src/utils/logger.ts options; loopback 127.0.0.1 only, fake sentinel values, no src/ import, no .env)` - axios-log-repro: "log line contains AUTH-HEADER-SENTINEL: true" and "log line contains the signed tx payload: true" for an ECONNREFUSED relay call logged exactly as bloxroute.ts:186-189; rpc-url-log-repro2 with a loopback server answering HTTP 500: SERVER_ERROR and "log contains URL-KEY-SENTINEL: true"; for a JSON-RPC revert (CALL_EXCEPTION) and a refused connection the URL was not in the line

- **Severity rationale:** S2, capital STRAND, graded by the 23-08 executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. Proven on the real path: while one HTTP call of the chain's provider is unanswered, every later call of that provider gets its answer from the node and still cannot return, so the whole chain's exit polls, sells and anti-rug evaluation stop together, not only the stalled call's own work. The plausible condition is an RPC request whose response never comes back (a dropped connection, an overloaded endpoint): the wait ends at the FetchRequest idle timeout, 300 s (AUD-TX-008). Same grade as AUD-TX-008: the stall is bounded, but for its length every position on the chain is held without a working exit, a rug included. Not S1 on its own because the stall is bounded and a later call recovers.
- **Files:** `src/utils/provider.ts`, `src/chainRegistry.ts`, `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/provider.ts:23@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - getProvider builds new ethers.JsonRpcProvider(url) with no network argument and no staticNetwork option, so the provider re-checks its network on every call
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:1065-1067@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - createChainContext: httpProvider = getProvider(chain.name, chain.httpRpcUrl) and the wallet is connected to it, so every HTTP read and every signing read of the chain shares this one provider
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js:707-719` - #checkNetwork(promise) resolves getNetwork() together with the call; call(), getBalance, getTransactionCount and the other account reads all go through it (getNetwork at :554-576 awaits _detectNetwork every time)
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider-jsonrpc.js:401-430` - _detectNetwork: with no staticNetwork, one #pendingDetectNetwork promise is shared by every caller and its eth_chainId goes out through send(), which batches it (batchStallTime 10 ms, :64 and :257) with the call that started the check
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:335-337@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - queryPrice: the exit quote goes through ctx.httpProvider (getAmountsOut), as do the V3 quote and every executeFullSell read through ctx.wallet
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1574-1577@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - evaluateV2Signals reads the pair (getReserves, totalSupply) through ctx.httpProvider; the confirm gate's getBlockNumber at :1845 too
  - command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/triage/AUD-TX-028.test.ts (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-11)` - real ETH V2 snipe, armed; the next exit quote is held on the node; a real 95 percent liquidity pull is delivered to the detector, whose getReserves and totalSupply reads are answered by the node at once, yet the evaluation does not finish while the quote is held (no antirug.confirm-gate.scheduled), and no eth_chainId reaches the node; on release the batch's eth_chainId is answered and the evaluation finishes (claim stalled-call-stalls-antirug-evaluation). staticNetwork on the provider reads looks fixed (scratch src mutation, restored identical)
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every provider the bot builds (git grep -n -e "JsonRpcProvider(" -e "WebSocketProvider(" -- src at 23a6461 and HEAD): src/utils/provider.ts:23 is the only HTTP provider and is affected; the WebSocket providers (provider.ts:37, bot.ts:1563/:1605, detector.ts:924) take a chainId but send each request as its own message, so a stalled WS call is not batched with anything (the shared network check can still wait on a stalled eth_chainId itself, not covered by a test). Callers of the HTTP provider: the exit poll (queryPrice), executeFullSell and executePartialSell reads (balanceOf, allowance, getAmountsOut, reconcile probes), the anti-rug evaluation, confirm gate and backfill (getLogs), the buy path's safety reads, the MEV strategies' fee and balance reads, preflight and the dashboard's live prices. All of them wait while one batch is unanswered. The FetchRequest timeout that ends the wait is AUD-TX-008's (300 s idle, RPC_TIMEOUT_MS read nowhere).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-TX-008, AUD-EXIT-005, AUD-EXIT-014
- **Tags:** found-by-realpath-harness, phase-23
- **Recommendation:** Give the HTTP provider a static network (new JsonRpcProvider(url, chainId, { staticNetwork: true }), the chain ID is known from the template) so calls no longer share a network check; and bound calls with a real timeout (AUD-TX-008, RPC_TIMEOUT_MS) so one stalled request cannot hold the batch it is in. test/realpath/triage/AUD-TX-028.test.ts reads looks fixed for the static network. Phase 24 together with AUD-TX-008 (OD-54), or Phase 29. Nothing is fixed in Phase 23.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (23-08 executor) / 2026-11-11 / 23a6461

  - command: `node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/subscriber-polling.js:53-83 (ethers@6.16.0)` - block events come from a 4 s poll and are emitted once per block number, so the gate fires at the first poll at or after confirmBlock
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1845-1857@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Confirmation delay never verifies that the triggering event survived a reorg
  - code: `src/anti-rug/lpBaseline.ts:110-119@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): Baseline reads are not pinned to their recorded snapshot block

##### AUD-ANTIRUG-024: On a chain's first anti-rug start with a fresh database, the dry-run stamp creates the chain_state row with last_seen_block 0 before the backfill reads it, so the backfill never takes its seed branch and instead raises a false GAP DETECTED (error log, Telegram alert, dashboard event) for the whole chain history

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** ANTIRUG / independent
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill)
- **Severity rationale:** S3 (misleading behavior and telemetry), capital_impact none, by operator ruling at the 23-01 Task 1 checkpoint (ESC-ANTIRUG-02, "New finding, S3 (Recommended)"). The gap branch takes no capital action, and on a fresh database there is no earlier window to replay, so the outcome apart from the alert matches the seed branch: cursor at the head, nothing replayed. The harm is a false error-level alert on Telegram and the dashboard telling the operator that the whole chain history was missed and needs manual review, on every first start, which trains the operator to ignore a real GAP DETECTED (AUD-ANTIRUG-005 sub-claim 3).
- **Files:** `src/anti-rug/detector.ts`, `src/utils/db.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:585@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - startChainAntiRugListener runs setAntirugDryRunStarted on every call, before the WS/HTTP split (:587) and before the backfill (:718) in the same call
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:702-707@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - INSERT INTO chain_state (chain, last_seen_block, last_updated_ts, antirug_dry_run_started) VALUES (?, 0, ?, ?): on a fresh database this creates the row with last_seen_block 0
  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:700-701@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the comment assumes the detector overwrites last_seen_block on the first event; on the WS path it is the backfill that reads it first, and it reads the 0
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1015-1032@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the documented no-prior-state path (seed with the current block, op antirug.backfill.seed) runs only when there is no row, which the stamp above has already ruled out; backfillSinceLastSeen has one caller (:718), so this branch is unreachable in production
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1035-1085@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - gapBlocks = currentBlock - 0 exceeds maxBackfillBlocks (7200) on any real chain, so the gap branch logs at error, sends the [GAP DETECTED] Telegram alert, broadcasts antirug_event kind gap-detected, then moves the cursor to the current block; no getLogs, no evaluation, no exit
  - code: `src/bot.ts:2130-2144@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - boot step 4 arms the listener on every verified chain whether or not positions exist, so every WS chain alerts on its first boot after npm run db:init (and on the first start of any newly enabled chain); a first start through a buy registration (detector.ts:447) does the same
  - code: `src/anti-rug/detector.ts:588@05c166529fe736ecfbf21c0407acf74db82e6f14` - same code at the Phase 23 HEAD (src unchanged in Phase 23): stamp :588, backfill call :721, seed branch :1018-1035, gap branch :1051-1088; src/utils/db.ts:509-514
  - command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath <transient probe of the AC-01 scenario> (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-10; probe file deleted after the run, never committed)` - real-path harness, real migrations on :memory:: chain_state had 0 rows before the listener; op trail antirug.lp-baseline.snapshot > antirug.register > antirug.listener.subscribed > antirug.backfill.gap-detected (no antirug.backfill.seed); error log {gapBlocks: 21000002, lastSeen: 0, currentBlock: 21000002, maxBackfillBlocks: 7200}; sendCtxAlert "*[GAP DETECTED]* eth missed 21000002 blocks (0-21000002); backfill skipped per D-BACKFILL fail-closed; review anti-rug events manually"; one antirug_event broadcast kind gap-detected fromBlock 0

##### AUD-API-006: CSRF: the state-changing HTTP routes are protected by the Origin check plus a SameSite=Strict cookie, but the WebSocket upgrade checks no Origin, so any same-site page (another port on the same host name) can open /ws with the operator's cookie and read the live feed

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / independent
- **Classes:** C19 (API auth/CORS)
- **Severity rationale:** S3 EXPOSURE: read-only disclosure of the whole live trading feed to a page on the same host name (for example a local dev server or another local web app the operator opens), needing no credentials; no control path found for HTTP. Not run in a browser here (code reading).
- **Files:** `src/api/ws/handler.ts`, `src/api/server.ts`, `src/api/middleware/auth.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/api/ws/handler.ts:37-66@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - handleUpgrade checks the path and the session cookie only; Origin is never read
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:183@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - server.on('upgrade', ...) bypasses the express middleware chain, so the CORS/Origin gate (server.ts:100-144) never runs for /ws
  - code: `src/api/middleware/auth.ts:66-71@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - cookie sameSite strict: not sent from a cross-site page, but SameSite treats every port of the same host name as the same site (http://127.0.0.1:3000 and http://127.0.0.1:8080; localhost:5173 and localhost:8080)
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:118-143@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - HTTP: a cross-origin Origin is rejected with 403 before any route runs (loopback repro in AUD-API-005: Origin http://127.0.0.1:3000 -> 403)
  - code: `src/api/ws/broadcaster.ts:39-50@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - what a hijacked socket receives: positions_update every 5 s, notifications (all Telegram alert texts), anti-rug events, pause and chain status
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every state-changing route (grep router.post over the snapshot): controls.ts force-sell, emergency-sell, pause, resume; chains.ts stop, start; antiRug.ts CB reset; auth.ts login. All are POST behind the Origin gate; no GET route changes state (the GET routes are read-only, trades export included). A form or fetch POST from another origin carries an Origin header in current browsers and is refused before the route; a cross-site page also lacks the Strict cookie. The WebSocket has no inbound message handler (no ws.on('message') in src/api), so a hijacked socket can read but not command; a browser cannot send the malformed frame that crashes the server (AUD-API-009). The configured DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS list (server.ts:133) intentionally opens HTTP to listed origins.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-66
- **Related:** AUD-API-005, AUD-API-009
- **Tags:** none
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] HTTP state-changing routes reject requests with a cross-origin Origin before the route runs (no HTTP CSRF gap found) (evidence: src/api/server.ts:118-143@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, node cors-host.js (AUD-API-005 repro))
  - [candidate] The /ws upgrade accepts any Origin and a same-site page receives the Strict cookie (evidence: src/api/ws/handler.ts:37-66@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/server.ts:183@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/middleware/auth.ts:66-71@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Check Origin on the WebSocket upgrade against the same allowlist as HTTP (and the Host allowlist from AUD-API-005); reject with 403. Card API-03. Phase 29.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-22 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-API-007: Authentication and sessions: no login rate limit, the cookie is marked Secure only when NODE_ENV=production (which nothing sets), sessions cannot be revoked, WebSocket sessions are never re-checked after the 24 h expiry, and the length pre-check leaks the key length by timing

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / independent
- **Classes:** C17 (key handling), C18 (env validation), C19 (API auth/CORS)
- **Severity rationale:** S3 EXPOSURE: each item weakens who can drive the money controls only in combination with something else (a guessable key, a network observer in remote mode, a stolen browser); with the default loopback bind and a random key of 16+ characters (enforced by preflight) none of them alone gives control.
- **Files:** `src/api/middleware/auth.ts`, `src/api/routes/auth.ts`, `src/api/ws/handler.ts`, `src/api/server.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/api/middleware/auth.ts:40-59@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - loginHandler: unlimited attempts; a failure only logs warn (:56) and answers 401 naming the env var (:57)
  - code: `src/api/middleware/auth.ts:51-55@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - apiKey.length !== expected.length returns before timingSafeEqual, so a wrong-length guess answers measurably faster than a right-length one (the "key-length leak" of research J1/J2)
  - code: `src/api/middleware/auth.ts:64-71@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'
  - command: `git grep -n NODE_ENV 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- src scripts .env.example` - only src/api/middleware/auth.ts:64: nothing in the repo sets NODE_ENV, so the session cookie is never Secure and is sent over plain http to the bot port in the documented remote mode (DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0)
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:148-162@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - routes: health, login, the protected /api tree; there is no logout and no way to revoke a session other than its 24 h expiry or a bot restart (sessions is an in-memory Map, auth.ts:17)
  - code: `src/api/ws/handler.ts:54-65@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the WebSocket validates the cookie once at upgrade; the open socket keeps receiving every broadcast after the session expires (SESSION_TTL_MS is imported at :9 and never used)
- **Sibling sites checked:** All auth code paths: auth.ts loginHandler, validateSession (:83-93), authMiddleware (:101-110) and the cleanup timer (:21-30); routes/auth.ts (login mount only); ws/handler.ts (cookie parsing :18-29, validation :54). Every /api route sits behind authMiddleware (server.ts:162); /health is deliberately public (AUD-API-010). The login compare itself is constant-time for equal lengths (timingSafeEqual) and a session id is a v4 UUID (auth.ts:61), correct. A key with non-ASCII characters can make the byte lengths differ while the UTF-16 lengths match, so timingSafeEqual throws and the login answers 500 instead of 401 (express 5 catches it; cosmetic). The DNS-rebinding path that makes the missing rate limit reachable from a web page is AUD-API-005.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-66
- **Related:** AUD-API-005, AUD-API-009
- **Tags:** none
- **Sub-claims:**
  - [confirmed] no login rate limit or lockout (evidence: src/api/middleware/auth.ts:40-59@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] cookie Secure depends on NODE_ENV, which nothing sets (evidence: src/api/middleware/auth.ts:64-71@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, git grep -n NODE_ENV at the base SHA)
  - [confirmed] no logout or server-side session revocation (evidence: src/api/server.ts:148-162@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, src/api/middleware/auth.ts:17@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [confirmed] WebSocket sessions are not re-checked after expiry (evidence: src/api/ws/handler.ts:54-65@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
  - [candidate] key length observable by timing (evidence: src/api/middleware/auth.ts:51-55@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)
- **Recommendation:** Add per-IP and global login backoff; set Secure from the actual scheme (or always when DASHBOARD_HOST is not loopback) instead of NODE_ENV; add a logout that deletes the server-side session; close WebSockets whose session has expired (timer or per-broadcast check); compare fixed-length digests (HMAC of both values) so length is not observable. Card API-03 (behaviour change for remote access). Phase 29.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-22 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-API-010: /health is unauthenticated and returns trading state (open position count, total exposure, 24 h P&L, chain and Telegram status, version), and every hit costs one RPC call per chain

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / EXPOSURE / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** API / independent
- **Classes:** C19 (API auth/CORS)
- **Severity rationale:** S3 EXPOSURE: discloses position count, exposure and daily P&L to anyone who can reach the port (or a rebinding page), and lets an unauthenticated client spend the shared RPC quota (one getBlockNumber per chain per request), which could rate-limit the exit quotes under a flood; no control path.
- **Files:** `src/api/routes/health.ts`, `src/api/server.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:148-149@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - app.use('/health', healthRoutes(...)) before authMiddleware
  - code: `src/api/routes/health.ts:78-90@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - response body: status, version, uptime, chains (connected, latestBlock, wsConnected), positions { open, totalExposure, dailyPnL }, telegramConnected, telegramError
  - code: `src/api/routes/health.ts:30-48@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - each request calls ctx.httpProvider.getBlockNumber() for every chain, on the same HTTP provider the exit monitors use
- **Sibling sites checked:** All routes mounted outside authMiddleware (server.ts:148-152, :164-177): /health (this finding), /api/auth/login (needed), the static SPA and its catch-all (no data). Every other /api route requires a session. The wording of D-20 (health unauthenticated for monitoring) covers liveness, not the money fields. Reachable cross-origin by a DNS-rebinding page (AUD-API-005) and by any network peer in remote mode.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-66
- **Related:** AUD-API-005
- **Tags:** none
- **Recommendation:** Keep an unauthenticated liveness answer (status, chains connected) and move the position and P&L fields behind the session; cache the block-number probe for a few seconds. Card API-03. Phase 29.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-22 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

The per-position exit poll with the same pattern is AUD-EXIT-005 (RC-21, EXIT slice, card EXIT-04). The dashboard Chain Controls page opens an extra socket per visit (DASH slice).

##### AUD-BUY-016: The GoPlus liquidity-lock check queries the pair address as if it were a token, and the Unicrypt call has no timeout

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** none
- **Severity rationale:** S3: both fail toward not buying. A wrong GoPlus query returns no lp_holders, so the lock reads as not locked and the V2 snipe is skipped on every chain that uses GoPlus for locks; a hung Unicrypt request stalls the safety bank (and the handler) with no timeout. Missed opportunities and stuck handlers, no capital loss. Grade re-read on 2026-11-11 (23-28) and unchanged: the real-path run shows a skip before any signing, nothing is spent. Status candidate -> confirmed on 2026-11-11 by the 23-28 executor under the operator's standing instruction (2026-11-11, verbatim: "All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"). Reasoning: in this register 'confirmed' means the mechanism is established by evidence, and Phase 22 confirmed entries from code reading without a live reproduction (for example AUD-ANTIRUG-018). This entry stayed a candidate only because of one external fact, whether GoPlus returns lp_holders for a pair address. GoPlus's published response contract says it does not (lp_holders has no return when is_in_dex is 0), and the committed real-path test shows the consequence end to end on a fake held to that contract (AC-48), with the token query reading locked on the same fake. The Unicrypt half is a code fact at the audit base, unchanged at HEAD. Not measured: a live GoPlus answer for an LP pair address, because Phase 23 makes no live third-party call; if GoPlus answered against its own documentation the first half would not reproduce live, and the recommended fix (query by the token) is the documented way either way.
- **Files:** `src/utils/safetyProviders/goplus.ts`, `src/utils/safetyProviders/unicrypt.ts`, `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/safetyProviders/goplus.ts:57-60@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - goplusLiquidityLockCheck(ctx, pairAddress) calls token_security with contract_addresses = the pair address and reads lp_holders of that result
  - code: `src/utils/safetyProviders/unicrypt.ts:18-20@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - axios.get with no timeout option, wrapped in retry()
  - code: `src/utils/tokenSafety.ts:65-67@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - legacy isLiquidityLocked: same missing timeout and a hard-coded chainId=11155111 (dead)
  - code: `src/utils/safetyProviders/goplus.ts:33-36@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - contrast: GoPlus sets timeout 10000
  - code: `src/bot.ts:977@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the V2 safety bank passes pairAddress to isLiquidityLockedForChain (HEAD :979); tokenSafety.ts:324 sends it to goplusLiquidityLockCheck when the chain's liquidityLock is goplus; a false lock skips the snipe at bot.ts:1026 (HEAD :1028)
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:329@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - base sets liquidityLock goplus; arb does the same at :386; both unchanged at HEAD
  - command: `GoPlus documentation, https://docs.gopluslabs.io/reference/response-details (read through the Context7 docs index /websites/gopluslabs_io on 2026-11-11 by the 23-28 executor; no call to the GoPlus API)` - lp_holders, lp_holder_count and lp_total_supply: 'When "is_in_dex": "0", there will be no return'. is_in_dex: 'Returns "1" if the token can be traded in a decentralized exchange; "0" if not ... Only true if the token has a marketing pair with mainstream coins/tokens.' An LP pair contract asked about as a token has no such market, so lp_holders is absent and goplus.ts:60 returns false ("no lock info = not locked"). This is GoPlus's published answer contract, not a measured live answer.
  - code: `test/realpath/harness.test.ts:965-1026@344ba3cd3bbc61e8c5b55ecc8815cfb60a578be3` - real-path test 'AUD-BUY-016 today' (plan 23-28, commits ff4ddf1 and 344ba3c) for base and arb V2: real listener, real safety bank and real goplus.ts against a GoPlus fake that answers only what GoPlus documents (AC-48). GoPlus is asked about the pair only, locked is the only failed check, the alert reads Locked: No, nothing is sent and no trades row is written. The same fake answered for the token reads locked, so the query is the cause. The test fails with 'AUD-BUY-016 looks fixed' when the query is fixed.
  - command: `export PATH="/c/Users/jackc/AppData/Local/nvm/v22.16.0:$PATH"; node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/harness.test.ts (2026-11-11, 23-28 continuation executor)` - 29/29 on three runs, rail ledger worker-start only (no network). RED: making bot.ts ask about the token (the fix) fails both AUD-BUY-016 tests with 'AUD-BUY-016 looks fixed', the trail showing 'All safety checks passed, buying' then 'TX sent (passthrough)'; a fake that returns lp_holders for the pair fails them the same way. Files restored byte-for-byte.
- **Sibling sites checked:** All four providers read: goplus (timeout 10000), honeypotIs (timeout 10000, dead path), mudra (timeout 10000, falls back to GoPlus), unicrypt (no timeout). Which chain uses which lock provider is set in chainRegistry.ts (DB slice), not changed here. Re-checked 2026-11-11 (23-28): base (chainRegistry.ts:329) and arb (:386) use goplus for the lock, so every V2 launch on those chains is skipped; ETH uses unicrypt (:203); BSC uses mudra (:272), which falls back to GoPlus with the same pair address on any Mudra error (mudra.ts:30-33 at the audit base), so a BSC V2 launch also reads not locked whenever Mudra fails. The V3 bank has no lock check (bot.ts:1313-1318 at the audit base), so V3 launches are not affected, matching the base and arb V3 real-path buys in the same test file. The external GoPlus fact this entry left 'to confirm in Phase 23' is settled by GoPlus's documentation (evidence above), not by a live call. Open for the Phase 24 fix: the same documentation writes lp_holders is_locked values in quotes ("1" means true) while goplus.ts:64 compares the number 1; the live answer type was not measured (no live GoPlus call in Phase 23), so the fix must confirm it, or a token query could still read not locked.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-30
- **Tags:** safety-gate, phase-23
- **Recommendation:** Query GoPlus by the token address (its lp_holders describe the token's LP) and add a timeout to the Unicrypt call matching the other providers. Behaviour change (more snipes can pass), card BUY-05. When fixing, confirm the live type of lp_holders is_locked (goplus.ts:64 compares the number 1). The real-path tests 'AUD-BUY-016 today' in test/realpath/harness.test.ts are the before-and-after proof: they fail with 'AUD-BUY-016 looks fixed' once the query is fixed and should then be rewritten as the base and arb V2 buys on route public.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-17 executor), claude (23-28 executor, GoPlus documentation and real-path test, 2026-11-11) / 2026-11-06 / 23a6461

##### AUD-BUY-036: The HTTP DEX poller (a chain without a WebSocket URL) asks for its whole outstanding range in one eth_getLogs, so after an RPC outage longer than the provider log-range limit every poll is refused and the listener stays blind to new pairs until the bot restarts, with only an "HTTP polling error" log line

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill)
- **Severity rationale:** S3, capital none, graded by the 23-10 executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. No funds are lost, stranded or overspent: held positions keep their exit monitor and anti-rug (which have their own paths), and a blind listener only stops new buys. The harm is operational and silent: on a chain without a WebSocket URL, after an RPC outage longer than the provider range limit (about 2 minutes on ETH at 10 blocks; a limit of 500 elsewhere is about 17 minutes on Base), the bot stops seeing launches on that chain until a restart, while the dashboard shows the chain running and the only signal is a repeating error log line. Exposure is unknown: the operator does not know whether any chain runs without a WebSocket URL (ESC-ANTIRUG-03, "Not sure"). Graded below AUD-ANTIRUG-018 (S1 STRAND) because no held position loses protection.
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**

  - code: `src/bot.ts:1627-1654@05c166529fe736ecfbf21c0407acf74db82e6f14` - same code at the Phase 23 HEAD (src unchanged in Phase 23): seed :1634, query :1643, advance :1649, error log :1651; V3 :1656-1679

##### AUD-BUY-038: The boot does not wait for the exit-monitor resume before it starts the anti-rug resume: startMultiChainBot calls resumeMultiChainMonitoring without awaiting it and that function returns before its balanceOf reads are answered, so the anti-rug resume starts before any exit timer is re-armed, although the comments say exit timers are armed first; today's completion order holds only because the exit side needs one round trip and the allowlist check four (and AUD-TX-028 makes later reads wait)

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** BUY / independent
- **Classes:** C12 (timer leaks)
- **Severity rationale:** S3, capital none, graded by the 23-24 executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. The boot breaks its own documented ordering: the exit-monitor resume is only invoked first, never completed first, and the order seen today is an accident of round-trip counts and of AUD-TX-028. No capital effect is shown: when both resumes finish every position is exit-monitored and anti-rug-registered, and if the anti-rug side ran first, its escape and the late exit monitor both sell through executeFullSell, which takes the per-token sell lock and reads the wallet balance before it sells (src/exitEngine.ts:834-841 at HEAD). It is misleading behavior that a later fix (AUD-TX-028) or a restructure (Phase 27) can turn into a real boot-time race, so it must be fixed with them.
- **Files:** `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1797-1805@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - startMultiChainBot calls resumeMultiChainMonitoring(contexts) with no await (it returns void), then awaits resumeAntiRugMonitoring; the comment between them says the lifecycle ordering is intentional, exit-engine first so trailing-stop / stop-loss timers re-arm before the anti-rug detector starts re-evaluating events
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1892-1960@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - resumeMultiChainMonitoring is a synchronous function: for each resumed trade it starts tokenContract.balanceOf(wallet).then(... await resumeExitMonitor ...).catch(...) and neither returns nor collects the promise, so it returns before any exit timer is re-armed
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1985-1987@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - resumeAntiRugMonitoring's doc comment: called AFTER resumeMultiChainMonitoring so the exit-engine timers are armed first before anti-rug events start dispatching; nothing in the code enforces it
  - command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/ordering/boot.test.ts (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-12, plan 23-24)` - a real in-process startMultiChainBot on the fake ETH chain after a real V2 snipe and a restart on the same file: on the shared sequence counter the anti-rug resume's first allowlist eth_getCode reaches the node before the exit monitor's balanceOf eth_call is even sent and before exit.monitor.resumed is logged (measured C129 getCode, C131 balanceOf, L132 exit.monitor.resumed); the exit timer is still re-armed before 'Anti-rug allowlist verified at startup' (L140) because the allowlist check is four serial getCode round trips, each with the provider's eth_chainId check (AUD-TX-028). The test throws 'AUD-BUY-038 looks fixed' when the first allowlist read comes after exit.monitor.resumed; a scratch src mutation (resumeMultiChainMonitoring async, collecting and awaiting its balance promises, awaited by startMultiChainBot) reads looks fixed alone (restored identical, git hash-object equal to the HEAD blob, git status --porcelain src empty)
- **Sibling sites checked:** The other resume and arm sites at 23a6461 and HEAD: armPositionMonitoring (bot.ts:415-454 at HEAD) awaits startExitMonitor before the baseline and the register, and the V3 snipe and the deliberate buy arm in the same order (pinned on the real path in test/realpath/ordering/boot.test.ts); resumeAntiRugMonitoring (bot.ts:1991-2148 at HEAD) awaits each step; the dashboard onRestart callback re-attaches DEX listeners only (no resume). The exit-worker watchdog is installed after both resumes, the separate finding AUD-EXIT-019. With a held balanceOf the boot never returns under AUD-TX-028 (measured by the first 23-24 executor, 30 virtual seconds still pending), so today a slow exit-side read stalls the anti-rug side too; once AUD-TX-028 is fixed a slow balanceOf no longer holds the allowlist reads, and the anti-rug resume can verify, register and subscribe before any exit timer is re-armed.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-019, AUD-TX-028, AUD-ANTIRUG-025
- **Tags:** found-by-realpath-harness, phase-23
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24 (with AUD-TX-028 and AUD-EXIT-019) or Phase 27 (boot restructure): make resumeMultiChainMonitoring return a promise that settles when every balance read and resumeExitMonitor call has finished, and await it in startMultiChainBot before resumeAntiRugMonitoring (installing the exit-worker watchdog before both, AUD-EXIT-019). test/realpath/ordering/boot.test.ts throws 'AUD-BUY-038 looks fixed' and its invocation and completion pins are then updated in a behavior: commit citing this ID. Nothing is fixed in Phase 23.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (23-24 executor) / 2026-11-12 / 23a6461

##### AUD-DB-005: RC-23 LOG_LEVEL in .env is never applied: the logger is created when config.ts imports it, one line before config.ts calls dotenv.config(), and bot.ts imports config first

Fixing it is a behaviour change because debug output includes whole ethers error objects, which carry the RPC URL (and so the provider API key, AUD-TX-014) on HTTP errors, at a volume of one line per position every 5 s.
- **Files:** `src/config.ts`, `src/utils/logger.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/config.ts:2-4@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - import dotenv; import { logger } from './utils/logger'; then dotenv.config(): the logger module runs before .env is loaded
  - code: `src/utils/logger.ts:6-10@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - pino({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info' }) evaluated once at import
  - code: `src/bot.ts:1-2@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - bot.ts imports ethers, then './config' as its first project module, so config.ts is the first importer of the logger on the bot path
  - command: `node -e "pino({level:'verbose'})" with the repo pino 10.3.1 (Node 22.16.0, scratch folder)` - an unknown level throws 'default level:verbose must be included in custom levels' at construction; 'DEBUG' is accepted as debug

A LOG_LEVEL set in the shell is honoured (the logger reads process.env at import). Scripts that call dotenv.config() before importing a src module would honour .env; scripts are the SCRIPTS slice. 14 debug-level log sites exist in src (git grep -c ".debug("), including { err } logs of failed RPC calls at bot.ts:996, :1011, :1330 and exitEngine.ts:342 (every 5 s per position on a failing price query).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-10
- **Related:** AUD-TX-014, AUD-DB-009
- **Tags:** none
- **Recommendation:** Load .env before the logger is first imported (or make the logger read the level lazily), after redaction is in place for err objects. Card OD-10. Phase 29 unless the card says otherwise.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-21 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

- **Evidence:**

  - code: `src/utils/db.ts:100-102@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Interrupted schema migrations can prevent every subsequent restart

The live database is at version 7 (AUD-FORENSIC-001), so only a database created or upgraded from now on is exposed; 22-09 moves migrateSchema verbatim into dbSchema.ts for npm run db:init (D-24), which keeps this behaviour. Multi-statement state changes outside a transaction in bot.ts (buy row, exit_state, lp_baseline) are SC-06 (BUY slice).

##### AUD-DB-017: Preflight checks that pass when they should not: the block-age check accepts an Infinity tolerance and any block dated in the future, the honeypot-checker check accepts any contract code at the address, and the cross-env rules read ENABLED_CHAINS with a different default from the registry

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** DB / independent
- **Classes:** C18 (env validation)
- **Severity rationale:** S3: each gap needs an operator mistake (Infinity tolerance, wrong address) or a clock problem and is backed by another layer (the registry FATALs, the honeypot dispatch returns unknown on a non-checker contract); misleading rather than capital-affecting at the base SHA.
- **Files:** `src/preflight.ts`, `src/chainRegistry.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:675-676@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - Number('Infinity') passes the NaN / <= 0 check
  - code: `src/preflight.ts:526-528@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - blockAgeSec <= tolerance: a negative age (block timestamp ahead of local time, or a wrong local clock) always passes
  - code: `src/preflight.ts:602-603@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - passed = code !== '0x': any contract at the configured address passes, not the HoneypotChecker bytecode
  - code: `src/preflight.ts:709-712@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - ENABLED_CHAINS || '' (no chain) versus chainRegistry.ts:644 || 'eth': with ENABLED_CHAINS unset, rules 1, 2 and 4 check nothing while eth is enabled
  - code: `src/preflight.ts:553-562@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - passthrough chains (Base, Arbitrum) always pass MEV health (no private path by design)
  - code: `src/chainRegistry.ts:675-676@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): Infinity passes configuration checks and disables RPC freshness protection
- **Sibling sites checked:** All nine preflight checks read: wallet balance and entry affordability fail closed on RPC error (:220-233, :462-477); chainId compares exactly; the anti-rug 7-day gate is time-based (SC-11, ANTIRUG slice); stale-data never blocks by design. With ENABLED_CHAINS unset the registry itself still exits on a missing FLASHBOTS_AUTH_KEY (chainRegistry.ts:948-951), so rule 1 is covered there.

- **Decision card:** OD-61
- **Related:** AUD-DB-001

##### AUD-EXIT-010: wait() errors on exit paths are not classified: a repriced replacement or a status-0 receipt both land in the generic catch, which stays capital-safe through the balance check but records and alerts the wrong outcome

- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1112-1127` - on replacement wait() throws TRANSACTION_REPLACED with reason repriced, cancelled or replaced; repriced still throws (cancelled is false only for repriced)
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1135-1143` - checkReceipt throws CALL_EXCEPTION for a status-0 receipt
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:552-562@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - public fallback awaits stx.wait() and returns stx.hash; no error is inspected
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:1112-1157@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - catch: re-fetch balanceOf; <= dust is treated as a genuine close with the alert "sell reported failure but position closed"; no sell trades row is inserted on this path (insertTrade is at :1073, before)
- **Sibling sites checked:** All three wait() sites (:422, :545, :556). The balance-is-truth catch covers every error class: a repriced sell that landed reads balance ~0 and is torn down; a reverted sell reads the balance held and keeps monitoring. Private-leg receipts come from the TX slice (reconciliation), not wait().
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-42
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-017
- **Tags:** none
- **Recommendation:** On TRANSACTION_REPLACED use err.receipt (check its status) to record the landed sell; on CALL_EXCEPTION record a reverted attempt. Card EXIT-08 (exit bookkeeping). Phase 29.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-18 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-EXIT-027: A V3 exit leaves its proceeds as WETH in the wallet and nothing ever unwraps them, while the bot buys, pays gas and checks its wallet floor in native ETH only

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** EXIT / independent
- **Classes:** C04 (slippage/minOut)
- **Severity rationale:** S3 (misleading behavior and ops friction), capital none, graded by the 23-07 executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. No funds are lost (WETH is redeemable 1:1) and the recorded proceeds are right, but every V3 exit moves trading capital out of the native balance the bot spends: buys, gas for later exits and the wallet-floor checks see less than the wallet holds, so the bot can pause or refuse buys early, and the operator must unwrap by hand. Not S2: the wallet floor keeps native gas in reserve for exits, so no exit is left without gas by this alone (code read, not run).
- **Files:** `src/exitEngine.ts`, `src/utils/receiptDecoder.ts`, `src/preflight.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/exitEngine.ts:378-407@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - buildV3SellTx: exactInputSingle with tokenOut wethAddress (:391) and recipient walletAddress (:393), wrapped alone in multicall(deadline, [swapData]) (:400); no unwrapWETH9 in the batch, so SwapRouter02 pays WETH to the wallet
  - code: `src/utils/receiptDecoder.ts:88@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the decoder reads the V3 proceeds as "WETH Transfer to wallet (V3 path -- WETH sent directly without unwrap)": the WETH result is known to the code, but nothing converts it
  - code: `src/preflight.ts:199@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - checkWalletBalance reads httpProvider.getBalance (native ETH only); :387 the entry gate the same; WETH in the wallet counts for neither
  - code: `src/bot.ts:548@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - buys send native ETH as value (also :748), so WETH proceeds cannot fund the next buy or any gas
  - command: `git grep -n -i -e "unwrapWETH9" -e ".withdraw(" -e "WETH_ABI" -- src scripts (at 23a6461 and HEAD)` - WETH_ABI is used only by the receipt decoder; there is no WETH withdraw or unwrapWETH9 call anywhere in src or scripts
  - command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/triage/AUD-EXIT-027.test.ts (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-11)` - real ETH V3 snipe, stop-loss sell landed through the Flashbots bundle: the decoded multicall holds one exactInputSingle paying WETH to the wallet, no unwrapWETH9, and the wallet sends nothing in the minute after (claim v3-exit-proceeds-stay-weth); an unwrap in the batch and a WETH withdraw after the sell each read looks fixed (scratch src mutations, restored identical)
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every sell builder: buildV2SellTx (swapExactTokensForETH, the router unwraps and pays native ETH: not affected), executePublicFallbackSell (V2 swapExactTokensForETHSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens: native ETH, not affected), buildV3SellTx (affected; V3 has no public fallback, AUD-EXIT-007). The V3 snipe buy (bot.ts multicall with exactInputSingle, recipient the wallet, tokenOut the token) is not affected: it receives the token. scripts/ hold no unwrap. Affected chains: every chain with a V3 dex in its template (ETH uniswap-v3, BSC pancakeswap-v3 and uniswap-v3, Base and Arbitrum uniswap-v3), on every private route (Flashbots, bloXroute, passthrough), full and partial exits, anti-rug exits included.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-001, AUD-BUY-033, AUD-TX-015
- **Tags:** found-by-realpath-harness, phase-23
- **Recommendation:** Phase 29: make the V3 exit pay native ETH (exactInputSingle with recipient the router, then unwrapWETH9(minOut, wallet) in the same multicall; the minimum ties to AUD-EXIT-001), or unwrap WETH after each V3 exit; until then count WETH in the balance and floor checks. test/realpath/triage/AUD-EXIT-027.test.ts reads looks fixed for both shapes. Nothing is fixed in Phase 23.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (23-07 executor) / 2026-11-11 / 23a6461

##### AUD-TX-011: Section C E6: the passthrough strategy swallows every wait() error, so a repriced replacement (same swap, higher fee) that mined is reported as landed-not-ours, and the buy path then reports a landed buy as a zero-spend failure

- **Slice / origin:** TX / research-candidate
- **Classes:** C09 (receipt status)
- **Severity rationale:** S3, matching the exit-path twin AUD-EXIT-010: the condition needs an external replacement of the bot's own pending tx. When it happens on a buy, the landed buy reaches the snipe catch as a failure with no row (AUD-BUY-002 consequences); on a sell the no-double-sell guard stays capital-safe through the balance check. Section C candidate (no RC number), so origin research-candidate with an empty rc list.
- **Files:** `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts:139-150@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - catch (waitErr) logs and sets nativeConfirmed false for every error; err.code, err.reason and err.receipt are not read
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1114-1127` - on a replacement wait() throws TRANSACTION_REPLACED with reason "repriced" (same data/to/value), "cancelled" or "replaced", carrying the replacement hash and its receipt
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1136-1146` - a status-0 receipt throws CALL_EXCEPTION
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts:576-603@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the reconcile then probes only the original hash: no receipt, nonce advanced -> landed-not-ours -> throw
  - command: `ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:963` - responses from getTransaction() start with #startBlock -1, so no replacement detection; the slice only waits on sendTransaction responses (replaceable, abstract-provider.js:757)
- **Sibling sites checked:** The only wait() in the slice is passthrough.ts:140 (flashbots uses the library bundle.wait, bloXroute never waits). The status-0 case is handled correctly: the catch defers to reconcile, which reads receipt status 0 as reverted (reconciliation.ts:376-378). The exit-path sites (exitEngine.ts:422, :545, :556) are AUD-EXIT-010; the deliberate public buy (bot.ts:750) is part of AUD-BUY-025. A repricing can only come from outside the process (operator wallet "speed up", a second process AUD-TX-005, or an out-of-process script).
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** OD-54
- **Related:** AUD-EXIT-010, AUD-BUY-025, AUD-BUY-002, AUD-TX-002
- **Tags:** section-c
- **Recommendation:** Phase 24 with card TX-01: classify wait() errors: on TRANSACTION_REPLACED use err.receipt (status 1 and reason repriced = our swap landed under the replacement hash; return that hash), on CALL_EXCEPTION report reverted, otherwise reconcile. Return the replacement hash to the caller so the trade row and receipt decoding use the hash that mined.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-20 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

##### AUD-TX-027: The MEV strategies reserve sell gas at the buy's estimated gas limit, not the chain maxGasLimit their comment names, and the buy's gas limit is the node's estimate with no cap, while the entry gate prices both legs at maxGasLimit

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** TX / independent
- **Classes:** C16 (gas/fee ceilings)
- **Severity rationale:** S3, capital_impact none, graded by the 23-05 executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"). The code does not do what its comment says: the strategies' sell reserve follows the buy's gas estimate (typically about 150 000 on a V2 swap, half of ETH's 300 000 maxGasLimit), and a heavy token's buy can carry a gas limit above maxGasLimit. Today no capital effect was found: the entry gate runs first with the maxGasLimit basis, a 2x sell buffer and the per-chain cushion, and is stricter at every default; a buy whose real estimate cannot be afforded is refused by the strategy itself (AUD-TX-007 strategy test). It matters for Phase 24: the doubled base fee of AUD-TX-007 currently over-reserves and so hides the smaller gas basis; fixing AUD-TX-007 alone shrinks the strategy reserve to 1.5 x base fee x the buy estimate.
- **Files:** `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/bloxroute.ts`, `src/preflight.ts`, `src/bot.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts:158-162@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - comment: "the sell leg reserves the same chain gas budget (ctx.chain.gas.maxGasLimit equivalent - 300_000n on ETH)"; code: buyGasLimit = txRequest.gasLimit ?? 300_000n, sellGasLimit = buyGasLimit
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts:57-58@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - same: buyGasLimit = txRequest.gasLimit ?? 500_000n, sellGasLimit = buyGasLimit (Base, Arbitrum)
  - code: `src/utils/mevStrategies/bloxroute.ts:84-85@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - same: buyGasLimit = txRequest.gasLimit ?? 500_000n, sellGasLimit = buyGasLimit (BSC)

##### AUD-TX-029: A two-attempt private escalation (a routine private sell; by the same code, a deliberate buy's private leg) that ends because its attempt budget ran out inside the swap's 60 s deadline is logged as mev.escalation.ceiling-hit and reported as "priority-fee ceiling reached", although its fees (1 and 2 gwei) never got near the 25 gwei ceiling, so the operator is told to raise a ceiling that did not bind

##### AUD-TX-030: The Flashbots strategy's legacy-fee branch still sends the raw (multiplier-scaled) gasPrice and drops the helper's clamped fee, so on a node with no EIP-1559 fields every attempt bids the same price: no escalation, no priority-fee ceiling and no affordability clamp on the submitted fee (the CR-01 bypass the bloXroute and passthrough legacy branches removed)

The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. The code breaks its own CR-01 contract (the clamp is the final authority on the submitted fee) on one branch: retries resend at the same price, the priority-fee ceiling and the affordability bound never cap the bid, and the anti-rug gas multiplier scales the raw gasPrice unclamped. It is not reachable on today's chains: the strategy runs only on ETH, whose blocks always carry a base fee, so no position is exposed; a provider that omits baseFeePerGas would reach it, and the node still refuses a bid the wallet cannot pay.

##### AUD-DASH-003: The dry-run review panel that tells the operator when to switch anti-rug to live selling shows only the events this browser tab happened to receive, plus hard-coded zero charts and a filter that does nothing, so "zero false positives in 7 days" cannot be read from it

##### AUD-DASH-006: Amount presentation can misstate money: "Total P&L" adds only the realized P&L of still-open positions (unrealized and closed trades are left out), the high-water mark (a probe quote) is printed as an ETH amount, every amount is cut to 4 decimals with no unit, and the sell confirmations show no amount at all

- **Severity rationale:** S3: operationally relevant presentation (never cosmetic): the headline Total P&L can read +0.0000 while every open position is losing, the high-water mark is a different unit printed as ETH, and small amounts vanish to 0.0000; the operator reads these next to the sell buttons. Not S2: the bot's own decisions do not use these numbers, and the larger unit defects underneath are registered separately at their own severity.

  - code: `src/api/helpers/positions.ts:91@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - highWaterMark is the raw exit_state.high_water_mark (the engine's probe quote, AUD-EXIT-003), not an ETH amount
  - code: `dashboard/src/utils/formatters.ts:5-19@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - formatPnL / formatEth: toFixed(4), no unit; anything below 0.00005 prints 0.0000 and a tiny loss prints "-0.0000"
  - code: `dashboard/src/components/StatCard.tsx:8-10@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - "-0.0000" is coloured as a loss, "+0.0000" as a profit

  - code: `dashboard/src/components/TradeTable.tsx:96-104@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - formatDate(timestamp) = new Date(timestamp).toLocaleDateString(...) with no * 1000
  - code: `dashboard/src/components/PositionTable.tsx:48-51@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - contrast: the positions table treats buyTime as seconds (Date.now() / 1000 - buyTime)

##### AUD-DASH-009: Chain Controls opens its own second WebSocket on every visit and never really closes it: the cleanup closes the socket, but the close handler then arms a new 3 s reconnect that nothing cancels, so each visit leaves a socket that reconnects (and reloads positions, chains and pause state) for as long as the tab is open

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S3 / none / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** DASH / independent
- **Classes:** C12 (timer leaks), C10 (WS reconnect/backfill)
- **Severity rationale:** S3: resource leak and ops friction. Each visit adds a permanent reconnecting client: more authenticated sockets receiving every broadcast, three extra API reads per reconnect, and the server's 5 s quote loop kept running. Over a long session this adds RPC and CPU load on the bot process that also runs the exits (AUD-API-012). No direct money effect.
- **Files:** `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx`, `dashboard/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts`, `dashboard/src/hooks/WebSocketContext.tsx`, `dashboard/src/App.tsx`, `src/api/server.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:7@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - imports useWebSocket directly
  - code: `dashboard/src/pages/ChainControls.tsx:21@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - const { chainStatuses } = useWebSocket(): a second connection next to the shared provider
  - code: `dashboard/src/hooks/WebSocketContext.tsx:32-35@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the shared provider every other page reads through useWs()
  - code: `dashboard/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:300-310@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - cleanup: clear the pending timer, then wsRef.current.close()
  - code: `dashboard/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:286-293@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - onclose (which runs after close() completes, i.e. after the cleanup) sets wsRef.current = null and arms setTimeout(connect, 3000)
  - code: `dashboard/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:109-119@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - connect() then finds wsRef.current null and opens a new socket, whose own onclose re-arms again; nothing references this hook instance any more
  - code: `dashboard/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:121-125@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - each open triggers refreshFromRest (three GETs)
  - code: `src/api/server.ts:186-187@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - the 5 s live-quote broadcast runs while any authenticated socket is connected (AUD-API-012)
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every caller of useWebSocket: WebSocketContext.tsx:33 (the shared provider) and ChainControls.tsx:21 (this finding). The same cleanup defect exists in the shared provider; it matters only if the provider unmounts. App.tsx:11-40 and :48-87 mount a WebSocketProvider inside each route's own AuthGuard; whether React Router reuses that instance across route changes was not established without running the app (no browser run in Phase 22), so a leak per navigation is recorded as possible, not proven. Other timers in the dashboard: GapDetectedBanner none; AntiRugExitDetailModal 2 s copy toast (harmless); PnLChart resize listener removed on unmount.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-API-012
- **Tags:** none
- **Recommendation:** Read chain statuses from the shared useWs() context instead of a second hook; in the hook, set a "closed by cleanup" flag (or remove onclose) before close() so the cleanup cannot re-arm the reconnect. Phase 29.
- **Reported by / found / audited at:** claude (22-22 executor) / 2026-11-07 / 23a6461

(evidence: test/integration/pauseFlow.test.ts:31-136@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, test/integration/pauseFlow.test.ts:160-257@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820)

- **Escaped regression:** Delete the v7 block of migrateSchema (src/utils/db.ts:194-230) or the v6 pause_state INSERT OR IGNORE (:181): a fresh production DB then has no exit_status column (every failed-held write throws) or no pause row (setPauseState updates zero rows, so the kill switch silently does nothing), and every helper-based unit test and pauseFlow Tests 1-4 stay green because they build their own schema.
- **Recommendation:** Phase 28: build the test DB from the production migration (the dbSchema.ts module the 22-09 relocation creates), assert user_version equals CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, delete the hand schema and the pauseFlow replica, and give pauseFlow Tests 1-4 the real setPauseState / getPauseState / clearPauseState statements on a temp DB. ##### AUD-TESTI-002: The shared mock provider models only the happy path of ethers 6.16.0: every receipt is status 1, wait() resolves immediately, a replacement or a never-mined transaction cannot be expressed, and reorgs do not exist, so the reconciliation and nonce code it feeds is never shown the failure modes ethers actually produces

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** TESTI / independent
- **Classes:** C07 (nonce management), C08 (reorgs), C09 (receipt status)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: a money-path mechanism mock (receipt status, replacement and confirmation are how buys and sells decide whether money moved). It is the shared default, so every integration test that uses it inherits the blind spot, and it hides the registered S1 AUD-TX-002 (never-settling wait inside the nonce lock).
- **Files:** `test/helpers/mockProvider.ts`, `test/integration/txManager.test.ts`, `test/integration/mevStrategies.test.ts`, `test/integration/wsReconnect.test.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/reconciliation.ts`, `src/utils/mevStrategies/passthrough.ts`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:25-30@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - broadcastTransaction resolves { hash, wait } with wait resolving { status: 1, blockNumber }; waitForTransaction and getTransactionReceipt resolve the same status-1 receipt for any hash
  - code: `test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:15@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - getTransactionCount resolves 42 forever, so "nonce advanced by another tx" (the replacement signal) never happens by default
  - code: `test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:11-33@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - no getBlock, getTransaction, on, once or off: the event and block APIs ethers wait() and the Flashbots library use are absent

  - [confirmed] Status-0 receipt: the mock wait() resolves { status: 1 } by default; ethers 6.16.0 wait() never resolves a status-0 receipt, it throws CALL_EXCEPTION. A test that wants the revert path has to hand-write it, and none in the integration suite does. (evidence: test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:25-30@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1134-1147)

(evidence: test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:11-33@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1113-1127)

(evidence: test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:27@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1043-1045, ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1165-1178)
  - [confirmed] Reorg or dropped transaction: the mock has no reorg concept and its receipt is permanent; ethers 6.16.0 resolves wait() once at the confirmation count and never re-checks, and a tx dropped from the mempool without a replacement looks exactly like the never-mined case. No integration test models a receipt that disappears or a block that is orphaned. (evidence: test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:29-30@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/provider.js:1179-1192)

(evidence: test/helpers/mockProvider.ts:29@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820, ethers@6.16.0 node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js:895-934)
- **Affected cases:** txManager.test.ts: a genuine resubmit reuses the re-fetched "latest" nonce, NEVER base+attempt (no double-spend), mevStrategies.test.ts: sendTransaction sends bsc_private_tx JSON-RPC call via axios, mevStrategies.test.ts: returns a real on-chain tx hash — no synthetic-hash bug on BSC path (regression), mevStrategies.test.ts: reconciles a wait-timeout to a landed tx and returns the real hash (no resubmit), wsReconnect.test.ts: RPC disconnect behavior cases
- **Escaped regression:** Change reconciliation.ts:373-377 to treat status 0 like status 1 ("included"): a reverted buy or sell would be reported as landed with its hash, and every integration test stays green because the mock only returns status 1. Likewise the registered AUD-TX-002 hang (passthrough tx.wait(3) with no timeout, never mined) is green today.
- **Recommendation:** Phase 28: replace the happy-path mock with a scripted provider whose receipts can be status 0, null-then-replaced (nonce advanced, TRANSACTION_REPLACED with repriced and cancelled), never mined (wait pending until a test-controlled timeout) and reorged (receipt removed after resolution), with wait() implemented by delegating to the real ethers TransactionResponse against that provider, so the error shapes come from the library and not from the test. ##### AUD-TESTI-021: Fork tests report a pass when they did not run: every guard and skip path (gate false, node unreachable, artifact missing, fixture unpinned, archive RPC unset, hardhat_reset failed) is console.warn + return inside the test, and the real-mainnet honeypot and V3 rug fixtures are unpinned skeletons, two of them consumed by no test, so the "real fixture" half of the honeypot and rug strategy has never executed

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / LOSS / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** TESTI / independent
- **Classes:** C18 (env validation)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: the honeypot gate and the anti-rug detector are capital controls; a fork run that executed nothing (or only the contrived halves) reports green, and the real-mainnet honeypot and V3-rug evidence the READMEs describe does not exist.
- **Files:** `test/fork/honeypotChecker.fork.test.ts`, `test/fork/honeypotMultiAmount.fork.test.ts`, `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts`, `test/fork/captureRehearsal.fork.test.ts`, `test/fork/deliberateBuyReplay.fork.test.ts`, `test/fork/exitStatePersistence.fork.test.ts`, `test/fork/realLaunchReplay.fork.test.ts`, `test/fork/fixtures/honeypots/eth-max-wallet.json`, `test/fork/fixtures/honeypots/eth-sell-revert.json`, `test/fork/fixtures/honeypots/eth-v3-honeypot.json`, `test/fork/fixtures/honeypots/README.md`, `test/fork/fixtures/rugs/eth-v3-CANDIDATE.json`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `test/fork/honeypotChecker.fork.test.ts:253-269@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 real-fixture case returns early when the fixture is missing or forkBlockNumber is null
  - code: `test/fork/fixtures/honeypots/eth-v3-honeypot.json:4-9@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - tokenAddress null, forkBlockNumber null
  - code: `test/fork/fixtures/honeypots/eth-max-wallet.json:9@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - forkBlockNumber null (eth-sell-revert.json:9 the same)
  - command: `grep -rn "eth-max-wallet\|eth-sell-revert" test (TESTI snapshot)` - no test reads the two V2 honeypot fixtures; only their README mentions them
  - code: `test/fork/fixtures/honeypots/README.md:1-11@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - claims the fixtures are consumed by honeypotChecker.fork.test.ts and asserted against expectedVerdict and expectedRevertContains
  - code: `test/fork/fixtures/rugs/eth-v3-CANDIDATE.json:5-16@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - V3 rug skeleton: token, pool, blocks and destinations all null; referenced by no test
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:187-199@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - isHardhatFork returns false when the node is unreachable ("skip gracefully")
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:749-800@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - HORSE replay returns early on gate false, missing fixture, unset fork RPC or a failed hardhat_reset
  - code: `test/fork/captureRehearsal.fork.test.ts:316-324@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - returns early on gate false or a missing HoneypotChecker artifact (deliberateBuyReplay.fork.test.ts:242-249, exitStatePersistence.fork.test.ts:281-285 / :406-414 / :580-584 and realLaunchReplay.fork.test.ts:470-485 the same)
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every `return` inside an it() in the 23 fork files (grep console.warn( ... return): 23 early-return sites across nine files; none uses it.skip / ctx.skip(), so Vitest records them as passed. Fixture pin status checked for all eight JSON fixtures: the three realLaunches and eth-v2-horse are pinned (HORSE resolves its token at run time); the three honeypot fixtures and eth-v3-CANDIDATE are not.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-TESTI-023, AUD-TESTI-022, AUD-TESTI-020
- **Tags:** test-quality
- **Affected cases:** V3 honeypot fixture: forkBlockNumber resolved → verdict === unsafe; null → skip, HORSE V2 rug fixture: forkBlockNumber resolved → multi-signal unsafe; missing addresses → skipped per Wave-1 follow-up, every fork case with a chainGuardOk=false early return
- **Escaped regression:** Delete the honeypot artifact build step (or leave ETH_FORK_RPC_URL unset with ALCHEMY_URL pointing at an unreachable host after setup): captureRehearsal, exitStatePersistence Test 2 and realLaunchReplay return early and pass, so a fork run that proved nothing reports green.
- **Recommendation:** Phase 25: turn every guard and missing-precondition branch into ctx.skip() with the reason (or a hard failure when the precondition is mandatory, such as the compiled artifact), make the fork run fail when any test skipped unexpectedly, and pin or delete the unpinned fixtures (and correct the honeypots README).

##### AUD-TESTI-022: The anti-rug "fork" test never uses the fork for the detector: it mocks the ethers Contract layer, never deploys RugPull.sol (contrary to its header), synthesises the event logs, and mocks the exit to succeed; only the HORSE case reads one real receipt from the fork, and even there the reserves the detector sees are test-controlled

- **Severity / capital impact / status:** S2 / STRAND / confirmed
- **Slice / origin:** TESTI / independent
- **Classes:** C10 (WS reconnect/backfill), C14 (idempotent exits)
- **Severity rationale:** S2: the fork-labelled anti-rug proof mocks the very chain reads the detector depends on and the exit it triggers, so it adds no real-path evidence and hides the registered anti-rug S1s (AUD-ANTIRUG-003/-004).
- **Files:** `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts`, `test/fixtures/contracts/RugPull.sol`
- **Evidence:**
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:4-9@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - header: RugPull.sol modes "each deployed against a hardhat fork ... executeRug emits the configured V2/V3 event(s)"
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:131-179@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - vi.mock("ethers") replaces Contract with a dispatcher returning test-controlled getReserves / totalSupply / liquidity / quote / balanceOf
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:561-565@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - comment: the tests run "without requiring an actual deploy + executeRug round-trip (which the Contract mocking precludes)"
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:575-581@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - synthetic RugPull and destination addresses; the log is built by makeV2BurnLog / makeV3CollectLog
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:95-103@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - exitManager and executeFullSell (resolves true) mocked
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:803-823@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - HORSE: the only real fork read is the LP-removal receipt (destination resolved from topic[2])
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:863-875@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - HORSE: supply and reserves are then mocked to the drained values and the Burn log is re-synthesised
  - code: `test/fork/antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:727-733@23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820` - mode 4: the held-burn assertion runs only if a test hook exists
- **Sibling sites checked:** Every place RugPull.sol is used: compiled by hardhat.config.ts:18-29; its artifact is loaded at antiRugDetector.fork.test.ts:464-470 and only asserted to have bytecode (:530-541); no ContractFactory deploy of it anywhere in the slice. The integration sibling with the same mocks is AUD-TESTI-005.
- **Escalation:** none
- **Decision card:** none
- **Related:** AUD-TESTI-005, AUD-ANTIRUG-003, AUD-ANTIRUG-004, AUD-TESTI-021
- **Tags:** test-quality
- **Affected cases:** RugPull mode 0..4: detector responds correctly to mode-N event payload, HORSE V2 rug fixture: forkBlockNumber resolved → multi-signal unsafe; missing addresses → skipped per Wave-1 follow-up
- **Escaped regression:** Change the V2 evaluator to read reserves from the wrong pair address (for example the token address): every mode case and the HORSE case stay green because the Contract mock returns the scripted reserves for any address.
- **Recommendation:** Phase 25/28: deploy RugPull.sol (or replay HORSE) on the fork with the real ethers Contract, let the detector read the fork's reserves and logs through a real provider subscription, and run a real (fork) exit so refusal and retry are observable.
